messages.text: Do Not Use
Nothing seems to happen.

After weeks of travel in the treacherous Khanark Rockies, you have finally reached the Sword Lands. These lush, coastal lands are notorious for being ruled by trading city-states, Merchant Lords, War Lords, and Rogue Lords of all kinds of creed.

Add to that the fact that nearly all undesirables and criminals eventually end up fleeing to these parts, and also the fact that these lands are infested with humanoids, giants, and monsters of all sorts, and you begin to understand well why ...

these lands are known as the Sword Lands!  Tired, you remind yourselves of the reason which prompted you to undertake such a long journey to these lands: to investigate, on behalf of the King of Bywater, who or what is causing the disruption of trade...
(And remember: use the arrow keys  -not the mouse- to cross from one land level to another, even if you are in a boat!)
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Rock Forest Waystation".  Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this place reads: "The Laughing Tempest".  Do you enter?

Unfurling a map which you purchased at great cost weeks ago, you find that you are near a tradeway town called Aranys, which is ruled by a Merchant Lord named Akkar Dhun.  A  stop there would help you catch some rest from your travels.

Not feeling particularly charitable nor self-sacrificing, you turn and walk away, the sounds of battle fading with each step you take. Yet in your hearts, you do feel somewhat guilty about your decision ...
Giant bees attack, seeing you as intruders!
The bees defeated, you wonder where their hive could be ... perhaps you should set yourselves to find it some other day?
A pack of boars attack, feeling threatened by your presence!
You see from a distance a trading caravan under attack. Do you rush to help the caravan?
Hungry giant beetles attack you!
Angry wasps attack!
Spiders attack, eyeing you as their meal!
Hunting wolves, lead by their pack leader, have targeted you as their preys!
A group of strange frogs attack you, obviously hungry!
A band of thieves attack, wishing to relieve you of the burden of your valuables!
Searching the bodies of the attackers more closely, you do find more valuables!
A pack of hungry rats move in for the kill!
Snakes!!!!!
A band of ogres attack!
A roving band of orcs attack, thinking you are easy prey!
A marauding band of goblins make the jump on you!
A group of dogres have decided to relieve you of your equipment and valuables!
A group of gnats make the jump on you!
A band of marauders attack you, being the dedicated cutthroats that they are!
"We have to go now", continues the Caravan Master, "of course, you may take any and all valuables from our ill-fated attackers!". Mounting his horse, he bids you goodbye: "Safe journeys, strangers!"
Strange worm-like creatures rise up from the ground and attack, mistaking you as lunch!
You spot dangerous-looking creatures in the distance. Will you approach?

Bearded, unkept guards wave you impatiently through the gate. "Come on!", one yells, "Come on! Get through already, will ya? We don't have all day to wait on ya!" Obviously, security is lax in Aranys ...
This appears to be Aranys' general store. Well stocked, but rather pricey. Do you wish to enter?
Enter
Leave
You eagerly join the fray!

After the battle, the Caravan Master comes up to you, smiling widely. "Well fought, strangers! We owe you our thanks! These caravan attacks are increasing by the week, I'd swear! Please, accept a token of our gratitude!"
You bet!
No way!

After the battle, the Caravan Master comes up to you, all smiles. "Well fought, strangers! Those damn orcs are becoming bolder and bolder, I'd wager! If only we knew where they come from! In any case, please accept a token of our thanks!"

After the battle, the Caravan Master comes to you, smiling. "Well fought! Those damn orcs are the bane of us, I say! I heard they lair somewhere north by the mountains. If only we knew where exactly! Anyways, please accept this token of our gratitude!"
Exausted after this needless confrontation, you realize that you could inherit some extra food supplies by processing further the carcasses of these animals, as a consolation.
After this clash, you search further the fallen bodies. You find a map on a goblin who looked like the leader of this particular band.
Some of the strange creatures dwelling in these woodlands attack you, perceiving you as a threat (or as preys? Or as meals?)!

After the battle, the Caravan Master beckons you, smiling. "Well fought, strangers! It seems as if those damn marauder attacks keep increasing. In any case, you have our thanks indeed! Please accept this token of our gratitude!"

After the battle, the Caravan Master beckons you, smiling. "Well fought! Those marauders are the bane of us, I say! Rumor has it that they are spawned from Dagger Keep, which would not be surprising. Anyways, please accept this token of our gratitude!"
After the clash, you decide to search further the fallen bodies. You find more valuables!

After the battle, the Caravan Master comes to you, smiling widely. "Well fought, strangers! Those goblins are sure becoming a nuisance of late! You have our thanks, indeed! Please, accept this token of our gratitude".

The battle over, the Caravan Master beckons you. "Well fought, strangers! Damn goblin raids are increasing, but no one knows where they come from! You have our thanks! Please, accept this token of our gratitude".

The battle over, the Caravan Master beckons you, smiling. "Well fought, strangers! Damn, those elusive goblins! I heard they possibly come from a secret lair in a forest west of here, near the mountains. Anyways, please accept this token of our thanks!"
A group of maurauders attack!
Wisely, you decide to leave well enough alone; besides, the creatures do not seem to follow you in any case. Plenty more battles will soon be coming your way, you are quite sure of that!
Hungry bears have chosen you for their next meal!
A group of harpies bear down on you!
Green dragons swoop down on you for the kill!
You spot a small group of green dragons, flying low and obviously on the hunt . Luckyly, it appears that they haven't seen you. Do you attack the green dragons?
Just as the dragons swoop down to catch whathever they were hunting, you jump in and attack!

Lying very low, you watch as the dragons swoop down on whathever they were hunting. After their kills, you see them fly away with their catches. You notice that they are heading towards the nearby mountains.

One of the dragons catches a glimpse of you as you were trying to hide away. He decides that you would make a better meal than whathever he and his friends were hunting: so the dragons swoop down and attack you instead!

After the battle, the Caravan Master walks up to you, smiling widely. "Well fought, strangers! Well fought indeed! We owe you our thanks for your much needed help. Please accept this token of our gratitude!"

After the battle, the Caravan Master beckons you, smiling. "Well fought, strangers! Those green dragons have been attacking caravans increasingly. We owe you our heartfelt thanks! Please, accept this token of our appreciation".

"Have to go, now", the Caravan Master sighs while mounting his ride. "I bid you safe journeys, strangers!", he says, smiling again. Giving the sign to go ahead, he then slowly rides away, followed by the other escorts, and then the caravans themselves.

The Caravan Master then shakes his head in frustration. "I tell ya", he says as he makes a fist to emphasize his point, "if only we knew where those damn dragons come from ... I'd be the first one to go there and put an end to their terror!".
Strange, animated trees attack you!
A group of badgers attack, perceiving you as a threat.
Strange wolves attack you!
After the clash, you figure that you might as well process further the valuable pelts in order to get more gold pieces out of them.
A group of adventurers, up to no good, decide to relieve you of your gold, items and other valuables!
Some suspicious-looking people are approaching. Do you attack them before they do you?
Initially surprised that you found them out, the bullies recover quickly and set out to do in the open whay they were hoping to do quietly: do you in and take your valuables!
You manage to move quickly enough (and without running) to elude your stalkers. They'll have to find other victims this time!
After the battle, you search further your attackers. One of them has an old, crumpled map.

From the smell of cooked food, raunchy alcohol, the blabbering noises, and the loud music, this place must be Aranys' inn.  And from the size of it, this inn must be the only one in town.  Do you enter?

Pushing the door, you enter the inn.  A LOT of people of all sorts are here! Merchants, traders, mercenaries, adventurers, and most likely a cutpurse or two as well.  You look at each other, grinning: this is the place indeed!
Do you want to leave?
Pet silverback wolves are guarding this door. The Innkeeper must be quite wealthy and fortunate to have such rare pets! Do you back away from the wolves or do you confront them?
Back away.
Attack.
Thanking the stars that no one has heard the battle, you gather yourselves and proceed onward.
Bodyguards of the inn come to investigate the noise: upon seeing you, they attack!
Now you've done it! This time, it is Zaran the Innkeeper himself, along with his consort Areyna, who have come to see what's all this fracas is about!
Seething with anger at seeing intruders, Zaran and Areyna glare at each one of you.  "What's the meaning of this?", shouts Zaran.  Raising her sword, Areyna shouts in turn: "Explain yourselves!"
Do you attempt at explaining your actions?

At first surprised by your offer, Zaran then whispers to Areyna, who is still seething. After he finishes whispering, she begins to smile greedily.  You start fidgeting, wondering what the two of them have in store for you.

"Your honesty and offer do have merit and interest", says Areyna in a steely voice.  Then Zaran chuckles.  "Aye! And it does take gall and guts indeed to sneak into our quarters in plain eye- and ear-shot of everyone else!", he exclaims.

"You should do fine indeed!", he says, looking to Areyna. She then comes closer to you:"In reparation, we want you to find a magical item known as Nessar's Monocle. All we know is that the great thief Nessar set out to explore the Tlaran Caves long ago,
and never came back.  His belongings, along with his Monocle, are presumed to lie somewhere deep in these caves.  You must go there and retrieve this item for us, agreed?"

"Excellent!", exclaims Zaran. "Here is a map to the Tlaran Caves. We will wait until your safe and successful return". Areyna then raises a warning finger at you:"But until then", she adds sternly, "you will not be welcome here!". The bodyguards ...
growl in agreement to that statement.  It looks like you will have to sleep under the moonlight for a while when you are in Aranys!
You are then escorted out of the inn. "Remember", shouts Areyna before shuting the door, "You don't come back here until you find the Monocle!".
Well, looks like you have quite a mission on your hand!
Zaran frowns.  "Very well, then.  Instead, you will give us all of your money, in reparation for your intrusion".   Areyna nods firmly in agreement.  Do you comply?

"All well and good", says Areyna as she accepts all your gold, gems and jewelry, "now, you will leave our inn!".  Zaran then puts up a hand to ward off Areyna's anger: "Now, now, dear. These people may come back any time they wish, provided ...",

then he chuckles, "that they have the gold to pay.  After all, they did make reparations, and all accounts are square by me". Areyna then nods, reluctantly:"Agreed.  But tonight -", and then she points at each of you, "-you sleep under the moonlight!"

You are then escorted out of the inn. "Remember", then whispers Zaran, as he is about to close the door, "come back anytime after tonight: I may yet have a use or two of your gall and guts!".   With a wink, he closes the door behind you.
Zaran and Areyna, along with bodyguards, rush up to you.  "Well? Do you have it?", asks Zaran with great anticipation.  What do you answer?
Both Zaran and Areyna are joyfull. "Excellent! Give the Monocle and your debt for your troubles are fully repaid!", says Zaran.  Do you give the item away?

Zaran happily snatches the Monocle from your hand and rushes to the private quarters.  Arenya looks at you thoughtfully: "I didn't think you would be as honorable and honest as you have been.  I thank you for that; take this gold for your troubles ..."
Do you take the reward?

Considering the circumstances, you thank Areyna for her generous reward.  Simply nodding, she adds: "Of course, you are now welcome here again.  But a warning: no more trouble out of you!".  Turning, she walks away to join Zaran.
At your embarassed refusal, Areyna smiles. "Truly, you are the principled and noble lot! I approve, and I am glad of it!  Take the reward and more, please, for it would make me happy."

"The brass key is for the 3rd suite on your left, here at the inn, which is on the floor level", she adds, winking at you.  "Enjoy yourselves as long as you wish.  And thank you again for retreiving the Monocle".  She then walks away to join Zaran.

"Well?", insists Zaran.  At your failure to produce the item, both he and Areyna go into a fit.  "This is the last time we brook insult from you, pathetic fools!", snarls Zaran. "Time to meet your Makers, and none too soon!", shouts Areyna.
Calling their friends, allies, bodyguards and other mercenaries at their pay, Zaran and Areyna set themselves to teach you a final lesson.
More friends, allies and hirelings join the fray!
Still not believing your lucky stars to have survived such an ordeal, you make haste to get out.

The door of the inn is boarded shut.  A sign hanging on the boards reads: "Closed until acquired by new owners".  You then notice some of the passerbys glancing at you in recognition: they were probably there when you defeated Zaran and Areyna.
Not wanting anymore trouble, you walk away from the closed inn, hoping no one will make a fuss about your presence in town.

"So, you don't have it!", mumbles Zaran rather testily.  "Why bother us with such empty news?".   Areyna then chimes in: "Didn't we tell you not to come back unless to bring the item to us?".  You are then immediately ushered out by bodyguards.
Areyna is seething.  "How-dare-you!  Not give us the item when you have it, will you?". "You owe us reparations",  yells Zaran as he unsheats his sword, "and we will get it ... with your blood!"
"Do you think us fools?", shouts Zaran. Areyna goes into a fit: "That's the last insult we brook from you, pathetic idiots!"
Zaran, Areyna, and their bodyguards have at you, their weapons drawn.

Then you stop, thinking that you should investigate the private quarters. After all the hassle you just went through, why not?  As you see that many people don't seem to make a fuss anymore about the battle, you're confident that you could do it!
Zaran looks at you suspiciously. "Have you a room key? Show it to us!"
Being unable to produce a valid room key, Zaran and Areyna go into a fit.  "This is the last insult we will brook from you, pathetic fools!", shouts Areyna.

Zaran and Areyna look at each other, grinning, upon your showing of your room key.  "Well then!", exclaims Zaran, "All is understandable and forgotten.  However, perhaps you should go sleep off the alcohol in your room?".   Areyna nods in agreement.
As you leave, you can hear Areyna scolding Zaran: "I told you that we need to repair the lock on this door!".   Then an embarassed Zaran closes the door.
Do you wish to leave the tunnel?
After a short walk, you end up outside of the cavern.
You find a crumpled map upon which the words "Dagger Keep/Secret entrance to Guild" are written.
While making your way through the crowd, you get bumped by someone. Before you realize what has happened, the culprit is nowhere to be seen and your purse feels a lot lighter!
A  beautiful woman smiles at you.  "Greetings and welcome! My name is Areyna. Will you be staying for the night?"
Please!
No thanks.

"Here is your key.  You room is on the upper floor; the stairs are near the bards' stage, to the left.  Your room is the 5th on your left, down the corridor of the upper floor.  Enjoy your stay at the Wildboar Inn!"
"Well, you do not have enough gold ... another time, perhaps?".   At that you leave the counter to make way for other patrons that are waiting in line behind you.
A grinning man bows to you.  "Greetings and welcome! I am Zaran, the Innkeeper of the Wildboar Inn!  How may I be of service to you?"
Zaran smiles.  "You will not be disapointed, I guarantee that! The meal costs 2 gold pieces per patron; for all of you, that will be 12 golds".
"One of our wenches will seat you and your meal with refreshments will be coming! Enjoy!"
You are served roasted chiken with vegetables, spiced potatoes, and cold milk.  Lots of food, and extremely good!
You are served grilled, spiced beef backribs with spiced potatoes and buttered vegetables.  Cold apple juice to boot.  Lots of food and excellent at that!
You are served vegetable soup, along with braised salmon steaks and buttered grilled potatoes.  With cold milk to boot.  Lots of food, and excellent too!
You are served grilled wildboar with strawberry sauce, buttered vegetables and spiced potatoes.  Along with cold apple juice.  A very succulent meal and lots of it too!
"What do you fancy? Any drink is 1 gold a piece.  For all of you, that will be 6 golds."
"One of our wenches will seat you and your drinks will come quickly!  Enjoy yourselves and the music!"
Seated, your drinks arrive soon enough.  The stuff is excellent! You sip your drinks while watching the people dancing at the bards' engaging music.
Zaran smiles.  "Excellent choice!"
"Very well! Meals with drinks are 5 golds a piece; for all of you, that will be 30 golds."
And almost immediately, large mugs of mead from the Dwarven Halls of the Khanark Rockies are served to you, with generous refills.  Excellent stuff all around!
Almost immediately, large pints of cold lagger from the local brewery are served. Very good stuff indeed, and numerous refills as well!
Almost immediately, large jugs of red wine imported from the great city of Tanirith are brought to you.  What a feast indeed!
And right after the meal, big mugs of rhum from the harbor city of Wailsrond are served.  Now, that hits the spot and helps digest the excellent food!

Zaran chuckles. "Indeed we do, and a very classy one at that!  Ladies for men, and men for ladies!  Unfortunately, it is so popular, with so many patrons, than none are available!".  He bows in apology.  "Perhaps another time?"
At that, you back away politely to make way for the other patrons waiting in line behind you.
As you pass near a barbarian warrior (who is eating like a slobbering pig), you notice a set of brass keys lying next to his boots, just under the table.  Do you attempt at retrieving the keys?
Without notice and with quickness, you bend down on all fours and retrieve the key.  The barabrian is oblivious to it all, being too much engrossed in his feasting and drinking.
A key is dropped.
A huge, burly bodyguard glares at you. "Have you a deluxe brass key?", he snarls, obviously suspicious that you do not have one.
At your negative answer, he sniffs.  "I thought so!  This door leads to the inn's suites: only those with a heavy brass key may pass.  Now begone!".  He unceremoniously waves you away.

As you show him your heavy brass key, the bodyguard's attitude changes drastically. "My apologies, sirs, myladies", he says as he makes a respectful bow.  He then opens the door for you.   "Have a good rest, sirs, myladies."
The bodyguard bows as you pass through the door.  "Had a good rest, sirs, myladies?" he asks politely and nicely.  As you nod, he bows again, then resumes his watch.
A bodyguard snarls at you.  "Have you brass keys?"

At your failure to produce brass keys, the bodyguard sniffs petulantly.  "Ha! I tought so! Only those with brass keys may go to the brothel upstairs. Now begone!".   He then impetuously ushers you away.
As you produce brass keys, the bodyguard bows.  "My apologies, sirs, myladies. Of course, you may go upstairs.  Enjoy yourselves".  He opens the door and lets you in.
These stairs go up.  Do you wish to go upstairs?
You end up on the brothel floor.  You can hear occasional muffled sounds coming from behind closed doors.
"Back so soon?" asks the bodyguard, a bit surprised, as he opens the door to let you pass.  You wonder what exactly he is surprised about.  You then dismiss the matter and go about the inn.
These stairs lead down.  Do you wish to go downstairs?
A ladder goes down.  Do you climb it down?
A ladder goes up.  Do you climb it?

This is the kitchen.  Very big and very busy! Wenches coming in and out, cooks working over stoves, fire pits, and pots, and apprentices going about bringing food stuffs to be cooked.  Rarely have you seen a kitchen so frantic with activity!
Then the Chef spots you: "What are you doing here???  No patrons allowed in MY kitchen! Out! Out! OUT!!!!!".   Wenches escort you out with haste, but nicely and politely.
Obviously, this is a food storage room.
Here, kegs, jugs, and bottles of all kinds of liquors and alcohols are stored.
A bodyguard mumbles at you: "Have you an iron key?"
At your failure to produce a key, the bodyguard glares at you: "No one goes to the bedrooms without an iron key.  That's why I'm here!".  He then ushers you away.
As you produce the key, the bodyguard nods politely.  "Very well. You may go through; the bedrooms are upstairs.  Have a pleasant rest".  He then opens the door and lets you pass.
"Had a good rest?", the bodyguard asks politely, as he opens the door and lets you pass.
The gates are locked.  Guards peering through small arrow slits speak to you: "No one passes ta Castle Gates without authorization.  Have ye a pass?"
As you show them your Gate Pass, one of the guards mumbles under his breath, and then the gate-doors are opened.  "Ye may pass", says the other guard, as he waves you through the Castle Gate.
"Whot do ye think we are?", yells one of the guards at your failure to produce a Gate pass.  "Begone now!" the other shouts, as the gate is locked.
Do you back away?
"I thought we told ye to leave?" the guard tells you.  "Leave now or pay ta consequences!"                                                   What do you respond?
"Then begone, NOW!", warns the guard, one last time.
"Oh yeah?", grins one of the guards. Suddenly, a volley of arrows rains on you from numerous directions!
As you back away, hurt and bloodied,  you can hear numerous guards laughing from behind the gate.
"Oh yeah?", shouts the first guard.  Suddenly, the gate opens and guards jump on you!
Panting and tired from such a battle, you proceed onwards.
More guards jump into the fray!
Overwhelmed by the sheer numbers, you flee for your lives!
As you open the doors, a bodyguard sees you.  "STOP!", he yells as others join him, "Ye're not welcome here any more!".  The bodyguards then remove you forcefully and throw you out.
At your approach, guards rush out of the compound and attack!

Upon your approach, numerous guards are now blocking the castle's entrance.  From a balcony, a man dressed in expensive clothes glowers at you; he is himself surrounded by other guards.  "I am Akkar Dhun, Lord of Aranys", he announces.
"Your transgressions are not to be tolerated!", he declares in a loud voice. "Leave now or face the consequences!"      Do you leave?
You decide that this has gone too far, and leave the castle grounds.
As you approach the Castle Gate, volleys of arrows rain upon you.
"Don't ye ever learn?" shouts a guard. "Begone, ye filth!"
"You've made your choice, then!",  Lord Dhun snarls.  He then leans over the balcony and yells: "ATTACK!"
The guards rush you!
Lord Akkar Dhun and his personal retinue take matters into their own hands!
More from Lord Dhun's retinue join the fray!

Defeated, you are bound in chains and made to stand on your knees. Lord Akkar Dhun then stands before you, grinning evilly.  In a last show of resistance, you try to break free of your chains, but to no avail.

Akkar Dhun laughs.  "Well! Hard-headed to the end, eh?"  (You are not sure, but was there a twinge of respect in his voice?)  The Lord of Aranys then leans over you: "If you wish to live, you will do me a service ... do you agree to my generous offer?"
"So be it, then!"  Callously, Lord Dhun gives the sign to his men to execute you. Your last vision is that of the Lord walking slowly back to his castle ....
Guards block your passage. "Have ye a pass?"                                                                       What do you answer?
"How did ye get here, then???" shouts one guard, at your failure to produce a pass.  At the same time, the other guard sounds the alarm.
You enter through the Castle's doors.
The guard nods as you produce a pass; he then waves you in.
You are in what appears to be Akkar Dhun's secret sanctum sanctorum.

Lord Dhun chuckles.  "Good. I want you to kill Jarad Noll, a reputed merchant of Tanirith.  He has become an annoying rival to collegues of mine; removing him would be helpful to me.  Here is a map of Tanirith, with Jarad's domain highlighted."

Lord Dhun continues: "Do this, and you will be rewarded. Otherwise, you will pay the price for failure".   At that, the Lord of Aranys grins maliciously again.   With a wave of his hand, his guards unchain you and expulse you out of the town.

Just before you are thrown out of Aranys, Lord Dhun's viceroy whispers to you: "To prove you have done the deed, you must bring back Jarad's family brooch.  Otherwise, Lord Dhun will assume you have failed ... and you do NOT want that, I assure you!"
From the remparts, the viceroy shouts: "Have you the proof?"
You are brought before Akkar Dhun.  Sitting on his throne, the Lord Merchant leers at you: "Well done ... unfortunately, I cannot have any witnesses or loose ends in my plans, so...."

"You have been entertaining", grants the Lord. "But that is ended". Akkar Dhun then gives the sign to his guards to slay you on the spot.  Your last vision is that of the Lord, frowning: "After you're done, DO send for drudges to clean up their blood."
At your failure to produce the brooch, the viceroy frowns.  "So be it, then ..."    Suddenly, guards swarm out of the gates.
Now Akkar Dhun himself stands on the remparts.  "Very well, then! Let's see how you fare against my best of the best!"
The compound is now empty, except for useless tables, cots, chairs, et al.   Even the weapon and armor depots are devoid of any interest to you.
Guards are lining up the castle's entrance. Upon seeing you, they attack!
As you approach the gates, volleys of arrows rain on you!

You stand before rows of open mines.  No wonder Sparklestone is a trading power, despite its small size!  Scores of miners and helpers come in and out of the mines, with cartwheels loaded with minerals and ores of all kinds.

As you sit on the bed, you feel a strange material just underneath the covers. After investigating this, you find that the material is a small sheet of parchment bearing a waxed seal. Upon closer examination, you realize that you are holding a pass that
will allow you to cross the town's Castle Gate and go "visit" Lord Akkar Dhun's domain! This pass must have been forgotten by its rightful bearer: what luck, you have!

After the battle, the Caravan Master comes to you, smiling.  "Well fought and greetings, strangers!  We're a caravan from Tanirith, going to Bywater, beyond the Khanark Rockies. Caravan attacks are increasing, even when Knights of the Flame escort us!"

The battle ended, the Caravan Master beckons you, smiling.  "Well fought, strangers! We're a caravan from Tanirith, heading for Sparklestone. Damn attacks keep happening, even when Knights of the Flame are sent to protect us!"

The caravan Master comes to you, smiling widely.  "Well fought, strangers, and greetings! We're a caravan from Tanirith, going to Wailsrond. Caravan attacks keep increasing, even when Knights of the Flame are sent to escort us!"

He then shakes his head.  "I tell ya, a dark storm is rising in the Sword Lands ... Something, or someone, has put terrible wheels into motion ..."  He sighs, then claps you on the shoulder: "Anyways, accept this token of thanks for your help!"

He then sighs, gazing towards the east. "Dark clouds are hovering over our fair Tanirith ... And I shudder to think what they are bringing."  Shaking his head, he claps you on the shoulders: "Anyways, thanks for your help! Take this token of gratitude."
The sign of this store reads: "Exotic and esoteric imports".   Do you enter?
This is the Castle's compound. You can hear talking noises from the guards living within. Two guards block you way: "No one is allowed here!"   They wave you away, eyeing you suspiciously.
You find a secret passage!
This building looks like a Town Business Hall.  Many traders, merchants and task-hunters come in and out.  Do you want to enter?

You enter the Hall ... Lots of people talking, doing business deals, coming about, and so on.  You see a sign that reads: "Adventurers Inc.".  Heading to the room the sign points to, a dwarf sitting behind a desk waves you to him.

"I s'pose", mumbles the dwarf, "that ye want a job or sumptin?"  You nod.  The gruff dwarf irritably shuffles through piles of papers; retrieving a specific sheet, he turns to you: "Here's what I cain offer ye ... which one will ye take?"

"Ah! Escort to the mining town of Sparklestone ... That will pay 50 golds per head, so that will be 300 fer yer group! Meet the Caravan Master outside of town, near the East Gate: he'll tell ye the rest". Grumping, the dwarf goes back to his paperwork.
"Well don't come an' bother me when ye want no jobs, then!", growls the dwarf, very much annoyed.  He waves you out, then slams the door.  You get out of the Town Hall.
As you enter Adventurers Inc. again, the dwarf leers at you: "Why do ye come an' bother me fer, when ye haven't finished the job I gave ye?", glares the dwarf.  "Git out!"

The dwarf looks at you in surprise. "The Gem, eh? Well, it's rumored to be located in the Crypt of Ptaraz, the First King of Tanirith. Bring back the Gem, and yer group will be paid 5000 golds.  Here's the map of the location of Ptaraz' Crypt."

The dwarf gapes at you. "The dragon? Okay, then! Here's the map to a cave which is supposed to lead to its lair." He then waves you out.  You swear you heard him mumble "fools" before he closed the door behind you.

"Ah ... escort to Wailsrond. That one pays 75 golds per heads, so that'll be 450 fer yer group. Meet the Caravan Master and he'll tell ye more; he'll be waiting inside the East Gate".  The dwarf then returns to his paperwork.
The dwarf is genuinely surprised. "Hey! Ye've done it already! I'm impressed!"  Taking the Gem, he hands you the reward.
"Come back if ye want another job".
The dwarf looks at you in surprise: "Ye've done it already! With all that loot ye have, no doubt about it! I'm impressed!".  He hands you the reward nonetheless.
The Caravan Master rides up to you: "We've arrived! Good job, people!".  He hands you your money, then leads the caravan through the gates.

The Caravan Master rides up to you: "Here you are! We are to head east, then north-east once past the river. ALWAYS stay on the road! I'll give your pay in front of the gates once we arrive".  He then gives you the sign to proceed onwards.

The Caravan Master rides up to you: "Hear, hear! We are to proceed east on the road, then all the way south from the branch point. ALWAYS stay on the road! You'll be paid in front of the gates when we'll arrive."  He then gives you the sign to proceed.
The caravan is suddenly under attack!!!
After the battle, the Caravan Master gathers everyone and gives you the signal to continue.
Restless undead and spirits are enraged by your disturbance; they rise from their graves and attack!
Mariners and harbor workers are busy loading and unloading goods and foodstuffs from merchant vessels.

Caravans and people of all sort are coming in and out of Sparklestone.  This mining town must be quite productive indeed!  Numerous guards line up the ramparts, watchful. Some of them eye you as you cross the gates, but you are left unbothered.
This huge place looks like Sparklestone's general store. Do you enter?
This is a temple dedicated to Woralduur, God of Earth, the Mountains, and the Underearth.  Do you enter?
This is a bank; not surprising to find one in such a place!  Do you enter?
This looks like Dagger Keep's general store. It appears shody, badly kept, and poorly stocked.  Do you enter nonetheless?

Upon seeing you, the store owner smiles. "You look like reputable folks! So, I will show you to my REAL store".  He then whispers: "You see, its not good to look wealthy around here, otherwise you get robbed or worse!".
He opens a trap door behind his counter, leading to the store's basement.  "Come on down!" he tells you, with a wink.
You find a trap door on the floor. Do you wish to attempt at opening it?
You find a chest.
This door is locked.
What do you want to do?
With a loud crash, the door gives way to reveal wooden stairs going down into a dark and damp basement.
Do you go down?
A forcibly opened trap door on the floor reveals wooden stairs leading down to a dark and damp basement.  Do you go down?
The trap door opens, revealing wooden stairs which lead down.
With great effort, you manage to forcibly open the trap door, revealing wooden stairs which lead down to a dark and damp basement.
You find no traps.
The lock is just too stubborn and you fail to work it!
Success!
A trap is triggered!
The explosion not only harmed you, but destroyed the chest and its contents as well!!!
You discover that a strong aura of magic is upon the chest.
Do you want to perform another action?
The lock is successfully opened!
Do you take the loot?
Briefly, a shimmering magic aura is visible then disapears. Obviously, some magic trap or protection has been inactivated.
The chest is opened, but your rough-handling has broken some of its precious contents!
You find a trap!
The contents are yours to take!
The door crashes and is opened!
The door is unlocked!

Many of the tavern's patrons have seen what you did and are scandalized!  Their shouts of condemnation and the noise you made alert the inn's bodyguards, who now rush up to you in order to teach you a lesson in good manners!
Thanking your lucky stars, you run out of the tavern with great haste before more trouble falls upon you, hoping you won't be recognized by anyone!
Nothing happens.  However, some patrons have seen you fidget about, and one of the inn's bodyguards walks up to you, his hand on the pommel of his sword, ready to draw the weapon.

"No one's allowed in here but the owners and their special guests, ya bums!", he tells you sternly.  "Have a drink or meal, or leave, get it?"   He then ushers you away, deciding to stand guard at the door while eyeing you suspiciously.
Thinking it best not to cause unecessary trouble, you walk away.
Do you try to slip into the room?
Without being seen, you slip by the door then close it behind you.
You find yourselves in the private quarters of the inn's owners.  The room is very well  -if not richly-  furnished:  the owners must make a lot of money indeed!
The door is unlocked.  Do you slip by it?
You manage to slip through without anyone seeing you!
The place is as noisy and busy as usual.
Just as you try to slip by the door, patrons and bodyguards see you!  Surprised and now surrounded, you then hear the inn's owners, Zaran and Areyna, making their way through the crowd up to you.

Just as you've sliped by the door and about to close it behind you, some of the patrons and bodyguards see you!  Surprised and now surrounded, you see the inn's owners, Zaran and Areyna, making their way through the crowd towards you.
Patrons see you fidgeting at the door! They alert the inn's bodyguards, which rush up to you in order to teach you a lesson in respecting other people's property!
A gnome, obviously the renter of this room, glares at you upon your intrusion, and attacks!

Numerous bodyguards from the inn rush in to help the bloodied patron!  Surrounded, you are escorted forcibly out of the inn. Just before the inn's doors are closed behind you, the innkeeper shouts angrily: "Never come back here again, you knaves!"
After searching the body and everywhere in the room, you find nothing much of value.
A swordswoman glares at you upon your intrusion in her room.  "What're the lot of ye doin' in here???" she asks, ready to draw her sword.
What do you do?
"Well git out then, ya bums!" she yells, as you close the door.
Your iron key is not for this door.  Do you attempt to pick the lock?
You do not have an iron key.  Do you try to pick the lock?
"Oh yeah?" she yells.  Drawing her sword, she lunges at you for the attack!
You fail your attempt at surprise!
Just as you are about to grasp the door's knob, the door opens!
A woman peers out: "Are you room service?" she asks testily.  After you shake you head in negatory, she slams the door in your face. From behind the door, you can hear mumblings of different voices.

A man peers out: "Are you room service? Took ye long enough!", he says angrily.  As you shake your head in negatory, he shouts: "Well where in the Abyss are they?"  He then slams the door in your face.

Two kids, a boy and a girl, peer out: "Are you room service?", asks the girl.  "Mom and Pop have been waiting long", adds the boy.  As you shake your head in negatory, the girl says timidly: "Sorry! We can't talk to strangers".  They close the door.
With your iron key, you open the door to your room.
You lock the door to your room after you get out.
You dont have an iron key and the door is locked.  Maybe you should pay for a room?
Your iron key doesn't fit the lock of this door.  Perhaps you should find your own room?
Four knights, obviously renting this room for the night, raise their swords and attack the intruders that you are!

Searching the bodies further, you find a sealed letter reading like this: "My Overlords.  All is going well here; the plans to disrupt trade in the region as well as create chaos in Tanirith are in motion, and have already produced results. I ...

... expect this part of your magnificient and far-reaching Plan to bear full fruition in no more than six months to a year, as you had already surmised and demanded of me.  I am most grateful and honored for the gift you have bestowed upon me, as ...

... delivered by your two knights.  I remain yours to serve and to command, my Overlords.  SIGNED: A.D."   Who are these mysterious Overlords?  Who is this "A.D."?  And what is this "Plan" that is afoot?  You find yourselves in quite a mystery indeed!
Knowing you have stumbled on a very important document, you fold the letter back, and keep it among your valuables.

The bards are playing superb music that is truly enjoyable and fun to dance to.  The band also have a lead singer: attractive with flowing red hair and green eyes, her voice is as beautiful as she is!
This woman is enjoying herself tremendously, singing along with the music.
"Ain't this place great?" this man tells you, his mouth full of food and smelling of ale. Obviously a satisfied patron!

"Hey, ya bums!", yells this drunken man, "Watch where yer going! Ya stepped on me boots!"  Knowing this is not true, you continue forward nonetheless.  Then the man steps in your path, his friends slowly surrounding you.

"Me thinks ye owe me an apology!", says the drunken man, "But I'm a good man, so I'll let ye off by only kissing me boot ye stepped on!"  Grinning, he turns to his equally drunken friends, who are laughing out loud.
What do you do?

After a few seconds of staring, the drunken man begins to lose his resolve. "Bah!", he yells between two hiccups, "Yer not worth our trouble!"  He sits back at his table, as his friends join him, all the while grumbling.  Looks like your bluff worked!
As you try to walk away again, the man yells: "Oh no yer not! I say yer gettin' a pounding in yer faces NOW!"  He then jumps at you with his sword drawn, as his friends do the same!

After the brawl, the inn's bodyguards seperate the lot of you. "What's the meaning of this?"  Asks angrily the biggest of the bodyguards.  Many patrons then intervene in your favor, pointing to the drunken man and his friends as the instigators.

"Very well and my apologies, good sirs, ladies!", the bodyguard tells you, as his collegues throw out the drunken brawlers.  "For your troubles, please accept these tokens. Enjoy yourselves!" The bodyguard finally says, before walking back to his duties.
"OH YEAH???" shouts the man. Immediately, he and his friends jump on you, weapons drawn!

After the brawl, the inn's bodyguards separate the lot of you.  Because many patrons either point to the drunken man and his friends, or to you, as the instigators, you are all thrown out of the inn, with orders not to come back until tomorrow.
As you start to shove the man, his friends immediately jump on you!

A beaufiful woman sits in this boudoir, along with other equally exotic and attractive ladies. "Greetings", she says with an enticing smile, "how may we be of assistance for your pleasures?"  At your blushing and evident nervousness,
the woman smiles again: "Feel free to look around, if that makes you more comfortable. Just respect the other patrons' privacy." She then winks at you, making you blush even more.

A young man, quite good-looking, smiles warmly at you, sitting in a boudoir with what appears to be other attractive men. "Greetings", he says, "how may we be of service for your pleasures? We serve both ladies and men here ..."

He then chuckles at you evident discomfort. "No worries ... feel free to look around, but please respect the privacy of the other patrons, if you know what I mean".  He then winks knowingly at you, as you start to walk away.
The moment you enter the corridor, the enticing scents of sweet perfumes and exotic incenses fill the air.  The place feels warm, quiet, cozy, and very discreet.  This brothel is indeed a classy one!

A gruffy dwarf glares at you: "Have at ye, durn intruders and robbers!", he yells, just as he jumps on you with his battle axe swinging high! Only then do you notice his comrades, who are also rushing up to you!
A rich merchant glares at you: "Who are you? GET OUT!!!!!"  At the same time, his bodyguards rise to stand in your way.  Do you leave?
With profuse apologies, you get out of the room as the bodyguards keep glaring at you.
At your refusal to leave, the Merchant and his bodyguards attack!
You find extra loot in the Merchant Master's traveling chest!
Your heavy brass key doesn't fit this lock.  Do you try to pick it?
Your heavy brass key doesn't fit the lock of this door.  Maybe you should go to the room you were given?
You heavy brass key fits the lock of this door. This must be your room!
As you open the door, a woman of the brothel yells at you from the bed: "What do you want??? Can't you see I'm busy with this patron?"  The patron, a merchant, glares at you.  You leave immediately.

As you open the door, a man of the brothel yells at you from the bed: "What? Why are you here??? Can't you see I am taking care of this lady???"   The lady, probably a rich merchant's daughter, glares at you.  You leave immediately.

As you open the door, a man gets up from the bed.  Gawking at you in surprise, he becomes indignant: "No, no, no, no!!!!  I did not ask for a group of people!!!  What is this???"  Embarassed, you leave while the patron is still fuming.

As you open the door, a woman gets up from the bed.  Surprised at seeing you, she becomes indignant: "What is this???? I NEVER asked for a group of people!!!"  Thouroughly embarassed, you leave while the lady goes on fuming.
As you open the door, you hear moans and groans rising in cadence with the loud springs of the bed's matress.   Without a word, you close the door quietly and leave, blushing tremendously.
You open the door and, with a sigh of relief, you find that it is not occupied.
You close the door behind you.

A beautiful woman dressed in exotic clothes glares at you; she is obviously waiting for someone.  You notice strange tatoos over her face and arms. "Who are you?", she demands in a smooth -but commanding- voice, "What is it you want?" What do you answer?
"Well, begone then!",  she replies harshly.  Only as you get out that you notice that she was holding what seems like a powerful magical staff ...  Looks like you made the right call!

The mysterious lady starts laughing.  "I knew Dhun and Mordrek would catch up to me one of these days ... But I never thought they would send fools like you to do their dirty deed!"  Immediately, she raises a powerful magical staff and attacks!
Night Blossom has summoned Shadow Spirits to her side!!!
You search Night Blossom's belongings, and find a few things of interest!
"Oh really?", the lady replies in a cold voice with steely eyes to match.  She then raises a powerful magical staff and starts spellcasting!
The lady relaxes. "Good", she replies, "I have been waiting for you.  Will you now take me to Lord Dhun?"

Knowing that you have a Gate Pass, you motion her to follow you.  "I look forward at seeing my friends again", mutters the lady.  For some reason, that statement makes you feel uncomfortable.  But you brush off the feeling as you start to leave ...

Having passed through the Castle's Gates, you are now in Lord Dhun's abode.  Night Blossom, the lady as you have come to know her as, looks very anxious to see the Lord.  With a shrug, you walk her up to the viceroy.
Knowing that you do not have a Gate Pass to get to Lord Dhun's castle, you mumble embarassingly to the lady that you are waiting for one and that you will be picking her up shortly.

"Well go and get it, then!!!!", yells the lady, quite angry.  You leave promptly, hoping that you'll never cross her path again!  (Well ... not unless you manage to actually get a Gate Pass ... maybe then you could come back and see her?)
"Well, there you are, finally!", says the lady quite annoyed.  "What took you so long? No matter! Do you have the pass?"
At your failure to produce a Gate Pass, the lady goes into a fit:  "I shall teach you yet what it costs to cross Night Blossom!"  She then immediately raises a staff and attacks you!
Upon seeing Night Blossom, the Viceroy goes into a fit: "The Renegade!!! She's here!!! Protect Lord Dhun!!!"  Immediately, Lord Dhun's retinue rush to his defense!

Now, Lord Akkar Dhun and his trusted accomplices join the fray!  "You will finally pay for your treason, Blossom!", yells the Lord, "And you, fools, shall pay as well for bringing her here!"  Looks like you are really in trouble!

Just as you are about to grab the knob of this door, a huge bodyguard gets in your way:  "This leads to the beer and wine storage room.  Only employees may go in there!"  Without further word, he ushers you away.
"Good choice! Who will pay?"
Areyna smiles warmly at you. "Greetings! Do you wish to return your key?"
Areyna smiles again as she takes the key. "Thank you very much for staying at the Wildboar Inn!  We hope you will come back again.  Safe journeys and safer returns to all of you!"
Areyna smiles warmly as you approach her counter.  "Greetings again!  Do you wish to enjoy our hospitality once more?"
Obviously, this is the room where the spirits, wine and other alcohols are stored.  In fact, the place is a bit chill compared to the other rooms in the inn.
What do you say?
The place is indeed dark, dirty and very damp ... the humidity is such that it is difficult to breathe.  This place hasn't been visited in a long time!
The occupants of this basement are eyeing you for lunch, and they attack!
You hear a strange slurping sound coming from the far end of the basement ... its as if something moved while being submerged in slime ...
You have disturbed some of the occupants of this basement!

As you rummage through the bags of rotten foods, you find the skeletal remains of some unfortunate adventurer, but without his skull.  By the looks of his bones, which have been picked clean, he died a long time ago!
However, your rumaging has disturbed some of the creatures which used the bones as shelter!
After dispatching the nuisances, you search further the remains of this unfortunate adventurer.  You do find some valuables!
You find here that parts of the floor has given away, revealing some water running underground.  No wonder the place is so thick with humidity!
Throughout the basement, bags and sacs of rotten foodsuffs lie about.  These are some of them.  Of course, you find nothing redeemable to eat or of value ...
You find what looks like a human skull.  You wonder to whom it belonged to ...  and what caused his demise!

You overhear a group of adventurers involved in a conversation.  "I tell ye", says a swordswoman, "a bad storm is brewin' over the Sword Lands!".  "I agree", adds a sorcerer, "Raids on trading caravans are increasing, and I've heard that a ...

mysterious force is behind those raids".  "Aye!", adds an elven archer,  "And I hear that a darkness, so to speak, is falling over the great city of Tanirith ... evil and powerful forces are at work indeed!". The sorcerer shakes his head in disgust.

You stumble in the middle of a conversation: "I have heard rumors of dragons attacking caravans out of Sparklestone", says an enchantress.  "Yep!", adds a caravan master, "As if those damn raids weren't enough! Even the Knights of the Flame can't do ...

a thing about it! They are as clueless as we are!". A merchant then chimes in: "I even heard of strange things happening throughout the Sword Lands, like monsters coming out in the open and stuff like that! I swear, a great evil has descended upon us!".

"And I also heard", adds the enchantress, "that people in power could be involved!". "Like the Lord of Aranys?" asks the merchant, with a grin. The others shrug silently in response, rolling their eyes. You then quietly go about your way.
As you near this big hole in the floor, you hear again the strange slurping sounds ... an now you are certain that the foreboding sounds come from within that hole!  Do you investigate closer?
As you peek into the hole, which is quite deep, you manage to make out some twisting, sliming, huge forms moving within ... until you realize that they are climbing toward you to attack!
Looks like you have destroyed the prominent residents of this basement!

This huge hole is now empty ... very deep, it seems to connect with some running water underground.  But the climb down to it is impossible: therefore, you figure nothing more of interest is in that hole, and you walk away.

Zaran smiles warmly. "I hoped you would come back! I would need of you to perform a paid service for me ... You see, when I bought this inn years ago, it was in an abandoned state.  Areyna and I then discovered that strange creatures had taken ...

residence in the basement, which I had planned to be our wine cellar ... I have never found a group of adventurers brave enough to get down there and rid the basement of these pests ... So, for 500 golds, would you do that for me?"
What do you answer?
Zaran is all smiles.  "Oh great! Thank you! I knew you had it in you! I would have done it years ago, but I could never find help!".
Zaran then brings you down to the basement.
"I have unlocked the door", says Zaran, "Go straight up and you'll enter the cellar room. Good luck!".  Zaran then walks back up to the inn.
Zaran is visibly disapointed: "I had hoped ... but maybe I was wrong about you after all. Very well, then". You then walk away from the counter.
You just can't leave without finishing the job, can you?
A happy Zaran walks up to you: "You've done it! Thank you!!!  Of course, here's the reward I promised ...."

"Thank you again, folks! Now I'll be able to work on this basement and turn it into a real cellar!" Zaran says, before going back behind the counter.  Well, looks like you have accomplished a good deed!  Congratulations!
Guards block your way to the door.  "No unauthorized folks may come through here!"
A richly dressed wizard comes your way.  "I am Mordrek, Lord Dhun's Viceroy.  I assume that you wish to petition the Lord ... What is your petition about?"

"Oh you do?", muses the viceroy. After scrutinizing and appraising you, he then motions you toward Lord Dhun's throne.  "Very well", says the viceroy, "follow me and I shall introduce you to the Lord".
"These adventurers wish to enlist into your service, mylord", then intones the viceroy.  Without a word, Lord Dhun motions you to come to his throne.
The viceroy Mordrek grins, visibly amused.  "If you wish to do so ..."  He then motions you to walk up to Lord Dhun's throne.

The viceroy frowns: "Well, you should go to the Town Hall for that; I hear there are many jobs for adventurers available there ... However, I may have something for you nonetheless ..."  The viceroy motions you to stay where you are while he goes to ...

Lord Dhun's throne. After a few minutes of whispered discussion, the viceroy comes back to you:"Very well! We have heard that a dangerous sorceress, who goes by the name of Night Blossom, has arrived in Aranys incognito.  She is a sworn enemy of the ...

good and just Lord Dhun.  We know that she is staying at the Wildboar Inn, in one of the inn's suite.  You can easily recognize her with the tatoos she bears on her face and arms. Rid Aranys of this menace, and we will pay you handsomely!"
With a firm nod, you accept this noble task and set yourselves to catch that infamous "Night Blossom".  Kindly, the viceroy sends castle guards to escort you out of the Castle Gates.
The viceroy becomes indignant: "What do you think this is, a museum? GUARDS!"  You are then promptly seized, your Gate Pass is confiscated, and then you are forcibly thrown out of the castle.

"Really?", says the viceroy, "And what is that proof?"  You hand the letter you found at the inn.  The viceroy reads the letter, then nervously walks over to Lord Dhun's throne.  After an intense, whispered conversation with the Lord, the viceroy ...
motions you to join him quickly at Lord Dhun's throne.

Lord Akkar Dhun, sitting regally on his throne, grins slyly.  "So", he muses in a deep voice, "you wish to enlist yourselves into my personal service, eh?"  He grins again.  "Very well ...  there IS a matter of great importance that ...
needs to be dealt with ... But first, do you swear absolute loyalty and fealty to ME?", he asks in a dramatic  -but deadly serious-  tone of voice.  What do you answer?
Lord Dhun continues: "Do this, and my appreciation for your services will be most generous.  Fail me, and you shall regret it bitterly."  Do you accept this task?

Lord Akkar Dhun, sitting regally on his throne, grins slyly. "So", he muses in a deep voice, "you wish to pay hommage to me? Words mean little in my mind, so I will accept instead a more concrete fealty ... if you know what I mean ..." He then chuckles.

You look at each other, a bit confused and unsure about what he does mean.  "The Lord", chimes in the viceroy, "wishes for you to donate moneys, which would insure of you being under his protection in exchange ..."
What do you do?
Lord Dhun smiles: "My thanks, noble adventurers.  Know that you are under my protection and may wander freely within Aranys".  You are then nicely escorted out of the castle.
Lord Dhun fumes: "Well don't come in my abode and waste my time, then!"  You are immediately seized, your Gate Pass is confiscated, and then you are forcibly thrown out of the Castle.
Lord Dhun chuckles: "Good.  I want you to kill Jarad Noll, a reputed merchant of Tanirith.  He has become an annoying rival to collegues of mine; removing him would be helpful to me as well."
"You've made your choice, then!", snarls Lord Dhun, as his guards rush to protect their Lord!

As you approach the throne, you see Lord Akkar Dhun grinning at you.  "Well, well, well!", he muses, "it appears that you have stumbled upon a very sensitive piece of information ... fools that you are!"

Mordrek the viceroy now laughs in turn:"Yes, fools indeed!  What do you think the initials A.D. stand for?" he says, while pointing to the Lord, who is chuckling at your stupidity.  You now realize that you are in deep trouble, but too little too late!
"Excellent!", chimes in the viceroy, as Lord Dhun nods with satisfaction, "Here is a map of Tanirith, with Jarad Noll's estate highlighted".

Lord Dhun continues: "As proof of the deed, you must bring back Noll's family heirloom; if you do not, I will assume that you have failed ... and deal with you accordingly.  Now go, and do not come back until you have done the deed!"
You are then escorted out of the Castle Gates.

The viceroy grins at you: "Well done! Well done, indeed! You have rid us of an annoying, but dangerous, rival ... Unfortunately for you, we cannot allow any witnesses or loose ends in our plans, so ..."
Suddenly, guards rush you!
"You have made your choice, despite your pledge of service to me", intones Lord Dhun, "and now you know too much. So be it, then!"

At your approach, the viceroy stands arms crossed over his chest, shaking his head in disapointment: "It appears that you are unreliable, for we know you have not killed Night Blossom, contrary to your pledge.  Lord Dhun doesn't tolerate failure, so ..."

The mysterious lady chuckles coldly: "Very well. I'll give you 5000 golds right now, and you take me instead to Lord Dhun ... I DO have a few words to say to him, you know." She chuckles again.  Do you take her offer?
The lady fumes at your refusal:  "Greed is good, but too much greed KILLS!"  She suddenly attacks!
The lady nods solemnly: "Here is your money, then."
The lady relaxes. "Good. Take me to the castle, now."

Panting and tired from such an ordeal, you can't believe that you have survived.  You then spot Night Blossom, who is now dead, fallen alongside Lord Dhun and Mordrek the viceroy.  Since none of them were up to any good, you think that ...
this is a fitting end for the three of them.  But what about those so-called plans that Dhun and Mordrek kept eluding to?  You then decide to explore the castle further.

"Well done!", says Night Blossom, obviously as tired as you are after such a battle.  "But now your usefulness is ended, and I seek the riches of this place for myself; why, I would even replace this fool Akkar and rule this town!"
Night Blossom then chuckles. "So, I bid you goodbye ... I will make this as painless as possible for you!"  She then starts chanting incantations, obviously aiming at you!

Defeated, the lot of you are bound in chains alongside Night Blossom.  Akkar Dhun then comes up to you, grinning evilly: "Well, it looks like I win the day after all!"  Mordrek then chimes in: "Indeed, mylord!"

Smiling with cruelty, Mordrek draws a dagger: "Finally, I get to do what I promised you, Night Blossom, when you attempted to steal my arcane secrets and thus betrayed our cause."  Without further word, he slits the sorceress' throat.

Before dying, Night Blossom manages to whisper curses at both Mordrek and Dhun.  The Lord then looks at you, his eyes laughing: "Thank you for bringing her to us, even if that was not the original idea ..."  Both he and Mordrek chuckle anew.
You seem to be in some sort of small, castle dungeon.  It is very damp, cold, and dirty.  The Lord's prisoners or indesirables must be jailed in here.

Prison guards are here, bored to death and having nothing better to do than playing with huge, tamed wolves that act as guard dogs.  Upon seeing you, one of the guards shouts: "Hey! Who're ye? What're ye doin' here?"  Immediately, they attack!
You enter what can only be a torture room.  However, you don't have much time looking around, since some gnats, dressed in tortionner's attire, and many dogre guards rush up to you and attack!
Looking at the fallen gnats and dogres, it appears that Lord Dhun certainly enrolled dubious  -if not suspicious-  lackeys ...

On the bloodied torture table, you find a young woman lying near death, having been horribly tortured.  Upon your approach, she somewhat awakes.  "No ... please ... not again ...", she whispers weakly, "I don't love Lord Dhun ... "

She then starts breathing with a rasping sound: "... I will ... not ... marry him ...". And at these words, she finally passes away.  You feel enraged at Lord Dhun's cruelty and maliciousness: an evil man he must be indeed!
This door leads to the cells. It is locked.
The jailer's key unlocks the door!
This cell is empty and its door is unlocked.
This secret tunnel leads back to the mountains and out of the castle.  Do you want to leave?
You find a well carved secret tunnel which, by all accounts, appears to lead underneath Lord Dhun's castle.  Do you go into this tunnel?
This cell door is locked.  From within the cell, you can hear someone shuffling.

You find a wretch of a man, bound in chains.  "Help me!", he pleads, "I'm a merchant who refused to sell out to Lord Dhun, so he had his mercenary soldiers kidnap me in the night, and then had me chained here until I decided otherwise ...."
Do you free that person?
"Oh thank you!!!", says the man, "Come to my house anytime, and I will reward you! I live right next to the exotic importations shop!"  He then scampers away.
"I beg of you!", begs the man, "Think of my wife and children!!!"  Nonetheless, you callously shut and lock his cell door.  As you walk away, you can hear him cry in despair.

You find a dwarf, bound in chains. As proud and as gruff as his kin, he stares at you silently with determination and courage.  "I'm a merchant of ta Dwarven Halls of the Khanark Rockies", he intones.  "Free me, and ye'll be well rewarded ..."

"Ye have me gratitude!", says the dwarf.  "Come to ta Dwarven Halls as soon as ye cain, an' come to me house which is in ta Living Halls next to ta Sacred Halls: I'll give ye a reward ta please ye ta no end!"
"That durn Akkar Dhun chained me here until I'd give him me secrets about how ta enter our Dwarven Halls ... Hah! I'd rather die a thousand deaths than betray me kin and mine!"

Without further due, the dwarf starts to scamper away, then stops suddenly. Reaching within his left boot, he takes out a small gem which he tosses to you:"I almost fergot! Ye'll need this ta enter the Dwarven Halls ..."  Winking at you, he then leaves.

Gazing with amazement at the perfectly cut ruby, you then start laughing.  It looks like the secret Lord Dhun wanted out of the dwarf was right under his nose all along ... or rather, within the dwarf's boot!

"Then I'll see ye in ta Abyss!", mutters the dwarf, under clenched teeth.  As you close and lock his cell door, he keeps glaring at you with hatred.  You wonder if dwarven curses are as terrible as the stories say ....

You find a swordswoman prisoner here.  She is not chained, but nonetheless badly bruised.  "Greetings, fellow adventurers", she says calmly with a grin,  "I thank you for freeing me.  I was looking around within the castle when I was ...
caught and thrown in here to rot."  She then chuckles.  "I don't have anything to do right now, so how I about I join your group for a while?"
Do you take this swordswoman into your group?
The swordswoman shrugs: "As you wish. Thank you nonetheless for freeing me!"  She then leaves, but not before recuperating some of her gear stashed in the torture room.

The swordswoman smiles warmly: "My chosen name is Naryl Dragonstone; I have been investigating on my own about the strange happenings in the region of late ... my clues have lead me here, but I am convinced that more powerful figures are ultimately ...

responsible.  I aim to find them and rid the Sword Lands of them!"  Then, Naryl goes back to the torture room to retrieve her gear. As you follow her, you congratulate yourselves at having chosen to take such an ally into your group.
This cell is unoccupied, except for the body of a dead man. From the looks of it, he had been tortured to near death, and then died alone and cold, a scant day or two ago.
Night Blossom has been added to your party.  Check out the Allies menu.
Naryl Dragonstone has been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.
You have entered the viceroy's private quarters.
You have entered what appears to be Mordrek's antechamber. It is well suited to receive guests and have private conversations.
You have entered a big dinning room.
This door lead outside to the castle's backgrounds. Do you want to leave the castle?
This is the castle's kitchen.  Many drudges are busy at cooking food.
This is a drudge's room.
This looks like a common lavatory for the drudges.
On the viceroy's desk, you find a few items of usefulness.
You spot some scrolls tucked between book covers.
You come upon Lord Dhun's private salon and study. However, Dhun's personal guards see you and attack!
You find a few interesting vials.
You find some items of interest.
You come up to Mordrek's study and laboratory.  However, his understudies and pupils immediately attack upon seeing you!
This is the dormitory of Mordrek's pupils and understudies.
This looks like the room of Modrek's assistant.
You enter Mordrek's private room.
In this rack of clothes, you find a few interesting pieces!
The explosion not only harmed you, but destroyed both chests and their contents!
Looks like Mordrek managed to secretly stash some goodies over the years!
While searching intensely, you notice a concealed trap door on the ceiling. Opening it, a wooden ladder rolls down!
It appears that Lord Dhun has amassed a little fortune during his tenure as Lord of Aranys!
While searching through the drawers, you stumble upon a one-inch square bronze plate, upon which the word "MENTYS" is engraved and etched in silver.
Nothing special happens.
Nice, but no avail.
You wasted you time and efforts again.
Nothing happens. maybe you should just forget about it?

Upon uttering the password, the strange mists within the globe begin to move and swirl, until the face of a beautiful woman appears.  As you see her, so she can see you: indeed, she looks startled at your sight.  "Who are you?", she demands while ...

glaring at you.  "No matter", she then immediately adds, "We can only assume that our agent is dead, especially if you are here and using the globe of communication".  Suddenly, you feel a strange pressure on your temples, as if something is pressing ...

against them. "So", muses the mysterious lady, "you are only a band of foolish adventurers, stumbling their way about what they think is a conspiracy or whatever ...." She then chuckles: "If you only knew, pathetic creatures that you are! Still, we ...

do give you credit for removing our agent, a favorite of ours. This demonstrates how ineffectual he was to begin with ... But no matter: this insignificant set back does not alter our plans."  Grinning evilly, she then mockingly bows her head ...
to you: "Well done, pathetic ones. Since no good deed goes unpunished, as they say, you shall now be honored to have but a very small taste of our powers ..."

Still reeling from this unexpected mental assault, you hear the woman chuckling again. "Of course, we can not leave in so unevolved hands such a wonder as a communication globe ... So, farewell, little ones: you better hope that you never cross ...

our paths again ..." At that, the globe begins to pulsate brightly with a deafening, vibrating sound, until it vanishes in thin air! Only the fading laughter of the woman proves that you did not dream what has just happened!
Only after you have regained your composure that you realize that you have met the face of the true enemy!

After you have regained your composure, Naryl Dragonstone walks up to you: "I heard it all while I was busying myself at snooping around ... I don't know about you, but I'm convinced that we have seen the face of one of those responsible for what ...
is happening in the Sword Lands ... We must find them, my friends, and confront this enemy once and for all!"
Your tampering with the strange globe has caused a feedback of tremendous energy which lashes out to you!
Your magical tampering of the globe has caused a feedback which lashes out at you!
A huge lever is here. Do you pull down on it?
You notice that the big mirror near the corner of the room has turned into a huge globe filled with a strange, greenish mist!
A huge lever is down. Do you want to pull it back up?
The globe turns back into an ordinary mirror!

Rumaging through Akkar Dhun's papers, you stumble upon a number of interesting tidbits, such as: 1) activity reports from a Doran Ghall, who has been put in charge of raiding caravans between Aranys and Wailsrond; 2) war reports ...

from a Drahl Ghuul, put in charge of raiding caravans between Aranys and Sparklestone; 3) a note on successful negociations with green dragons regarding the disruption of trade between Sparklestone and Tanirith; 4) notes on successful negociations ...

with a tribe of goblins regarding the disruption of trade along the Aranys-Wailsrond road; 5) memos concerning the raids on dwarven caravans and the Dwarven Halls themselves; 6) many mentions of the "Overlords" as the real power behind those ...
numerous activities. Well! It looks like Akkar Dhun was some sort of Coordinator for those Overlords indeed!
On this weapon's rack, you find a few useful items.
This is Akkar Dhun's private bedroom. Surprisingly, the door is not locked ... Dhun's lackeys must be very loyal to him indeed if he trusts them so!
Rummaging through the drawers, you stumble upon something interesting!
At your approach, the merchant you rescued waves at you with a wide smile. "There you are! Welcome! Please, come in!!!"

After a few drinks and casual conversation, the merchant's wife announces that dinner is ready.  With the insistance of both the merchant and his wife, you graciously accept to stay over. The food is delicious and you eat your fill. After sending the ...

children to play outside, the merchant comes back with what looks like a shield wrapped in cloth and a small leather sac. "I told you I would prove my gratitude for freeing me", he then says, "and I did not lie. Please, take these with our blessings!"

Seeing your amazement at the shield, the merchant chuckles: "I found that shield years ago in the aftermath of the battle of Tanirith, when giants attacked the city. I learned that it first belonged to a dwarven hero named Galduur ..."
who died centuries ago ... other than that, I don't know much more of it." You continue to talk over more drinks until midnight. With a last farewell, you then leave.

You see the merchant's wife on the porch, watching over the children playing. She waves at you and smiles warmly:"My husband is gone, doing trading business and all ... I thank you again very much for freeing him!"  With a farewell, you go on your way.
This is the throne.
"Maybe you should go to the throne now?", the viceroy tells you, "After all, Lord Dhun is very busy and does not like to have his time wasted!"
Do you want to go back into the castle?

As you open the door, guards see you as intruders and shout the alarm. You have barely the time to make out a princely man sitting on a throne and a richly dressed wizard next to him, before the guards rush at you and attack!
As you open the door, guards see you as intruders and attack! You have barely the time to notice a richly dressed wizard and a regal  -if not princely- man already sitting in the room.
As you open the door, you see a princely man and a richly dressed wizard coming your way, along with a full contigent of guards. Upon seeing you, the wizard shouts: "Intruders! Protect Lord Dhun!"

Just as you open the door, a drudge from the kitchen along with numerous guards shouts from behind you: "There they are, the intruders I told ye about, mylords!"  The guards immediately attack. You have barely the time to make out a richly dressed ...
wizard and a princely man, both looking at you sternly from behind the guards.
This is a local brewery. You then notice what looks like a hatch on the ground next to the shack. Opening it, you find that it leads into a well built tunnel.  Do you go into it?
You find a concealed hatch on the wall. Opening it, you see that it leads to a well built tunnel.  Do you go into it?
Do you wish to get out of the inn through this secret tunnel?
You end up inside an ale and wine storage room.
Do you wish to go into the inn through this tunnel?
What kind of accomodations would you like?

"Here is your key", Areyna tells you, smiling. "Go to the corridor on the left end of the inn, and your suite will be the 3rd one on your left.  Enjoy yourselves, and thank you for staying at the Wildboar Inn!"
One of the drudges eyes you fearfully: "May I ask who ye may be, mylords?"  As you pretend to ignore her, she scampers away, most likely afraid of having irritated you.
One of the drudges bows to you: "Mylords? May I ask who ye be?" At your silence, the drudge simply goes about his chores, visibly scared of having offended you.
Suddenly, the castle starts to shake at its very foundations!
In a flash, you run out of the castle, hoping that it will not crumble right upon your heads!
It looks like those mysterious and powerful Overlords leave nothing to chance, don't they?
This secret tunnel is now hopelessly filled with boulders and rubble, having collapsed upon itself.
"Whot do ya want?", yells a gruff voice from behind the remparts. You can't make anyone from where you are standing.
What do you answer?
You come upon well built remparts. You cannot help but shudder at the site of numerous rotting heads mounted on pikes and left all along the remparts as a ghastly warning.
You hear numerous chuckles. "Well then, ya need ta pay us a thousand golds ta pass through here!", replies the same gruff voice.
Do you pay?

After giving the money through an opent slot on the steel doors, you hear more chuckles. "Well then", replies the same voice, "Me think ya should give all yer money instead!"  Suddenly, the doors open and orcs rush out to attack!
The steel doors of the remparts are wide open; the place certainly appears to be undefended, if not abandonned.
"No money, eh?", replies the gruff voice. "Well at least, let's hope ya'll give us some good sport!"  Suddenly, the doors open and orcs rush out to attack you!
"Too bad fer you!", replies the voice. Suddenly, the door open to let orcs rush out and attack you!
As you approach the compound, a score of orcs rush out to attack you. From behind them, you see what appears to be their commander.
After the battle, you search the compound and find the accumulated loot of the orcs' recent caravan raids. Looks like they had not yet sent it back to their village ... lucky for you!
This compound is abandoned.
"Ya'll see right now!", replies the voice. Suddenly, the doors open and orcs rush out to attack you!
"WHOT??? We've dwarf-friend scum at our doorstep!!!", shouts the voice. Suddenly, the doors open and orcs rush out to attack you!
As you approach this compound, orc guards see you and sound the alarm!
"Rid me of them intruders!", shouts a booming voice, as more orcs rush out of the compound to attack you. From behind them, you make out what appears to be their commander.

Caravans and people of all sorts are coming in and out of Wailsrond.  Although relatively small, this port city appears to be a major trading center nonetheless.  Numerous guards line the remparts, watchful.  Some of them eye you as you cross the ...
gates, but you are otherwise left unbothered.

These gates have a sign which reads: "First Port".  Numerous sailors, merchants, helpers, and carts carrying goods are coming through the gates, either going to the port or coming from it. You notice again numerous watchful guards along the battlements.

These gates have a sign that reads: "Second Port".  Numerous sailors, helpers, and carts carying goods come in and out through the gates, although in lesser numbers than the first port.  Again, you notice numerous watchful guards along the battlements.
This damp and dark cave appears unoccupied, except for the occasional bones of animals and humanoids lying about.
This looks like Wailsrond's Central Market. Many people and merchants are about, buying goods and foodstuffs, and haggling over prices.  Do you enter?
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master".  Many sailors, ship captains, travelers, and merchants go in and out of the building.  Do you enter?
The place is busy indeed!  What do you want to do?

You walk up to a series of kiosks, each one with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets" and the destination. You go to the kiosk marked with "Tanirith".  There, a lady smiles at you: "A ticket to Tanirith? That's 200 golds total".  Who will pay?
"Thank you. Go to the First Port, last pier on your left.  Your boat is right at the end of the pier.  Departures are at every four hours; have a good trip!"
"You don't have enough money ... another time, perhaps?"  Embarassed, you get on your way.

As you walk up to the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon".  After handing your tickets to him, you are escorted to your cabin: "The ship leaves in about five minutes and the trip will last eight hours".
Indeed, the ship leaves soon after you are settled in your cabin.  After an uneventful trip, you finally disembark at your destination.
While it took more time before leaving, the ship finally sails out.  After an uneventful trip (aside for high waves which were unsettling), you finally disembark at your destination.

As the ship leaves, you notice dark clouds looming.  Sure enough, a thunder storm rages throughout the trip, with high winds and rocky seas!  Nonetheless, you arrive safely at your destination, thanks to an expert captain!
You walk up to a series of kiosks, each with a sign with the words "Fare Tickets" and the destination. You walk up to the one with "Coral Towers".  There, a lady smiles at you: "Trip to the Towers?"

"Unfortunatley, all trips there are cancelled due to a high pirate activity", says the lady.  "Until this problem is dealt with, we must turn passengers away. I'm truly sorry." Pondering on this, you leave.
Guards block you way. "This area's restricted: no unauthorized folks may come here!"

You walk up to the office with the sign: "Ship Rentals".  As you open the door, an old mariner storms out, fuming: "Me cain't believe this! No more rentals because of them damn pirates!  When will this problem be taken care off?".  Resigned, you leave.
The watch-guards nod to you politely.
Knights of the Flame are on watch duty. They politely nod to you.
You are entering Wailsrond's farmlands, which are also famous for the rhum that they make!
Pirates!!!
Your boat is about to be attacked ... do you veer around instead and surpise the would-be attackers?
A pirate vessel nears your ship.  Your captain tries to outsail it as best as he can, but to no avail.  In no time, the pirates board your ship!
After the battle, and having set the pirate ship a-fire, you help your captain take care of the wounded, and then you set sail once again.

Your mast-watcher spots a pirate ship attacking a merchant vessel.  Your captain wishes not to get involved, and would rather keep on sailing.  Do you try to convince him to sail forth in order to help the hapless merchant vessel?
