With much vigorous insistance, you change the mind of your captain.  Quickly and very deftly, your ship approches the merchant ship: you soon jump on board to help the sailors against the pirates.
Agreeing with the captain, you decide that the trouble is not worth the hassle.  You sail forward, leaving the merchant vessel's fate in the hands of the ruthless pirates.
After the battle, the merchant and the captain walk up to you: "Our thanks, strangers!  Without your help, we would be done for!  Please, accept this token of our gratitude".
"Good sailing!", bids the merchant, as your ship and his part.  Your captain then gives the order to sail forth.
Seedy-looking characters attack you!
The gates are closed and locked.  From the battlements, knights of the Flame glare at you: "No one's allowed to the castle grounds, except those with proper business!", yells one of the knights.
"No problem", replies the knight, as you back away.

The knight appraises you for what seems like an hour. "Hey!", he says finally, "Aren't you the guys who put Akkar Dhun out of commission?"  Without thinking, you nod.  The knight then smiles: "We may need folks like you! Come in, but go to the guard ...
compound before going to the castle, okay?  There, you'll get a pass for the castle.  Tell them what you just told me!"  The doors open and you are waved through.
"Sure", replies the knight derisively, as his collegues chuckle along with him.
"Who do you think we are?", yells the knight.  "Begone NOW, or you will pay for your mischief!"
You are rapidly overwhelmed, especially since the Knights get quick help from Tanirith's militia. Bound in chains, you are brought to the Justice Hall in order to be judged by a magistrate.

The magistrate comes in the court room: "What have we here?", he asks. After hearing of your mischief from each of the officers involved, the magistrate looks at you sternly: "We scoff at such activities in our city. However, we are kind ...
and just. Therefore, since this is your first offense, each of you shall be fined 100 gold pieces."  Who will pay?

You pay the fine. "And remember", adds the magistrate, "one more offense, and to Tarterys you go!".  You are then escorted out. Before you finally go, a soldier tells you: "Believe me: you don't want to end in prison on Tarterys Island!"  He then leaves.
"Very well, then", the magistrate intones at your lack of money to pay the fine. "I therefore sentence you to a week in jail!"

You are then chained and brought to a ship leaving for Tarterys Island. After an hour's sail, you are disembarked, quickly striped of your gear, food, and spell components, then thrown in what looks like a communal incarceration facility.
"You again?", intones the magistrate upon seeing you. "I gave you fair warning: I therefore sentence you to a month in Tarterys Island!"
Do you wish to go back into this tunnel?
You find a tunnel leading within the mountains. Do you enter it?
You find yourself within fortifications.
As you approach the gates, orc guards see you and attack.  One of the guards shouts: "Alert! Intruders!!!"
You find yourself outside the fortifications and near the mountains to the east of them.
This is Wailsrond's City Hall.  Do you enter?
This is a temple of Ukkor, God of the Seas.  Do you wish to enter?
You see a lot of people going on and about their business.  Right in the lobby, you see an information desk.  What do you enquire about?
"I see that you are adventurers indeed!", replies the clerk.  "Here is a pass to the Lord's Castle; he is looking for brave folks like you. I bid you safe journeys!"
"Yes! We have grave problems about that! In fact, the Lord of Wailsrond has let it known that we need adventurers to help us resolve this problem: are you interested?"  What do you answer?
"How unfortunate", replies the clerk, visibly disapointed.  He then briskly waves you away to let other people come to his desk. You decide to leave.

"Unfortunately", replies the clerk, "tasks and jobs are currently unavailable, due to more pressing problems like the caravan raids and the pirate attacks. Would you be interested in helping us about these two bigger threats?"
The lobby looks as busy as ever.  You see the same clerk still sitting behind his information desk. Upon seeing you, he smiles: "I've heard the news! I bid you good luck!"  You then leave.
The guards nod politely as they let you pass.
This is a temple of Lharishar, Goddess of Life. Do you enter?
This temple is dedicated to Danuur, God of Commerce, Riches, and Luxuries.  Do you enter?
You are jumped upon by trolls!
An old beggar comes up to you and asks for charity.  Do you give him a gold piece?
A young boy comes up to you and asks for charity.  Do you give him a gold piece?
A woman holding two kids asks you for a bit of charity.  Do you give her a gold piece?
A young girl, dressed in rags, asks you for a bit of charity.  Do you give her a gold piece?
You just walk away without a word.

"Thank ye", mumbles the poor wretch.  "Times are hard ... whenever it gets too cold, I just go hide in the warm sewers through a secret tunnel, right under the monument in the park".  The wretch then goes away.

"Me thanks", mumbles the poor wretch. "Me often sleep in ta sewers when it gets cold, but too often strange things go on in there ... Me wonder where I'll find shelter, cuz me ain't going back there no more ..."  The wretch then goes away.
"Me thanks", mumbles the poor wretch, before simply going away.

"Me thanks", mumbles the poor wretch. "Me used to work for one of ta wine farms, but great evil has come upon this area ... vines and fields are rotting away fer no reason, and monsters abound now!"  The wretch then walks away.

"Thank ye", mumbles the poor wretch.  "Everything is going bad nowadays ... Me heard even the knights of the Flame have been corrupted ... if that's true, then there's no hope for us anymore ..."  The wretch then walks away.
Castle guards take your pass.  After examining it carefully, they let you enter the castle of the Lord of Wailsrond.
This is the compound for the castle's guards and Wailsrond's militia.  Two watch-guards nod at you as a militia patrol leaves the compound to make rounds in the city proper.

A huge warrior blocks your way. "I am Belrion, Lord Pyre's Captain of the Guards. I take it you wish to confer with our Lord?"  After you nod, he appraises you with much seriousness. "Very well", he finally says, apparently satisfied about your ...
character. "Follow me to the throne and to Lord Pyre", he then adds, before walking to the throne in order to stand beside a kingly man.
Belrion nods at you politely, while standing protectively near his Lord.

"Greetings, good adventurers!", announces warmly the Lord of Wailsrond. "I am Nerellius Pyre, Lord of this fine city of ours and home to these lands' famous rhum!  I take it you wish to help us in these times of need?"  You nod. "Your help is most ...

welcomed, brave ones!", chimes the Lord, obviously in relief. "Three major crises face our city, presently: numerous goblin and marauder raids on our trading caravans, and ruthless pirate attacks on our merchant vessels".

The Lord nods with approval.  "Yes, the goblins. They have been plaguing our trading caravans going to Aranys for the last six months or so. Their hideout is somewhere within Hark Wood, a forest just north-west of here, at the foot of the mountains".

"Find their hideout and eradicate their menace; 1000 gold pieces for each of you will be rewarded. I wish you a safe but successful hunt!"  With a handshake to seal the deal, you leave to complete your task.
The guards nod at you and let you enter the castle.
Guards nod at you in recognition.
Belrion waves at you at your approach.
"I assume you have been successful?", he says, smiling widely.  "Come! Let's go see Lord Pyre immediately!"
He then frowns. "I take it your task is not completed ... maybe you should come back only when you do so. Wailsrond needs to be rid of its menaces".  You then walk away.
"Which problem would you like to tackle?"

The Lord nods approvingly. "Yes, the marauders. We believe they are hiding somewhere in Dagger Keep, a shody town just north-east of us; the Keep's Lord, a shifty man named Doran Ghall, has consistently refused to look in the matter ...

I suspect that he is somehow involved in these raids. Find the marauders and their leader, and rid these lands of them! I pledge 1000 gold pieces for each of you if you do so".  After a handshake to seal the deal, you leave.
The Lord of Wailsrond greets you warmly: "Well done, friends! Well done indeed! Word of your deeds have reached us already! As promised, here is the reward you justly deserve!"
After pocketing your reward, Lord Pyre eyes you appraisingly: "Not that I would impose, but would you be willing to help us more?"  What do you answer?
Visibly relieved, the Lord smiles: "By the Gods, I hoped you would!"
Disapointed, Lord Pyre sighs: "Ah well, perhaps you need rest after all. If you change your mind, please come back".  You then leave.
Lord Pyre greets you warmly: "Welcome back, friends!  I trust you feel ready to help us again?"  You nod in agreement.

Lord Pyre welcomes you with open arms: "Amazing! You have done it all!!! Wailsrond will always be grateful to you, her official heroes! Here is the reward as promised, along with a few more items for our deep appreciation!"

The Lord then calls out for a day of celebration with, of course, you as the city's guests and declared heroes. During the festivities and the grand feast, the Lord leans over to you: "Truly, I thank you for restoring trade for our city".

The Lord goes on: "I will let the Lord Paladine of Tanirith know of your deeds; you will then be welcomed by him as the true heroes that you are and, besides, I know that he may need help as well".  Raising another toast to you, the Lord ...
winks knowingly in your direction. You look at each other, sighing in resignation: looks like a hero's work is never done!

After two more days of feasting, and staying at the castle as Lord Pyre's guests, you now feel the need to move on. After saying your goodbyes to the Lord and his trusted Captain, Belrion, you set out for more adventures.

The Lord nods pensively: "Yes, the pirates.  We have learned that they hide within an archipelago located far south of here, deep into the Great Ocean. The small islands are surrounded by coral reefs; a fleet is therefore ineffective to attack them ...

But one vessel, carrying daring-do-adventurers, could reach the main island where the mansion of Nurale Darkstrome, the Pirate Queen, is located.  Rid the seas of the Pirate Queen, and the other Pirate Lords will resume fighting among themselves ...

their menace therefore becoming less of a problem for merchant vessels. Do this, and I pledge 1000 gold pieces for each of you; of course, I have a vessel, with crew and captain, at your disposition. Board it as soon as you can; it is achored ...
in the First Port, at the end of the last pier on your left. I bid you success, brave ones!"  With a handshake to seal the deal, you then leave.

The Captain of your vessel is waiting for you: "Greetings, mateys! I'm Kaleb, Captain of ta Wandering Siren. A fine ship she is, mateys; no need to worry! Me and me crew are ready to sail at yer orders; all has been cleared by Lord Pyre! So let's go!"
The Captain then boards his ship, shouting orders to leave anchor and prepare to sail out.  You figure you should board the ship as well, lest it leaves without you!

Kaleb then stops: "Oh, one more thing ... Ta deal with our Lord is that we go where ye tell us; no problem! But once we're done, we'll have to dock back right here, or I'll throw ye out in ta sea as is me right! Agreed?"  You nod.

Belrion is at the gate, looking over guard duties. "Greetings again! Lord Pyre is occupied with city management and trade. I'll tell him you have come by to say hi".  After exchanging more news with Belrion, you then leave.

Belrion is at the gate, drilling some recruits at watch duty. "Greetings! Lord Pyre has gone to Sparklestone on city trading business. I'll tell him you have dropped by".  After swapping news with Belrion, you get on your way.

Belrion greets you at the gate. "Welcome back! Lord Pyre has gone on an extended trip to Tanirith, to meet with traders and merchants there. I'll tell him you came by!" After exchanging news with Belrion, you leave.

You walk to a series of kiosks, each one with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets" and a destination. You go to the one marked with "Coral Towers". There, a lady smiles: "Trip to the Towers? That's 1000 golds total for all of you".

As you approach the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon". After handing your tickets, you are shown to your cabin: "The ship leaves in 5 minutes; the trip will last four days".

You walk up to the office with the sign:"Ship Rentals". After waiting for about an hour (many merchants and mariners were waiting for their turn before you arrived), a lady makes you fill out forms. "Rental is 6000 golds, time unlimited, along with ...
Captain and crew".  Who will pay?
"Thank you. Go to First Port, last pier on your left: your vessel will be waiting for you there".

"Greetings!", a stout man chimes, as he walks up to you. "I'm Jerod, Captain of ta Sea Lion, ta ship ye have rented. We're ready to set sail and waitin' for ye!"  He then turns and boards his ship, shouting orders to prepare for setting sail.

The clerks smiles warmly at you: "Actually, and great thanks to the heroes that you are, all is well now for Wailsrond; trading is back in earnest both on land and sea!"  After more news swapping with the clerk, you then leave.

Captain Kaleb runs up to you, along with a few of his men, their swords drawn and bloodied: "I gather ta Pirate Queen's dead, for them other pirates are already fighting among themselves! We cain't be staying in ta crossfire! We have ta leave NOW!!!"
Figuring that you could come back later after renting a ship in Tanirith, you decide to follow the wisest course and go back to Kaleb's ship.  The Wandering Siren then sets sails hastily.

With relief, the trip back to Tanirith goes without any problems. The pirates must be fighting themselves indeed ... although, deep down, you know it won't be long until some of them begin their pirating anew.
"Take you good care!", shouts Kaleb after you disembark, "It was fun indeed, mateys!".  With final goodbyes, you set out for Lord Pyre's castle.
The sign above the door reads: "The Mariner's Den". Many sailors, merchants, and other people come in and out; the place looks busy indeed. Do you enter?
The place is loud, full of pipe smoke, dark with poor lighting, and reeking of swill.  You figure that you are in Wailsrond's favorite tavern for sailors and seamen.
"Whot will it be fer ye?", asks the bartender.
"That'll cost ye a bit", whispers the bartender, leaning towards you. "Me price is 10 golds ..."  Do you pay?
Who will pay?

He pockets the money, then whispers: "Wailsrond's a great city in full growth. Ta current Lord, Lord Nerellius Pyre, used ta be a merchant who made a fortune; ta all, he's turned out ta be great fer ta city and ta people! He's a good Lord indeed!"

He pockets the gold then whispers: "Sparklestone's a mining town growing fast! It's lorded over by two merchant companies; they're rivals but, so far, their squabbles haven't been bad for ta miners or ta townfolks; well, that's what I hear anyways ..."

He pockets the money:"Tanirith's centuries old; it's a huge city! Rich folks, merchants, and Lords live in High Town, which's high in ta nearby mountains. Ta current Lord Paladine, a knight of virtue by custom, is reputed fer his fairness and goodness."

He pockets the money: "Ta hole called Dagger Keep is rough. Many thieves abound there; ta current Lord, a rogue named Doran Ghall, is rarely seen or heard of. No one knows how he makes money, especially since ta Keep doesn't trade or anything ..."

He pockets the money then whispers: "Don't ye cause trouble in Tanirith, or ye'll be sent to the island-prison they call Tarterys. All criminals and rogues are sent there; its a grim, bad, and ugly place, I tell ye! And no one can escape!"

He pockets the money: "Sharranth's a fair-sized city; it was conquered five years ago by the Warlord Antraxus Storm; a ruthless warrior and a mighty one at that! Everybody knows he's looking ta gain dominion of ta whole Sword Lands, especially Tanirith!"
"Don't have ta money ta spare or that ye wanna give, eh? Then, don't ye be wasting me time!"

He pockets the money: "I've heard that beastmen live within a cave complex just west of here ... They've been a bit of a nuisance lately, especially fer trade caravans; rumor has it that a whole tribe of them lairs in them caves!"

He pockets the money, then whispers: "I've heard that them goblins, that have been raiding caravans, lair somewhere underneath ta Hark Wood, a forest just north-west of here. The entrance to their lair's rumored ta be hidden and hard ta find!"
He pockets the money: "Rumor has it that them marauders, that have been raiding caravans, hide in Dagger Keep and under Lord Doran Ghall's protection at that!"

He pockets the money then whispers: "I've heard that the Lord of Aranys is somehow connected ta all ta raiding that's been happening! Others say that he's even the mastermind behind it all! He's a greedy, power-hungry lot, that one!"

He pockets the money: "Rumors abound about Tanirith's sewers ... They say it's like an undercity down there, full of monsters and dangerous creatures! Many have gone exploring in there, and so far none has come out!"

He pockets the money then whispers: "I've heard that the Warlord of Sharranth is building up his army, a sign that he's itching for new conquests. I also heard that this time, he's hiring mercenaries of all sorts, including ogres and minotaurs!"

He pockets the money: "I've heard that ta Dwarven Halls are under siege from armies of orcs, ogres, and even giants! That's why dwarven merchants are rarely seen these days, and that their goods and mead have become rare luxuries!"
He pockets the money then whispers: "Rumor has it that ta pirates, that have been raiding merchant ships, have spies in Wailsrond, and in Tanirith! But no one knows who they are ..."

He pockets the money: "I've heard that Queen Aquillae, ta queen of Coral Towers, has disapeared ... Her Regent has been ruling in her stead, and brutally at that! Ye make yer own conclusions about this one, now ..." He then winks at you.

He pockets the money, then leans over to whisper: "A man named Harym is known around here for his contacts and secret deals ... He hangs here, always in ta right corner of ta pub, near ta entrance. Tell him I sent ye ... but be careful, eh?"

Harym sits alone quietly, sipping his rhum. "The bartender sent ye?", he replies after you approached him. "How cain I be of service to ye?", he then whispers, his eyes darting left and right to make sure no one pays attention to you and him.
"No problem", Harym replies, still whispering. "Me fee is 1000 golds ... ye pay me now or we have no deal".  Do you pay him?

He pockets the money, still being watchful at not being seen. "Meet me later at me house; it's ta last one behind ta pub, right next to ta city walls. Ta password is: MIDNIGHT". Finishing his rhum, he then leaves promptly.
This looks like Harym's house; the door is locked. What do you do?
No one answers.
The door opens, and Harym peers out: "Ye have come! Good! Come inside, me have ta information ya need!"
This is Harym's bedroom.
This looks like a pantry.

Harym looks a bit nervous. "Look, folks ... it took me a whole lot more to git ta information ye wanted than what me thought ... So, me needs an extra 1000 golds for me troubles, or ye don't git ta information".  Do you pay the extra?
"Well git out, then! And me better never see ye again!", snarls Harym.  Do you leave?
"Not enough money, no information! Git out then; and me better never see ye again!", snarls Harym.  Do you leave?
Harym hastily pockets the money. "Follow me to me basement: me have all ta papers that prove ta information ye asked". Without a word, you follow him, eager to finally get the information you seek.

Going down a ladder under a trap door, you end up in the basement only to find Harym standing behind a bunch of thugs: "Git them boys! They be asking ta wrong questions about our friends!"  At that, Harym and his accomplices attack!
At your refusal to leave, Harym runs to a trap door in the corner of his house, yelling for help. Out of the basement come numerous thugs  -obvious accomplices of Harym-  and they all jump on you!
It looks like you had been set up by Harym all along, and that he was working for the enemy!  You decide to further investigate his house for useful clues.
No one seems about; the place looks abandoned.
This trap door is opened, revealing a ladder going to a basement.  Do you wish to go down?
"No problem", replies the bartender, smiling. "What will ye have?"
The bartender pours your drinks. "That'll be 2 golds per drink; 12 golds fer all of ye".
With your drinks in hand, you leave to find a table and some good seats.
"Dwarven Hall mead is gettin' a bit rare because of ta siege of ta Dwarven Halls, so it'll be 10 golds per drink, 60 golds for all of ye".

"Greetings!", says this man at your approach, "My name is Runelore Magius; I'm a mage looking for fame and fortune, if you know what I mean"; at that, he winks at you while smiling. "I saw you come in, and I wonder if you would have me in your group?"
Do you take Runelore into your ranks?
Runelore Magius has been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.
"Ah well", sighs Runelore, "I had to ask".  Without further word, he walks away.
"Superb!", Runelore exclaims, obviously happy to join you. "You shall not regret your decision!" He winks at you once more, before starting to follow you.

A militia patrol barges in right after the brawl has ended. "What's going on here?", asks the patrol leader. Because patrons accuse the drunken thugs, or you, or both, of starting the brawl, the patrol leader fines everyone involved 25 gold pieces ...
each, or go to jail.  Which option do you choose?
Pay fine.
Go to jail.
The patrol leader collects the fines. "Be warned", he then adds, "that we have your names; a second offense from you and you will be expelled from Wailsrond!" At that, the militia patrol leaves.

"No money to pay or ye don't want to pay? To jail, then!"  The militia escorts you to the  City Hall, straight to the city jail located within its basement. After a night, your personal items are returned to you, and you are freed.
Before you leave, a justice clerk warns you sternly: "One more offense, and you will be expulsed from our city; so, you better behave from now on!"  Without a word, you walk away.

A militia patrol barges in right after the brawl is ended. "What is going on here?" yells the patrol leader. He then gasps upon seeing you: "The Heroes of Wailsrond?  What honor that we have!"  He then looks sternly at the thugs: "We should have ...

expulsed you long ago! And now you bother our acclaimed Heroes???"  After apologizing for the rude behavior of these thugs, the patrol then escorts the lot in order to expulse them out of the city. Some patrons start looking at you with awe and respect.

A militia patrol barges in right after the end of the brawl. "You again?", yells the patrol leader. "That's it! You were warned! You are now forbidden to come within Wailsrond!" You are promptly escorted outside the city walls.
Guards block your way: "You have been forbidden to enter Wailsrond. Begone!"
A militia patrol stops you: "We regognize you! You have been forbidden to enter Wailsrond!"  They promptly escort you outside the city walls.

A militia patrol barges in after the end of the brawl: "What goes on here?", yells the patrol leader. Because the patrons all point to the thugs as the culprits for starting the fight, the patrol takes them to jail, with an apology for your troubles.
Knights of the Flame on watch duty politely nod at you, and let you pass.

"Halt!", a knight of the Flame begins to tell you, only to stop in surprise. "Aren't you the Heroes of Wailsrond?", he asks tentatively.  You nod. "Hey!", he then turns to his fellow knights also on watch, "It's them! They're here!!!"

The other knights then gather around you in cheer: "We have been waiting for your arrival since we heard of you!", adds the young knight, "And so has our Lord Paladine! Please, go to the castle; I'll give foreword of your coming!"

The young knight then rushes out to the castle, while his comrades go on cheering, and gazing at you in admiration and respect.  After a few handshakes and claps on shoulders in return, you then slowly walk to the castle, feeling a bit embarrassed ...
at such attention and praise.  Looks like heroic deeds are truly their own rewards!
Knights of the Flame on watch duty nod at you in respect before letting you through the gate.
You are suddenly under attack by hill giants!

A bunch of somber, tough-looking, and cocky adventurers are sitting here. Their leader, a huge and brawny warrior, rises up to you: "Whot do ye want, ye bums?", he asks menacingly, his hand already on the pommel of his sword.
How do you make your stand?
Walk away.
Make a stand.
The warrior and his fellow adventurers laugh out loud. "What a bunch of yellers!" he shouts, as you walk away peacefully. Despite the jibes, you know you have done the right thing.
You come upon a bunch of mean-looking, foul-smelling, drunken seamen. One of them looks at you: "Hey you! Why don't ye pay us a round of mead fer us nice sailors!" His friends chuckle at that.
Pay the round.
At your acceptance, the drunken seamen burst into a cheer. A wench brings over the mead: "For all", she tells you, "it will cost 125 golds".  Who will pay?
"Thank you". replies the wench, before walking away. In turn, you walk away from the seamen, who have now started singing (and badly at that!) some bawdy song about sirens ...

"What do ye mean, no money?" the wench asks angrily, at your failure to pay her. "LOAF!!!", she then screams. Immediately. a huge half-ogre, along with six other strongmen, surround you. "Me Loaf", the half-ogre says, "and me and me buddies ...
will throw ye out now, okay?"  Without even having the time to breathe, Loaf and his six comrades throw you out of the pub, while the other patrons burst out in laughter.
You open the pub's door only to come face to face with Loaf the half-ogre: "Ye no welcome here, okay?" he says, before slamming the door in your faces.
"Oh no ye don't!", shouts the sailor as he grabs your shoulder, "Ye pay us a round or we don't be friendly!" His friends begin to mumble, obviously looking for any excuse to fight.

The wench leans over you as you keep searching for some money: "No worry, good Heroes of our city", she whispers with a wink, "I'll charge them double their drinks fer the rest of the night; that's all they deserve fer annoying decent folks like you!"
The wench then walks away, not before smiling at you one more time.
You ship is suddenly under attack!!!

welcomed, brave ones!", chimes the Lord, obviously in relief. "I heard word of your deeds concerning the goblins: I would like to thank you for solving that problem without our asking!" He then sighs: "But we still have two crises plaguing us:
