You stumble on a conversation: "I hear that Akkar Dhun's castle was brought low!", chimes someone. "Yep!" replies another, "From what I know, some adventuring group exposed him as a link to what's been happening lately in the Sword Lands!"

"But what happened to his castle, exactly?" asks the first. "He was messing around with dark sorcery and demon lords, from what I hear", replies the second, "and it all blew up in his face!". Both start laughing.

"What happened to the castle?" asks the first. "Dhun's masters, some lich-sorcerers, got angry at him for being exposed, or so I hear". "Powerful masters!" chimes the first. "Yep", replies the second. Then both stay silent at that dread realization.

"What about Dhun's castle?" asks a third person. "His masters, some ancient, dark and evil Gods, got angry at him for his failure, or so I hear" replies the second. Then all involved remain silent at that dread announcement.
"And the adventurers?" someone asks finally. "I heard the brave fools died too!", replies the first. "A damn shame", adds someone else, "for we need folks like that in these troubled times".
You then go quietly about your way, thinking that news travel fast indeed, even more so grossly altered versions of them!

Naryl Dragonstone then whispers to you: "I would not do that, if I were you, for he is not to be trusted ... something about him tells me that. Don't ask why or how I feel this, simply trust me, if you would ..."  She seems quite convinced and sincere.
Do you still accept Runelore Magius into your ranks?

Naryl gathers her gear: "I, for one, know that I will not regret your decision", she says with genuine sadness, "for I have to go somewhere else. Fare you well, friends, and I sincerely hope that! I'm sure our paths will cross again, the Gods willing."

Naryl then leaves, with you having no time to stop her or convince her to do otherwise. "Is something wrong?" asks Runelore, obviously confused. Not sure yourselves about what just happened, you shrug the whole thing off and go about your business.

You come upon a well-kept adventurer sitting comfortably while sipping his mead and smoking his pipe. You notice a huge white wolf dozing next to his chair. "Greetings!", the man chimes, smiling warmly as he invites you to join him at his table.

You sit down as he pours you some mead from his buck. "I understand that you were responsible for Akkar Dhun's demise", he states with a grin. Visibly amused at your surprise, he goes on: "Actually, I had an interest in finding out who performed ...

this noble deed, for I was in the castle when it started to fall upon my head!" The man chuckles good-naturedly. "People call me Strider", he adds as he shakes your hand, "Like you, an adventurer; I was trying to find out if Dhun was involved or not ...

in the rising troubles of late. It appears that we have set ourselves on the same path! On my end, I had already found out that some mysterious Overlords are responsible for what's going on, and that Dhun was likely to be an agent for them."

At that, you tell Strider what you found in the castle before it crumbled. He frowns: "Much you have uncovered, but much remains to be exposed. Nonetheless, the Overlords are real and must be dealt with as soon as possible ..." Strider then yawns.

"Well, it's time for me to turn in; I have been on the road for days, along with dear Whitefang here." At the mention of her name, the wolf raises her head. "I rescued her a few years ago from a bear trap", Strider adds fondly, "and since then, she ...

has been following me." After gathering his gear, Strider shakes your hand one more time: "Safe journeys and safer returns, friends! By working on each other's end, we will both uncover those Overlords; for that, we will meet again I know!"
Strider then walks out of the pub, with Whitefang faithfully not far behind his steps.

You sit down as he pours you some mead from his buck. "It's always a pleasure to meet fellow adventurers", he adds, smiling warmly. "I have been traveling for days with dear Whitefang here." You notice that the wolf raises her head at the mention of her

name. "I'm sorry: people call me Strider", the man chuckles, as he shakes your hand, "and this is Whitefang; I rescued her a few years back from a bear trap: since then, she has been following me!" You and Strider then go on exchanging news and bits.

At one point, Strider yawns. "My apologies, but my body is telling me that it is time to go to sleep. I thank you for your company, and I bid you safe journeys and safer returns!" At that, Strider gathers his gear and shakes your hand once more.

You notice Naryl Dragonstone staring intently at the departing Strider. You then ask her what is wrong: "Oh! Nothing!", she replies demurely, yet quite preoccupied, "Somehow, I percieve this man to be special ... very much good-hearted and noble".
At her hesitation to explain her say further, you drop the matter and go on about your business.

You notice Runelore Magius staring at the departing Strider, while being deep in thought. You then ask him what is wrong: "Oh! Nothing", he replies distractively, yet obviously preoccupied. "Its just that ... well, I don't know, but for some reason ...

I get the feeling that this man is not to be trusted ...." At that, he shrugs, going back to sipping his mead. Dropping the matter, you do the same; however, you are begining to wonder if you should remain trustful when meeting strangers.

You sit down as he pours you some mead from his buck. "I take it you are the famous Heroes of Wailsrond" he states while winking good-naturedly at you. "Of course, good deeds are news that travel far and wide! But I'd rather hear of them from those ...

involved, and not distorted, preposterous versions of them!" He chuckles. "People call me Strider; I'm a humble adventurer like you. This here is Whitefang; I rescued her a few years back from a bear trap, and she has been following me since."

You notice the wolf raising her head at the mention of her name. "So", adds Strider, smiling warmly "care to spin your tale for me?" You then proceed to tell him of your recent adventures. "A conspiracy involving a mysterious "A.D", going as far ...

as Coral Towers, eh?" he chimes in after you have finished. "Well", he chuckles, "it's rather easy to guess who A.D. is, no?" Amused by your surprise, he goes on: "Akkar Dhun, of course. I had reasons to believe that he works for some ...

self-proclaimed Overlords, and what you told me confirms my suspicions ... As to who the Overlords are, that remains a mystery; however, I am certain they are responsible for the troubles of late!" Strider chuckles again: "Well! It appears that ...

we are more or less embarked on the same path!" He then yawns, "I guess it's time for me to turn in; I have been on the road for days, you know." Gathering his gear, Strider shakes your hand: "Safe journeys and safer returns, friends! I have ...
a hunch that we will meet again!" After another good-natured wink, Strider walks out of the pub, with Whitefang faithfully not far behind his steps.

You sit down as he pours you some mead from his buck. "I take it you're the famous Heroes of Wailsrond", he states good-naturedly. "I also understand that you were responsible for Akkar Dhun's demise." Visibly amused at your surprise, he goes on:

"Actually, I had an interest in finding who performed the latter noble deed, for I was in the castle when it started to fall upon my head!" The man smiles warmly: "People call me Strider", he adds as he shakes your hand, "Like you, an adventurer."

"I have been looking into who is responsible for the troubles of late; my hunch is that Dhun, the goblins, Doran Ghall, and the pirates are mingled together". You nod in earnest, then proceed to tell him about what you have uncovered so far.

After listening to you patiently, Strider nods in deep thought. "It appears that we have stumbled onto the same path", he then says. "Yes ... much has been uncovered, yet much remains to be exposed. I had already found out that those mysterious ...

Overlords are the true puppet masters behind it all; I also know that they come from Anarym, the large continent to the east of the Realmz, far across the Ocean of Ukkor. They must be found and dealt with, my friends!" At that, Strider yawns.
This chest hold personal belongings like boots, gloves, old clothes, and such.  However, you find do find something of value!
This hanger holds pants and cloaks. You find something useful among them!
In this chest, you find numerous bottles of wine and rhum; looks like Harym kept a personal reserve of fine spirits!
You find nothing of interest on this coat hanger, save for old cloaks, pants, and the like.
These look like goods stolen directly from merchant warehouses. It appears that Harym was a true black market dealer, and a successful one at that!
This chest is empty.

This looks like Harym's business desk. Aside from black market transactions, buyers, sellers, and contacts, you find three scroll cases, each holding a letter. The first one reads: "Harym- Good work so far on keeping us informed on what is going on ...

in Wailsrond. We now need you to send the attached letters through the usual channels. One is for Coral Towers, the other is for our esteemed but tempestuous Lady of the seas. Your contact should have given you the appropriate moneys for you and your ...

friends. Keep up the good work. Signed: M for A.D." You then open the case destined for Coral Towers: "Dear T.R.. Your last report was received; the Overlords are pleased. However, they have expressed their misgivings concerning your methods of ...

quelling any and all signs of discontent or dissent. They warn you to be careful: too much will attract too much attention from opposing leaders, and this would jeopardize your position (and that of the Overlords). My advice to you is to heed their ...

warnings, if you know what is best for you. Until your next report, good health and glory. Signed: A.D.". You open the second one: "Dear N.D., I hope all goes well and that your treasury keeps growing. The Overlords are pleased by your efficiency and ...

success! However, they express some reservations about the cohesiveness of your fleet, and how long you could manage to keep it united. I have assured them that you were in complete  -and absolute-  control. But remember that the Overlords are ...

generous to those who serve them well; I think that they value you: hence, they would help you maintain or consolidate your rule, as much as they have helped you to achieve your current seat of power. So do not hesitate to ask for help if required; ...

to do otherwise would be too costly (aside from earning the Overlords' wrath). I bid you good health and continued success. Signed: A.D.". Knowing you have stumbled upon crucial documents, you put them back in their scroll cases for safekeeping.

You stumble upon a suspicious depression under the rug. After removing the rug, you find a trap door, which opens to a small compartment in the floor. Looks like you have found Harym's secret cache of his ill-acquired earnings!
Harym's cache is now empty, thanks to you.

A group of dwarves, very drunk, are commiserating together. "It be now impossible to get back to ta Halls", rages one, "because of those durn orcs!".  "Aye!" chimes another, "an' I hear ta same orc bastards are allied wif ogres an' bloody giants!"

"By ta Gods!" adds a third one, "all together are laying siege to ta Halls?" The first one nods: "Aye! An' no one knows how much longer our kin cain stand and resist ...". A fourth one gets up: "I got me an idea! Let's round up all dwarves from here ...

ta Tanirith, an' march up to the Halls to help, kicking heads wif those orc pigs while we do that!!!" The whole lot of dwarves then burst into a cheer and start to sing one of their numerous songs of battle. You know they won't be going nowhere the ...
way they are drunk, and how much they keep drinking.

Just as you turn around to leave, you find yourselves face to face with another dwarven adventurer, this one quite sober. From his attire, he must be a warrior-priest of Moradin, God of Dwarves and of the Holy Forge.

"I noticed yer shield", he says in a low voice so his words remain out of earshot of his drunken bethren. "Galduur's a great, legendary hero to us. That ye have somehow found his shield is good tidings not just fer us dwarves, but fer all goodly ...

races as well! Fer indeed, Galduur helped all those who needed help, defended all those defenseless, regardless whether they were dwarves or not. So I say this to ye: follow Galduur's example, and help all those who need help." He then sighs: "Even ...

desperate dwarves, who have lost all hope against seemingly impossible odds. So I ask ye to think hard on helping my bethren, and go to the Dwarven Halls; bring them this sign of hope that ye hold! I cain't force you, fer some paths can only be ...

chosen, not imposed. I do hope that ye will do what's right by all and the Gods". At that, he nods respectfully and goes back to his comrades, joining into their songs while pretending to be as drunk as they are.

You see on the porch of this rich house a woman sitting in a rocking chair and visibly in tears, with what looks like her husband who is trying to console her. He himself looks on the verge of despair. "My rebellious daughter was kidnapped days ago" ...

the husband tells you. "Her kidnappers demanded 10000 golds for her return, and we have paid the ransom. But ..." Then the woman screams: "But she hasn't been returned to us!!! What are we to do?" She breaks down and cries.

"Ever since she turned seventeen, she has been impossible", mumbles the husband. "At first, we thought she had ran away, once again. But when we received the ransom note, we knew then what really happened ..." The man sighs: "The authorities are on ...
the case, but we have yet to receive any news. We fear the worst, now". You then walk away quietly, respecting the grief of these desperate parents.

You see Belrion conversing with a couple on the porch of this luxurious house. "We meet again!", he greets you. "How goes your task?" You tell him you are on it. "Good! I have some serious business to take care here, so I bid you farewell!"

Before going, you ask him what business is that. Belrion sighs: "Anaele, this merchant's daughter, has been kidnapped. The 10000 golds ransom was paid, but ..." He slowly shakes his head at that. Understanding his meaning, you quietly go about your way.
"Wait!", calls the husband. "I recognize you, now: you are the Heroes of Wailsrond! I beg of you: help us find our beloved Anaele!"  Do you accept to help these distraught parents?
"Oh thank you!" exclaims the husband. You then set yourselves to find their daughter.
"To the Abyss with you then! Some heroes you are!", snarls the husband. You then leave promptly, feeling ashamed of yourselves.

As you approach the porch of this rich house, Anaele runs to the door: "Popa! Moma!", she yells, happy tears in her eyes. Her parents come out, embracing their daughter. "You are safe!", cries her mother. "Thank you so much!" the father tells you.
You then leave quietly, respecting the privacy of this happily reunited family.

You find a couple in tears on the poor of this luxurious house. "Our daughter was kidnapped", the man tells you. "We paid the ransom, but she was never returned to us", the woman adds. You then tell them the painful news about finding their daughter ...
but she later died. The woman becomes hysterical with distress, while the man starts sobbering uncontrollably. You quietly leave them to their private grief.

As you approach the house, Anaele starts running to the porch: "Moma! Popa!", she yells. Her parent rush out of the house, embracing their daughter. "You are safe!", cries the mother. "Thank you so much!", the father tells you. "I would never guess ...
that you cared enough to go and find our girl!"  You then slowly walk away, respecting the privacy of this happily reunited family.

You walk to Anaele's parents, still making some kind of vigil for their daughter's return. You tell them that you found her, but that she later died. The woman then becomes hysterical with distress, while the man starts to sob. You quietly leave.
"Go away! Leave us alone, you louses!" yells the man from behind the closed door of his house.

Anaele's parents are still making a vigil on the porch, waiting for the return of their daugher. "Have you found her?" asks the mother with hope. At your negative answer, she starts crying as her husband quietly comforts her. You then leave.
You see Anaele on the porch, still resting and recuperating from her ordeal. She waves at you with a happy smile. All things seem to be for the better, now.
No one seems to be about. You wonder if the merchant and his wife have moved away after the death of their daughter.

The merchant then comes out with a small chest: "Please take these as tokens of our deepest gratitude! We will be eternally thankful!"  The wife, crying with happiness adds: "Truly, you are heroes worthy of the title!"
You then leave quietly, respecting the privacy of this happily reunited family.
The sign on the door reads: "The Tranquil Tide Inn". Do you enter?
The place is cozy and very well kept. "Greetings", chimes a woman behind a desk, "Would you like to stay the night?"
"That will be 20 golds for each of you". Who will pay?
"Come back whenever you want", the desk-lady tells you, before you leave.
"Here is your key. Have a good sleep". You walk to your room; you find it to be of top class, very comfortable, and very clean.
"Not enough money? Another time, perhaps".
You wake up the in morning, well rested and ready to tackle another adventuring day. After gathering your gear, you bring back the key to the desk-lady.
You find nothing of interest on this desk, save for some parchment sheets.
Searching this desk, you find some parchment sheets. You also find a secret compartment which holds a key.
You find nothing more of value here.
You find a concealed door, well blended with the brick walls. After searching further, you notice a small lock.
You enter a dark and damp room. From your left, you can hear a girl moaning.
The key fits the lock, and the door opens!
You leave the make-shift cell.
You enter the make-shift cell.

You find a young girl, barely seventeen years old, chained to the wall. Her clothes are all thorn or ripped off, and she looks badly bruised. A thick straw rug serves as a matress. "So", she mumbles weakly, "More friends of Harym who will have their ...
way with me?"  She then spits at you in defiance.  What do you do?

Without a word, you free her of her chains. She gapes at you, while rubbing her sore wrists and ankles. Tears begin to trickle down her cheeks. "Thank you so much", she sobs. "My name is Anaele; I was kidnapped days ago and kept here at my captor's ...
whim, a terrible man named Harym. Will you please bring me home?"  What do you answer?

Anaele jumps into your arms, crying of joy and gratefulness. You notice how much she is now shivering from the stress brought about after days of enduring such cruelty. You heal her as best as you can and provide her with some spare clothes ...
that you found in Harym's house. "I live in one of the rich houses nearest to the castle of the Lord of Wailsrond", she finally adds, before you all set off.
Anaele has been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.
"Fine", Anaele states, sobbing. "I guess I am truly worthless after all! Better to be on my own then!"  She then rushes out of her make-shift cell. Before you can react, she is long gone.
Without further due, you bury the body.

You find the body of Anaele, the kidnapped girl you refused to take home. From the looks of her mangled body, she was attacked by wolves. You now realize the folly of your earlier decision to leave her to her own devices.
Sadly, and without a word, you bury what is left of her body.
"Why?" she snarls. "You like to know the name of those your are about to violate? You are scum perverts!"  She spits at you again.

"Not interested in me anymore, eh? I'm damaged good now, eh?" the girl snarls as you start to leave. "Well congratulations! You get to watch me die, instead! And to the Abyss with Harym, my captor!"  She then takes out a broken piece of glass she ...

had been hiding under the straw rug and swiftly slits her own throat! Rushing back to her, you see that there is nothing you can do. Upon her last gasps of breath, you hear the girl whisper, as tears trickle down her cheeks: "Anaele is free, now ..."

After you slap her, the girl starts giggling hysterically. "I'm tired of this ... over and over again. You can violate me all you want, but you'll never own me! And to the Abyss with Harym, my captor!" She then takes out a broken piece of glass she ...
Some adventurers nod at you politely.
You find some foodstuffs you can take with you.
You also find a useful map.

After searching the cavern, you find a secret door within the north wall. You notice that this door is extremely large, being about 30 feet high and 40 feet wide! You also find the opening mechanism of the door, consisting of a false rock to be pulled.
Do you open the door?

The door opens, revealing a huge tunnel carved out within the very mountain rocks. Although visibly ancient, its walls are smooth, as if the tunnel had been made by using huge quantities of corrosives! You go into the tunnel.
Do you wish to enter the tunnel through the secret door?

You come upon a large cavern, being about 80 feet in diameter and a good 50 feet high! In the center of it, you see a huge pile of coins, gems, jewelry, exotic fabrics, weapons, armors, shields, and so on!!! You also spot other chests filled with riches!

Pretty sure that the place is abandoned, you rush to the treasure pile. Obviously, you have found a long-forgotten cache of riches! As you throw yourselves with glee into the coins, you wonder to whom such accumulated wealth used to belong to!
Suddenly, the center of the pile begins to move and heave! And out of it comes a huge, dark brown, draconian head! This brown dragon doesn't seem happy to have been disturbed ...

"What would you be?", the brown dragon asks you, his deep, rumbling voice booming throughout the cavern. Not understanding the question, you simply stare at him dumbfounded, and stricken with fear. "Mortals!", sighs the dragon in disgust. "I am ...

Chlorapyroshyndragosuur, a brown dragon, and scourge of the world. I ask again: what would you be?"  Each of you stammers his or her name, and your races. The dragon sighs again: "I meant, you simpletons, if you are thieves, food, or servants".

"No matter", the dragon adds at your failure to reply, "I have been sleeping for centuries, and I am hungry!" The brown dragon then swiftly raises himself to his full height and attacks! At the same time, a couple of his "servants" rush in to help him!

However, you notice that something big is actually lying underneath the pile of riches. No sooner that you have realized this, a huge, dark brown, draconian head comes out of the pile! This dragon doesn't seem happy to have been disturbed ...

To your chagrin, you find that most of Chlorapyroshyndragosuur's hoard was destroyed in the battle. But having survived such an opponent, and seeing that there is still enough loot to please, you happily shrug off the feeling!
You grin at each other: looks like you have really hit the jackpot!
Suddenly, a family of cave bears rush out from the deep end of this cavern and attack you, obviously feeling threatened by your intrusion!
After the clash, you decide you might as well process the carcasses.
You are then escorted out of the inn. "Remember", adds Zaran before closing the door, "come back anytime after tonight".
"Ye want another job?" the dwarf asks.  What do you answer?
"Here's what I have", he says.

"Ha!", exclaims the dwarf. "Gnats, eh? It's simple: a whole tribe of Gnats is lairing inna cavern complex near Wailsrond; they've become a nuisance. Destroy their lair, is all! Here's a map to their caverns; the job pays 500 golds fer the group".

"The wyrm, eh?" chimes the dwarf. "We don't know much except that Chlorapyroshyndragosuur was a fearsome menace. He disapeared centuries ago; he's probably sleeping! All we know is that he used to lair inna cavern just north-east of here. Good luck!"
"Ye've done it already, I heard about it through some of them fast traveling news! Good job!" The dwarf hands the reward.

"Durn it!", exclaims the dwarf, "I already paid fer that one! This paperwork is a mess; why'd they pick me to do that crazy job???" He then searches through another pile of sheets, retrieving one of them: "Here! Let's see if THIS job list will do!"
You have the uncomfortable feeling of being observed or followed. Do you attempt to make your "virtual" pursuers reveal themselves?
You turn around and dash in the general direction from where you felt you were being observed. And you were right: you WERE being stalked, and now your pursuers have no choice but attack you!
Shrugging off this weird sensation, you go on about your way. Suddenly, you are ambushed: looks like your gut instinct was right after all ...
Tired and panting after this clash, you tell yourselves to better listen to your instinctive feelings from now on!

A thick, barbed wire fence surrounds the yard of this big house. A bronze plaque reads in big letters: "Bloodstone Heights Mining Company and Traders".  Mercenary guards, along with tamed wolves, patrol within the estate.

A guard walks up to you: "No one without proper business is allowed here! Begone!"  You notice other guards looking in your direction, as their tamed wolves bark angrily in warning. You decide to walk away.
This mine is closed and boarded shut. The word "Condemned" is painted in red dye onto the wood planks.

A guard walks up to you: "Hey! Aren't ye those guys who did Akkar Dhun in?" Unsure if you should answer, you remain silent. The man grins: "Yes, ye're the ones! My boss would like to meet ye!" He then opens the gate and leads you to the estate.

You are then brought to a luxurious office in which a middle-aged man sits behind a huge oak desk, obviously busy with paperwork. At your entrance, he gets up from his chair, smiling warmly: "Greetings! I am Lharond Dragonspurr, owner of ...

this humble mining company. I'm quite honored at meeting genuine heroes such as you!" He exclaims, shaking your hand. "I was hoping you would drop by our town, for we have a problem which perhaps you could solve for us. One of the mines is haunted ...

or something like that; it had to be shut down weeks ago because miners refused to go back in. Maybe you could investigate this matter for me? In these troubled times, companies such as mine need all the money they can get! Of course, I will ...
compensate you generously for your efforts and troubles! What say you, brave ones?"
Do you accept to help?
"Thank you!", replies Lharond. "Come with me and a few of my guards: we''ll take you to this troublesome mine". You then all leave.

"This is it!" Lharond tells you. "I'll wait for your return in my estate: I bid you sucess!" After Lharond's guards remove the wooden planks of the closed mine, you go in. "Good luck!", Lharond tells you again.
"Ah well ...", sighs Lharond. "If you ever change your minds, please come back".  You are then courteously escorted out of the estate.

"Ahem!", chimes in Runelore, quite demurely. "Actually ... This is so embarassing ... I am afraid of enclosed spaces, you see ... So, perhaps I could sit this one out? I'm so sorry friends." He looks genuinely afraid to go underground.

"I do not mind entertaining your friend in the meanwhile", suggests Lharond, with a smile. You decide to assent to Runelore's request. "Oh thank you friends! I have been working on being less afraid of enclosed spaces, but I still have ways to go".
You then proceed to the mine alongside Lharond and some of his guards.

Once you have entered the mine, you hear Lharond laughing out loud from the outside: "Fools!!! That will teach you to mess with the wrong people! You have the best wishes of the Overlords!" Suddenly, the entrance to the mine begins to cave in!!!
Looks like you were suckered good, and now you are trapped!
"My friends", intervenes Runelore, "If heroes that you are, heroes you must remain. Can you truly refuse to help and live with your conscience afterwards?"
Do you reconsider?
Lharond sighs again. "Well, I still hope you will change your mind". You are then escorted courteously out of the estate. You notice that Runelore seems a bit pensive.
As you approach Lharond's estate, you see him come out to meet you. "Have you changed your minds?" He asks hopefully. You nod.

As you approach Lharond's estate, you see him already outside behind a line of mercenary guards and their trained wolves. "So! You managed to make it back, eh?", he snarls. Without word, he gestures to his guards to attack.
Now Lharond himself enters the fray, along with his remaining mercenaries!
The entrance to this mine is hopelessly blocked by fallen rocks and rubble.

Defeated, you are bound in chains. "This was easier than luring you into the mine", muses Lharond. "Only now you realize what futility it was to oppose the Overlords". Turning your back on you, he gives his soldiers the order to execute you.

Having defeated Lharond, you decide to perform a quick search of his office. Among various paperworks, you find two letters of interest. The first letter reads: "Greetings Lharond; Our plans to cast doubt or discredit the Lord Paladine are going ...

well: Vineyards are slowly rotting, trolls are roaming outside of the city, and the people are scared. I do have some concerns about your slowlyness at taking care of those meddlesome adventurers; the Overlords are also dubious about your efficiency ...

in taking over Sparklestone, since you are a few months behind schedule. I urge you to correct this state of affairs, if you know what's best for you; don't make me regret proposing you to perform this part of the Overlords' Plan. Signed: G.T.".

The second letter reads: "Greetings, Lharond; I am replying to your request for me to send knights to Sparklestone in order to take over the town. You know that is impossible, especially as long as the current Lord Paladine is in power, and as long ...

as too many loyal knights remain at commanding positions within my Order. Weeding them out is a slow process, since we must be careful as to not attract undue attention. Please refrain from making any more requests of the like to me. Signed: S.F.".

Looks like you have uncovered more players in the Overlords' conspiracy! After carefully folding these incriminating letters, you then spot a small chest: opening it, you also find a few valuables for your troubles!
Finding nothing more of interest, you leave Lharond's estate.

Having defeated Lharond, you decide to perform a quick search of his office. There, you find Runelore Magius lying on the floor, unconscious. After waking him, he proceeds to tell you what happened to him: "I heard the mine cave in, so I ...

confronted Lharond and his guards; but alone, I could not prevail. He forced me to drink a sleeping potion to keep me prisoner; I started drifting away when I heard that you had made it back! I'm so glad to see you, my friends!"

Searching further Lharond's office, you find nothing interesting save for business paperwork. It then strikes you how Lharond was disorganized: indeed, his desk is a mess of paperwork lying around and about! You guess he was not cut out to be a good ...
book-keeper! Along with Runelore, you finally leave the estate.
Lharond's estate is boarded shut. The bronze plaque has been replaced with a wood sign: "Closed until bought by new owners".

This estate is surrounded by a barbed wire fence. A silver plaque reads: Sparklestone Mining and Smeltering Company. You notice a few guards patrolling the estate's yards. One of them walks up to you: "No one without proper business is allowed".

This estate is surrounded by a barbed wire fence. A silver plaque reads: "Sparklestone Mining and Smeltering Company". A few guards patrol the yards. One of them walks up to you: "Say! Aren't ye the guys who did Akkar Dhun in?" Unsure what to answer ...

you remain silent. "Sure ye are!", exclaims the guard. "Come! My boss wants to talk with ye!" You are then brought within a humble office, full of paperwork and files. Behind a maplewood desk, a middle-aged man is busy reading accounting sheets.

"So, you're the so-called heroes who caused Dhun's demise, eh?" the man snarls, still sitting behind his desk. "I'm Cheron Ironseed, owner of this company. I have enough problems with my caravans being raided by marauders and dragons, or with ...

haunted mines. I'm warning you as one of the two Lords of Sparklestone: stay out of my business and don't cause trouble in my town!". With an impatient gesture, he orders his guards to promptly escort you out of his estate.
You are back at Cheron Ironseed's estate. A guard walks up to you: "Lord Ironseed wants ye to leave here ... and our town as well, while ye're at it!"

Cheron Ironseed is at the gate of his estate, with numerous of his guards. "I heard what you did to my competitor Lharond Dragonspurr. While I can't say I'm sorry about his loss, I've to remain true to Sparklestone: so, you either get out of my town ...
or I make you get out! I did warn you about making trouble here!"
Without word, you are promptly escorted out of the town. "And don't come back!" a guard tells you before closing the gate.
"You've made your choice, then!" snarls the remaining Lord of Sparklestone. His guards immediately attack!
Now Cheron Ironseed, along with his remaining guards, join the fray!
"Your arrogance is without bounds! You've made your choice, then!", snarls Cheron. His guards immediately attack!

Cheron is obviously taken aback by your revelations concerning his competitor. "I knew he was scum, but I had no idea!", he says. "It explains a lot of things now; like the raids on my caravans more often than on his own caravans, or even those dragons."

Cheron sighs: "It appears that I have greatly misjudged and wronged you, noble ones. I would ask you to help Sparklestone one last time, but I'll understand if you refuse because of my lack of trust and good judgement ..."

"That changes things a bit", replies Cheron. "I knew he was scum, but never thought he could resort to murder. However, I'm still suspicious of self-styled adventurers like you. Perhaps, if you performed a deed for Sparklestone, I would be convinced ...

of your true characters. So, this is what I propose: our caravans are often raided by green dragons. I have learned that they lair within a cave complex just south-west of here. So I ask you to rid us of those dragons."
Numerous guards block your way: "By orders of Cheron Ironseed, sole Lord of Sparklestone, you are no more welcome here!"

Overwhelmed, you are finally made prisoners. "Adventurers!", fumes Cheron. "People like you need to learn that you have no right to do as you please!" He then turns to his captain of the guards: "Strip them of all equipment and moneys, then throw ...
them out!"  You protest and attempt to resist as much as you can, but to no avail.
After the battle, you search Cheron's estate but find nothing of value. Frustrated, you leave.

Feeling magnaminous, you urge Cheron to tell you about this other problem: "You are noble ones indeed!" replies Cheron, visibly with relief. "Our caravans are being raided regularly by green dragons; we have learned that they lair in a cavern complex ...

just south-west of here. I ask you, brave adventurers, to rid us of those green dragons; of course, I will compensate you generously!" Accepting this challenging task, you get on your way. "Good luck!", shouts Cheron, his voice filled with hope.

You then tell Cheron that you have already dealt with the dragons. One or two may still be around, but they shouldn't bother the caravans anymore. "By the Gods!" exclaims Cheron with relief. "Thank you very much! Please, accept this reward!"
You then leave, along with Cheron's best wishes.
Cheron sighs: "It appears that I have greatly misjudged and wronged you, noble ones. Please accept my apology". Feeling gracious, you accept it then go about your way, with Cheron's best wishes.
Cheron nods in approval: "Very well. I wish you good luck!", he says, his voiced filled with hope. You then set out on this new adventure.
The traffic to Sparklestone is still as busy as usual; however you notice the lack of guards at the gates ...

You overhear a conversation between soldiers of Lantharond: "Things're bad" one mumbles, "with them treacherous amazons having broken the peace, and them cowards in Tanirith not living up to their part of the alliance". Another one nods: "Aye".
Cheron's estate is abandoned; you notice obvious signs that the place has been looted by passerbyes.
One of Cheron's guards runs up to you: "How goes your task?" You tell him that you are still working on it, then leave.
Cheron has been waiting for you: "By the Gods, you've done it!" he exclaims, obviously impressed. With happiness, he hands you a chest containing your reward.
"Greetings!", a guard tells you at your approach. "Lord Ironseed is busy, but he gives ye his best!"  You nod, then go on about your way.
"Hah!", exclaims Cheron. "I knew you were frauds!" Without further due, you are promptly escorted out of Sparklestone.
The sign on the door reads: "The Smelter's Den".  What do you want to do?
The place is busy, being filled with patrons. Looks like this is the miners' drinking place in Sparklestone!
He pockets the money: "One of ta mines has been shut down. Some say it's haunted by angry spirits; others say it's a ploy from one of Sparklestone's Lords to make ta other loose money".

He pockets the money: "Sparklestone has two lords, each owner of his own mining company. One's Cheron Ironseed, who owns Sparklestone Mining and Smeltering. Ta other's Lharond Dragonspurr, a late comer, who owns Bloodstone Heights Mining and Trading."

He pockets the money: "Cheron Ironseed used to be ta sole Lord of our town; then five years ago came Lharond Dragonspurr, who opened his own company and, according to our by-laws, became co-Lord with Cheron. Ironseed has been fuming ever since".

Pocketing the money, he leans toward you to whisper: "I've heard that one of our two Lords could be linked ta those caravan raids; it's said that he made a deal with them green dragons that have been attacking lately!"
A lady behind a desk smiles warmly at you: "Greetings! Would you like to stay for the night?"
"That will be 10 golds each."  Who will pay?
You come upon a bunch of though-looking, drunken miners. One of them looks at you: "Hey! Why don't ye pay a round of mead fer us nice miners!"  His friends chuckle at that.
"Whot do ye mean, ye have no money???", yells the wench. "Well get out of here and don't come back!"  You are then thrown out as the other patrons laugh out loud.
"Get out, ya moneyless bums!"

The place is loud and quite rowdy! Just as you're coming in, you see a fight break out between a couple of drunken miners. Surprisingly, no militia comes to stop this, or take the brawlers for a quiet night in jail. Sparklestone may not be lawless ...
but is does feel like a typical frontier town!
You find a few gems in this pile of uncollected ore.
From the ceiling, hungry spiders fall upon you!
More spiders attack!
Hungry centipedes fall on your head!
You run into a pack of cave lizards on the hunt!
You have disturbed some very hungry rats!
You find yourselves at the mouth of a small, quiet cave in which you think you could rest safely.
You leave the safe cave.
You find the remains of an unfortunate miner. He must have died weeks ago; however, you notice that most of his bones have been picked clean! You wonder with dread what could have done this ...
A group of troglodytes surprise you and attack!
More troglodytes join the fray!!!
Because of your alertness, you spot a group of troglodytes lying in wait down this corridor.
You surprise the troglodytes!
This cave is empty.
It appears that a tribe of troglodytes have made this cavern complex their home since the mine was shut-down ...
Troglodytes have made this cave their home. Upon seeing you, they attack!
From all accounts, this looks like the cave of the troglodyte tribe chief. And HE's not happy with your intrusion!
Searching the tribe chief's cave, you find a few valuables. Obviously, these were abandoned items throughout the mine which had been picked up and given to him by his subjects.
You have disturbed some slimes!!!
You are attacked by slimes!
This section of the mine is unfinished; you cannot go further.
You come upon a mine shaft which is leading down. You notice that the ladder normally used is missing; looking down in the shaft, you cannot make out how far down the shaft goes.
Who will go?

Your chosen member attempts to climb down the shaft, using protruding rocks and depressions. However, it does not take long to hear rocks fall, followed by your comrade's death scream, then followed by a distant thud.
Using the rope, each of you manages to climb down the dark shaft.
With the help of your spell, you easily hover down the mine shaft.
Do you climb up the shaft?
Do you climb down the shaft?
With the help of your spell, you easily climb up the mine shaft.
You notice a draft of fresh air coming from cracks and small depressions within the cavern wall.
You hack away at the cavern wall with your weapons as best as you can, but you soon realize that it's a futile effort; besides, you may damage your weapons in the process.
Using the iron spikes, you hack away at the cavern walls. After hours of hard and sweaty work, the wall finally falls, revealing a tight tunnel leading to the surface in which you can crawl!!!
However, once you get out of the tunnel, it collapses upon itself! Lucky for you that you were quick enough with your crawling!
With the help of your spell, you easily open the cavern wall, revealing a tight tunnel leading to the surface which you can crawl into!
A mine shaft goes up, but there is no ladder to be found.
You find a few mining tools abandoned beside this pile of uncollected ore.
You notice suddenly that some of your food rations are missing!!! Scurying rats must have taken them the last time you were resting!
"Git outa here, ye bums!", yells a guard. You notice that he, along with his collegues, look somewhat unkept and dirty. Do you try to force your way past the gates?
"We're being attacked!!!" yells the guard, as others come to join him. You then notice that these are not guards at all, but thugs, marauders, and rogues.
More rogues and marauders join the fray!
Wisely, you walk away.
Just as you approach this compound, its huge metal doors are shut and locked. You are then fired upon from arrowslits in the doors and nearby windows!
Who will try?
It was a valiant effort, but all it did was to hurt your party member ... You realize that those doors must be quite thick and reinforced!
More arrows rain on you!
You have managed to unlock the metal doors!!! You then rush into the compound to face the marauders!
You have failed. Now what?
The only response you get is laughter on the marauders' part ... and more of their arrows!
Wisely, you choose the better part of valor.
Just as the battle ends, you hear doors closing and being locked.
You are greeted with arrows!
This door is ajar.
This door is closed, but not locked.
Obviously, this is a weapon storage room. While the weapons displayed look in good shape, there is nothing in particular that catches your eye.
Obviously, this is a kitchen.
You find a metal door cleverly disguised as part of the wall!
The trap appears to be small arrows shot through tiny holes. A web-like array of silk treads, barely noticeable to the eye, is the obvious trigger. What do you want to do?
You trigger the trap!!!
You are ambushed by marauders!
You find a concealed trap door on the floor!
From behind the door, you hear numerous loud voices talking and laughing.  Do you open the door?
Opening the door, you see a large group of marauders eating and drinking. In unisson, they stop talking upon your entrance, gawking at you in disbelief.
From the far left, you hear a man shout: "Well don't just sit there, you fools! Dispatch those intruders!!!"  The marauders and thieves then jump from their seats and attack!
Opening it, it reveals a ladder going down. Without further due, you climb it down.

You find that one of the tombstones in this cemetary is hooked on a sliding mechanism, and thus can be pushed aside. When you do so, it reveals a small tunnel going underground. Do you go into the tunnel?
Unexpectedly, you come face to face with a group of marauders!
To your complete surprise, the floor underneath you opens to a deep pit full of iron spikes!!!
You can do naught but fall to your deaths!
A good thing that your spell is still in effect!
The floor-trap then suddenly closes on its own.

As you open the door, you see a man that can be none other than Doran Ghall, standing proudly and sternly, while being surrounded protectively by his retinue. "I was wondering when you would show up!", he snarls. "I don't know who you are, but ...

you are in quite the trouble now! Since I'm a man known for his generosity, I offer you the chance to surrender; do so and your lives will be spared".  You notice his lieutenant, probably the Guild Master, snickering. Do you surrender?
"So be it!" replies Doran Ghall. At the snap of his fingers, his marauders attack. You also notice that more of them are coming from behind you!

"Wise choice, strangers", replies the Rogue Lord. "Now, drop your weapons to show you mean it ", he then demands. After you complied, Doran Ghall, his lieutenant, and his retinue, start laughing at you. "Fools", muses the Rogue Lord, just before his ...
men drop upon you with their weapons.
"So that you know", snarls Doran Ghall, "I didn't become a Lord by merely standing on the sidelines!" Doran then jumps into the fray, along with his Guild Master and the rest of his retinue!
You then notice on Doran's and the Guild master's bodies intriguing sets of keys.
And a good thing you changed your minds, since you would have never noticed an intriguing set of keys on Zaran's body!
Too late, you notice that you have somehow lost Zaran's key. Figuring that you don't really need it for anything, anymore, you shrug off the matter and go on your way.
The compound is deserted, and looks to have been looted by the local populace not so long ago.
This is Lord Ghall's bedroom.
This is a dormitory of some kind. Numerous marauders sleep here; in fact, a few of them are lying cozily in their cots. Seeing you, they jump up and attack!
You stumble into some sort of council room.  Those already present are not happy by your intrusion!
You feel a very strong dweomer on this iron door.
You also notice that the door has a very special, if not weird, key hole; you are certain you do not have the appropriate set of keys to open it.
Using the Guild Master's brass keys, you manage to open the door, its magical dweomer shimmering away in the process.
You then find yourselves in what can only be the marauder's storage room for all the loot they have stolen from their trade caravan raids!
As you open the door, a group of marauders, obviously on watch here, get up from their chairs and attack the intruders that you are!
You enter what appears to be a private study.
You enter in what can only be the private quarters of the Thief Guild Master.
While searching, you notice a concealed trap door on the floor, just under the bed. Opening it, you find the Guild Master's secret stash!
The floor here is nothing but a series of huge, gaping holes which appear to go down very deep!
You realize that you are hopelessly trapped!
You teleport yourselves safely outside of this place.
The exit to this tunnel has been made to collapse; it is now hopelessly blocked.
You find some tombstones which have been removed; in their place you see evidence of a tunnel entrance which has been filled with rocks, dirt, and soil.
You phase yourselves to the end of the corridor.

On this table, you find charts and schedules of planned departures of trade caravans from Sparklestone, Aranys, Wailsrond, and Tanirith. It seems that these marauders were quite well informed, and quite studious in the preparation of their raids.
You are convinced that the marauders must have some sort of spy network within their target cities, to supply them with such complete and accurate information.
Do you pull that lever?
Well!  It looks like you can now walk through this corridor!
With Ghall's skeleton key, you easily open this door: you find yourselves in what can only be the Rogue Lord's secret treasure room!
The floor sections have retracted back!
A few maps also catch your attention.

You find an interesting map attached to a letter and a note. The note reads: "This is for your safekeeping, a little something A.D. forwarded to me; it may come in handy should our associate of Coral Towers loose his hold on power. Signed: D.G."

The letter reads: "Here is a map of Coral Towers marking the location of the passage underneath the cliffs which leads to the Queen's cell. I do not know why the Overlords want this, but here it is nonetheless. Signed: T.R.".
You carefully fold the map for your own safekeeping.

You find a map attached to a letter. The letter reads: "Dear Doran; here is a map of Nurale's Isles, with a secret passage known only to her, her Pirate Lords, and now to us. This passage will be useful for secret meetings and the likes. Signed: A.D."

You also find a strange written story entitled "My True Loves": "When I think of my true loves, I always think of my second one first, for her joy and warmth lifted me up; but then I had to leave her and forget her, because of life's insistances ...

This brings me to my very first, who brought  my heart and spirit low due to her vanity. From her I met my third love, who did the same to me; yet fate brought me back to my first so I could lift her heart and soul as a lesson for what she had done ...

to me. Feeling good about myself, I went away to do the same to my third. How convoluted life is; and yet all of that paved the true way to the needs of my heart."  You wonder how Doran Ghall could enjoy such incomprehensible rubbish!
A bunch of thugs rush up to you, their weapons drawn: "It's them!!!", yells one of the thugs, "Let's do them once and for all!"
You wonder what was this attack about. You also realize that no one is making a fuss about it; there is not even a militia patrol to be seen.

This huge cavern looks empty, except for animal bones littering its floor here and there. Just as you notice that the cavern goes further into the mountain through a corridor, a huge shape happens to come up to you from that direction.
Only too late you realize that the huge shape is a green dragon; and it is none too happy to see you! "Intruders, eh?", chimes the dragon out loud. "We'll see about that!"
Do you go down the corridor?
Do you go back?
You find a map on one of the orcs!
You stumble upon a group of trolls who have taken residence in this cave!
Searching the cave, you find some items of interest.
Suddenly, the ground gives away underneath your feet, and you fall to your deaths into a deep pit!
Your alertness allows you to notice that the ground looks somewhat weak here; any weight could make it break open into a pit or the like, Deftly, you bypass it and continue on your way.

Just as you walk upon this area, you notice that the ground is rather fragile, looking as if any weight could break it, opening a chasm of some sort. Luckily, your spell allows you to continue on without causing any disturbance.
Opening the huge door, you find yourselves face to face with a group of green dragons, apparently resting and relaxing amidst a humid mushroom forest!
Opening this huge door, you come face to face with another group of green dragons; obviously, you have stumbled upon the main lair of these foul beasts!
You have found the hoard of the green dragons!

You find people kept in a make-shift prison, behind a high barbed-wire fence. Most likely, they were kept here by the dragons like chickens and ducks for future meals. From these poor folks, a proud dwarven warrior walks up to you:

"Our thanks, brave ones. We've been prisoners fer days now. The dragons already ate a dozen of us; and we had to watch them do it! I wish I could've been able to give ye a hand in killing these foul beasts!"
As the other prisoners run out of the cavern to their freedom, the dwarf shakes your hands warmly: "I'm Braggan Stoneheart, a warrior of the Dwarven Halls".

"I've been in these lands fer a few weeks now, trying to find good and brave folks to come to the Dwarven Halls and help us against the war with the orcs, and their allies. I'm also trying to find the Shield of Galduur, an item which belonged ...
to a great hero of ours; his shield would be a symbol of hope fer me people, and hope would sure help us in this ugly, hopeless war!"
Do you offer Braggan to help him and his people?

"Me thanks, brave and noble ones!", exclaims the proud dwarf. "Let us go forth to find this hero's shield, and then off we go to the Halls to win this bloody war!" You can't help but be infected by his enthousiasm!
Braggan Stoneheart has been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.
Braggan gapes at your shield: "By Moradin and the Holy Forge!", he exclaims. "Ye have it! Please! Come with me to the Halls now: we need to show it to me King and me kinfolk!"  Do you accept?
"Me thanks, brave and noble ones!", exclaims Braggan in relief. "Let's refresh our strength, then off we march to the Dwarven Halls!". You can't help but being infected by his enthousiasm!

Runelore then whispers to you: "I mistrust this one: his story is too far fetched and convenient. A simple shield winning a terrible war with impossible odds? Please! Does he think us fools? Correct me if I'm wrong, but don't we have more pressing ...
matters to deal with?"  He then shrugs, awaiting your decision. Do you reconsider?
"I did hope ...", mumbles Braggan, visibly disapointed. Without a word, he then gathers his gear and goes away.

"Ye can't refuse!", shouts the proud dwarf. "Decent folks are dying! How can ye let that go by?" He is now visibly outraged by your attitude: "I'm sorry, but I'll pry that shield from ye even if I die trying: too much is at stake!" He then attacks!
Upon his dying breath, Braggan curses at you: "May yer indifference and callousness be yer doom!"  You hope that dwarven curses are not as bad as the tales make them out to be ...

Naryl whispers to you: "Maybe we should reconsider this. I do have a strong hunch that the troubles of the Dwarven Halls are the Overlords' doing; if the fall of the Halls is part of their plans, then shouldn't we help the dwarves ?"

"I, too, must leave" announces Naryl, with obvious sadness and disapointment in her voice. "I thought we had the same goals, but it appears that I was mistaken. Fare you well; Gods willing, we may meet again." She then walks away alongside Braggan.

"HOW COULD YOU???", screams Naryl as she runs to the dying Braggan. "Evil is killing these lands, and you make yourselves accomplices of that with your foolishness!", she snarls, tears falling on her flushed cheeks. She then bandages the fallen dwarf ...
as much as she can. You also notice some faint light coming out of her hands whenever she touches Braggan, each time healing some of his wounds! Once she is done, she picks up the noble Braggan.

"You are selfish fools and I pity you!", she then tells you with utter contempt in her voice. "I take my leave of you, for I have to stop the Overlords, even if by myself alone!" Without a word, she walks away with an unconscious Braggan in her arms.
For a while, you stand there in silence, feeling deeply ashamed of yourselves.
"Praise Moradin!", exclaims Braggan. "Now that we have Galduur's shield, let's go to the Halls! I know secret passages and the likes to get there: we won't be bothered!"

With a determined nod, you all set off north through the Khanark Rockies.  After a journey of about two weeks in the treacherous mountains, you finally arrive near "Stone Gate", a fortification protecting the secret passage to the Dwarven Halls.
The sign here points to the east for Arvoranaan, and to the south for Tanirith.
This sign post reads: "Creek Dale-Trade Caravan Waystation".  Also, the sign points to the north for Lantharond, and to the south for Arvoranaan and Tanirith.
This cave appears to be empty. Its walls and floor are thick with ice; you also notice huge icicles hanging from the ceiling. In any case, the temperature in there is freezing!

You find an entrance to a tunnel, at the back of the cave, which is rendered practically invisible by being covered with a thick layer of ice. Breaking this ice with your weapons, you enter the tunnel.
You soon arrive to a huge cave, also covered thick with ice and icicles. Suddenly, out of nowhere, snow yetis jump on you!

"WHO DARES DISTURB MY SLEEP?" shouts a deep, booming voice. From within a large dome of ice in the center of the cavern, two huge blue orbs look at you angrily. You realize that you are facing Icingbreath, the great ice dragon!
Seizing the opportunity that Icingbreath appears to be imprisoned in ice, do you launch yourselves on the attack?
To your complete astonishment, Icingbreath manages to break himself free of his shell of ice, apparently ready for your attack! At the same time, more of his snow yeti servants show up by his side!

Without a word, Icingbreath shows why he has come to be called by this nickname, by breathing freezing air of snow and hail on you! Looks like you failed to notice two openings in the ice shell right beneath his eyes and aligned with his snout!

Then with incredible ease, the ice dragon brushes away the ice shell covering him, and launches himself on the intruders that you are! At the same time, more of his snow yeti servants join him to help!
After this battle, you notice Icingbreath's hoard lying beneath a thick layer of ice. Breaking through with your weapons, you can claim his hoard for your own!
"We're almost here!", exclaims Braggan, as he opens a concealed door leading to a secret passage. You go on following him.
You leave the secret passage.
You stumble upon a group of giant trolls who have taken up residence in this cave!

The floor of this large cave is littered with charred remains of animals and humanoids. The air about the cave appears to be charged with electricity; you feel your hair raising with electrostatics. Do you investigate further down this cavern?
Streams of lightning assault you, obviously coming from the end of the cavern. Immediately after this attack, you see the source of this lightning coming toward you: a small group of blue dragons!
In the far end of the cavern, you find the dragons' hoard.
You stumble upon a big battle between gnomes and an alliance of ogres and orcs. Obviously, the gnomes are defending the gates of their village. Do you rush in to help the gnomes?
With your best battle cry, you join the fray!
You start to turn away when some of the orcs spot you and rush to you for the attack! Before you realize it, you get fully involved in this battle!

After the battle, one of the gnome warriors walk up to you: "Our thanks, strangers! We've been having dire problems with them orcs and ogres ... Please, go to our King's castle and speak with him; he will give ye the details of it". The gnome then ...
goes back to helping his kin with the wounded and the dead.
Gnome warriors nod at you respectfully and let you pass. "Welcome to Gnomilar", one of them tells you.
Gnome warriors on watch nod at you.
This looks like Gnomilar's general store. Do you enter?
This looks like a magic shop. Do you enter?
A sign reads: "Lharod's Gems and Precious Stones Exchange". Do you enter?
"Welcome!" an old gnome exclaims in greeting. "What do ye wish to exchange: money? Gems? Or both?"

This is an marble obelisk of some sort. From its markings and the gems encrusted into it, this must be a monument dedicated to Woralduur, God of the Earth and Underearth. At the base of the obelisk, you notice an alcove that is empty.
You are in Gnomilar's mining area. Numerous gnomes go in and out of the mines, pushing wagons filled with ore and gems.

You cross paths with a gnome miner. He nods politely at you. "Beautiful day" he says, smiling. "Too bad days like this are numbered fer us; without our Lamp, Woralduur cain't protect us". He then goes about his way.

You cross paths with a gnome warrior. "Thanks again fer yer help", he tells you in greeting. "I'm afraid that we won't be able to hold out fer long, especially since our Lamp was stolen from us". He then goes about his way.

You cross paths with a gnome mother going to the general store with her children. "Greetings" she says, smiling. "I hear the dwarves are also besieged, like us. We would help, but without our Lamp, Gnomilar cain't be left unprotected". She then goes.
You stumble upon the body of a fallen gnome warrior. Although he has been striped of his gear, you find a crumpled map underneath his torn shirt.
"Alert! We're under attack!!!", yells a gnome warrior. Do you help the gnomes defend their village?
After the battle, a gnome warrior walks up to you: "Our thanks again, good strangers! Without our Lamp, I just don't know how long we'll be able to hold on to Gnomilar". The gnome then ...

"Halt!" shouts a guard at the gate. You notice numerous other guards watching you.  You do not recognize their crest; they are certainly not the same kind of guards that you had seen previously in Aranys!

The guard goes on: "By order of our Warlord, Aranys is now under the protection and tutelage of Sharranth since the unfortunate death of Lord Dhun at the hands of lawless adventurers. Accordingly, adventurers such as you are no more ...
welcome here, just as adventurers are already not welcome in Sharranth!"  Faced with scores of knocked arrows and determined soldiers, you walk away.

You notice that knights of the Flame from Tanirith are guarding and policing Sparklestone. Considering that you were responsible for Cheron's demise, you decide it would be best just to leave the town and avoid further trouble.
You are surprised to find no guards at the gates of Dagger Keep.
Guards from Wailsrond's militia are now guarding the gates of Dagger Keep.
You notice numerous guards from Wailsrond watching the gates of Dagger Keep's compound. Looks like the town has been annexed by Wailsrond, and most likely for the better of it.
Dagger Keep's general store is now fully opened for business. Do you enter?
You find a dead orc warrior. Although his gear has been striped away, you notice a crumbled map underneath his torn shirt.
You see knights of the Flame engaged in a battle with what seems like cavalry troopers. Do you help the knights?
You start to turn away, but too late: one of the troopers sees you! In no time, you get involved in the battle alongside the knights of the Flame!

After the battle, the knight commander rides up to you: "Our thanks! I don't understand why the troopers of Lantharond attacked us! Tanirith and this city are supposed to be allies! I guess the rumors about their Lord turning an evil leaf are true ..."
After a warm handshake, the knights ride back to Tanirith in order to report on this grave, and disturbing, incident.

Cavalry troopers from Lantharond ride fast in your direction. "Halt!", shouts their leader. "We are at war with Tanirith: no one is allowed from this foul city into our territories! Turn back or face the consequences!"  Do you turn back?
As you peacefully turn back on your tracks, the troopers attack nonetheless!
"So be it!" snarls the leader, as his troopers charge you!

The Caravan Master rides up to you after the battle: "Well fought, strangers! We're a caravan from Tanirith; I don't understand why troopers from Lantharond attacked us! They claimed to be at war with us, but we are supposed to be allies!"
Confused, he orders his caravan to go back to Tanirith in order to report on this disturbing incident.
You spot in the distance a group of Lantharond cavalry troopers riding in your direction.
Lying in the woods, you wait patiently for the troopers to pass near you, then make the jump on them!

Upon his last breath, the Cavalry Leader looks at you in disbelief: "Why?" he asks in a whisper, just before passing away.  You are left with a strange taste in your mouths, as grave doubts about your actions arise in your minds.

Hiding in the woods, you watch the troopers ride by you unnoticed. Suddenly, a larger group of Lantharond troopers comes out of nowhere and attacks the first group! Only then you notice something strange about that second group:

Although their uniforms are the same, they appear less clean and less fitting. You also notice that the riders of that second group appear less disciplined and organized than those of the first group. Do you help one of the group against the other?

The battle is savage, but brief, as the larger second group cruelly dispatches the unsuspecting troopers of the first group. Unexpectedly, one of the remaining riders spots you: suddenly, it is your turn to defend yourselves!
Which group do you help?
First.
Second.

After the battle, the leader of the first group comes up to you: "Our thanks, strangers! We were going to Tanirith to ask for help, since the amazons broke peace with us for no reason and are waging war against us". He then looks at the dead attackers.

"For the life of me, I have no idea who these impostors are, and why they attacked us!"  You tell him that these impostors are attacking knights of the Flame and spread false word that Lantharond is at war with Tanirith. "What?", exclaims the leader.

"As if the amazons were not enough!", he adds, with desperation in his voice. "We have to go back and appraise our King of this dire development; thank you for telling us this!". Turning away, he and his men ride back with haste to Lantharond.
After the battle, the leader rides up to you: "Thank you, but we did not need your help, fools!"  Unexpectedly, he and his men attack you!
You are begining to think that you made the wrong choice ... Which group, then, was the real cavalry detachment from Lantharond?

The leader rides up to you: "Greetings, strangers! If you are thinking of going to Lantharond, I advise you not to -- ..."  Suddenly, another group of riders comes out of nowhere and attack the first group! You notice something about the second group:
The sign-post here reads: "Crescent Lake".

You stumble upon a detachment of fallen Lantharond cavalry troopers. They appear to have been involved in a fierce battle and lost. All of them are dead, except for their leader who is down to his last breath of life. "Why?", he whispers to you.
"Why have the amazons broken peace and now wage war with us? Why do they call us betrayers and butchers?" He then passes away.
"Why did knights of the Flame attacked us? Are we not allies? Why did they call us betrayers and butchers?"  He then passes away.
You see a detachment of cavalry troopers from Lantharond engaged in a battle with what can only be amazon warriors.  Do you help the troopers?

After the battle, the cavalry leader comes up to you: "Well fought, strangers! We need all the help we can get against those savage warriors!" He and his tired men then slowly ride back to Lantharond.

As you near Lantharond, you come upon a fierce and bloody battle between riders and soldiers of the city, and a large contingent of amazon warriors.  Looks like the amazons are undertaking a major assault on Lantharond itself! Do you help the defenders?

After the battle, priests and helpers come out of the city to tend the wounded. Standing within all that chaos, along with the cries of the wounded and dying, no one has even noticed you or your participation in the defense of the city.
Amazon warriors ambush you!
You stumble face to face with an amazon patrol!
You stumble face to face with an amazon patrol; fortunately, Scyrella is there: upon seeing her, the other amazons bow respectfully to her, then let you go about your way.
You stumble upon a battle between amazons and cavalry troopers of Lantharond. Which group to you help?
Troopers.
Amazons.
"We must help my sisters!", exclaims Scyrella with fervor. You can't help but think that she is actually glad for the opportunity to test her fighting skills once again.
After the battle, Scyrella proudly claps arms with her surviving sisters, then motions to you to get on the way again. She's a real princess and leader indeed!
After the battle, a beautiful and proud amazon walks up to you: "Well fought, strangers", she acknowledges politely, "but why did you help us?" She appears very suspicious of your motives.
You explain to her what you found about impostors posing as Lantharond troopers to cause stryfe between the city and her people.

"I would believe you if you had proof. We will leave you be, since you helped us; but you better get out of our forest. This is your first and last warning!" She then regally walks away with her amazon sisters, who seem to view her as royalty.

To convince her of your conspiracy story, you show the letter you found in the compound of the impostors. "By Barask!" she exclaims. "You speak the truth! What fools we have been! We must show this to my Queen!" You nod in agreement.
Scyrella Silverspear has been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.

"We leave now", orders Scyrella. "Our village is at the south-east end of this valley". As the other amazons leave to continue their patrol of the forest, you march on to the amazon village with Scyrella at your side. You notice that Scyrella's ...
warrior-sisters appeared very defferential to her, as if she is some kind of royalty to them.
Numerous amazon guards, ready for war, shower you with spears!!!
Surprised at seeing Scyrella with you, the amazon guards bow respectfully to her and let you pass.
Scyrella then turns to you: "We now go to the Queen's house, at the far end of our village."

The Amazon Queen is already waiting for you outside her house, with her personal retinue of warrior-sisters. She does not look very happy. "What is this, Scyrella?" she demands. "You would bring strangers, if not enemies, into our haven?"

Having been told by Scyrella to remain silent in the presence of the Queen unless spoken to, you let your amazon friend speak: "These are no strangers, my Queen", exclaims Scyrella, "but friends who have uncovered our true enemies!" She then proceeds ...

to tell the Queen what you found out so far. For long moments after, the Queen ponders on what Scyrella has revealed. However, you notice all the while that the Queen is no less angry as she was at first: you begin to have a bad feeling about that.

You then notice that numerous amazons have also gathered around your party and Scyrella. "You are a fool, Scyrella!", snarls the Queen, "A princess you may be, and a heroine to our warrior-sisters, but you have still much to learn about ...

choosing the right allies. I damn you for forcing my hand so soon on this; but so be it!" The Queen then adresses all the amazons present: "My sisters! Scyrella has shown herself to be a traitor; as saddened as I am by this, we must make her pay!"

To Scyrella's horror (and yours as well), you see that a large majority of amazons agree with their Queen. "But my sisters!", yells Scyrella, "It is our Queen who has allowed rogue impostors to attack us, only to make us believe that the King ...

of Lantharond had betrayed the peace we had with his people! It is our Queen who has betrayed our honor and our nation!" The Queen then raises her weapon in a dramatic gesture: "Lies!!! Lies from a base traitor! Time to dispense our justice!!!"
Then the Queen, along with her retinue and a large number of amazons who believe her, attack you and Scyrella!
More amazons join their Queen!

You rush to the side of Scyrella after the battle. Numerous other amazons do the same. "My sisters", Scyrella whispers, lying near-death, "Our victory shows that we spoke the truth. War must end now ..." And then she passes away.

An amazon then steps forward: "Scyrella will get the heroine's funeral that she most rightfully deserves. That will not be so for our treacherous Queen; she is almost dead as well, but she is near-death crazy". You look surprised by that announcement.

The amazon shrugs. "She keeps saying something like "They took my mind and made me do this"; I have no idea what she means by that. In any case, go to the King of Lantharond and tell him that we now know the truth, and will send our peace envoys."
With a solemn nod, you take your leave of the grieving amazons and set yourselves to go back to Lantharond.
Amazon warriors launch another raid on the city! Before you know it, you get involved in the battle!

Amazon guards stand watch at the gate of their village. One of them nods to you in recognition: "All is well as it could be, considering that we are still grieving for Scyrella", she tells you. Reassured by this statement, you leave.

"Your daughter and these folks speak the truth, Queen Moretta!" a man's voice booms in. Everyone turns to see who dared to intrude and speak thus: you are surprised to find Strider, with his faithful Whitefang at his side. He winks at you in recognition.

Strider then goes on:"I have been an honorable friend of the amazons for years, Queen Moretta. I also found out about this conspiracy and the treachery to your people; so I say this to you respectfully: fight the mind poisons in you and do what's right."

No one, including Scyrella, seems to know what Strider just meant by that. However, the Queen appears to struggle within herself; suddenly, she goes into a fit and attacks, along with a few amazons who have sided with her despite these revelations!
Strider and Whitefang have been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.

"A moment, my friends", Strider tells you. You see that he is carrying a badly wounded Whitefang. "I will leave my friend here with the amazons; I know they will heal her. As for me, I would now join you so that, together, we may finish these Overlords".

After leaving Whitefang in the care of the amazons, Strider gathers his gear and gets on his way, this time at your side. "Oh! And by the way", he then adds slyly, with a mischievous smile on his face, "I managed to find the location of the sanctum ...

sanctorum of the Overlords: they are hiding in the ruins of an old temple of Graaz'z, God of Evil and Power. Here's a map to a portal that is said to lead there!" As you look at the map with amazement, Strider adds: "But first, off to Lantharond!"

"A moment, friends", chimes in Strider. "I think it is time for us to join forces, in order to deal with these Overlords once and for all. But first, I would leave Whitefang behind for her own safety."

Runelore intercedes in the conversation: "I do not think this is a good idea; we know next to nothing of this man!" he says while pointing to Strider. "How can we trust him? Especially since these Overlords seem to be able to bend minds to their will!"
Do you follow Runelore's advice and refuse to take Strider into your ranks?

Strider appears genuinely surprised and disapointed. "I have heard of foolishness in times of trouble", he says quietly while slowly shaking his head, "but you have made your decision. Good luck then". Without further due, he goes ...

back to the amazon village. "I did not mean to cause any sour blood", adds Runelore in apology, "but I felt I had to speak my mind on this". After reassuring him that he did the right thing, you finally get on your way for Lantharond to see the King.

"Well", adds Runelore, "I didn't mean to cause any sour blood, but I felt I had to speak my mind. I will follow your decision of course, my friends". You look to Strider, who shrugs nonchalantly at that. However, you get the feeling that ...
he himself is quite suspicious of Runelore, which only complicates matters for you.

Just as you all finally get on the way, Runelore whispers to you a final warning: "I don't know, but I have this feeling that we may walk into a deadly trap if we go to that temple". He then drops the matter and goes on walking, brooding silently.

Naryl then intercedes: "Queen of the amazons", she chimes with conviction, "I implore you to believe us!" She then whispers in your ear: "I was afraid of this: I'm convinced that she is under the Overlords' mental thrall!"

After the battle, you join Scyrella who is standing at the side of the dying Queen: "Forgive me, mother", Scyrella whispers, tears in her eyes. The Queen smiles gently: "No worries, my daughter, for you have freed me of the Overlords' hold on my mind ...

and saved us all, including Lantharond, in the process. I love you always, my child ..." The Queen then passes away, as Scyrella breaks down and cries. After a few moments, she turns to you: "I will join you to hunt down those monsters!" she says,

with much anger. "If they could bend the will of my mother, then they can easily do the same to anyone and everyone. I swear that I will bring them down for the pain and suffering they have caused!" After making arrangement with her warrior-sisters ...

so that the Queen and those who died at her her side get the appropriate funerals that they nonetheless deserve, Scyrella leaves the village in the hands of the eldest amazon until her return, then joins you for the task of defeating the Overlords.
"Of course", she then adds, "We must first go to Lantharond to tell the good King that the war is over, and that my sisters will send their peace envoys".
You stumble upon a terrible battle where orcs, ogres and giants are assaulting a forteress being grimly and bravely defended by dwarves.
Do you help the dwarven defenders?
"This is it, me friends!" shouts Braggan. "Looks like we've arrived at Stone Gate just in time!" With a roar worthy of a demi-god, Braggan rushes out to help his kinsfolk.

After the battle, a dwarven warrior comes up to you: "Ye have our thanks, strangers. Stone Gate is ta trading post of our Dwarven Halls, ta way to which must remain secret ta non dwarf-kin. Them giants and orcs have been attacking us ta find that ...

secret passage or force us ta show it ta them." He then slowly shakes his head: "Blasted fools ... don't they know we'd rather die than tell them?" He then walks away to help his kin take care of the wounded and dying.
