"I agree with his sentiments" adds Naryl. "I helped you out of friendship, but because of the nature of our actions, this is now tainted. I'm sad to say that you do the Overlords' biding by being irresponsible and arrogant".
Without any other word, she also leaves.

"But I have a feeling that this lesson in humility will be fruitful for you, and make you realize that". She then looks over the gear that Jhalor left you. "He is a very noble and good man", she muses, "to have left you these; be thankful and let ...
his gift be an example of what is required, of what the world needs, to keep evil at bay".
"Why do you not free him?" Jhalor intercedes. You see in his look confusion and disapointment. Pushing you aside, he unchains the poor prisoner. The freed man is now quite jubilant.
"Why do you not free him?" intercedes Naryl, with a look of confusion. Pushing you aside, she unchains the poor prisoner. The freed man is now quite jubilant.
As you walk away, Jhalor stops you, a look of disgust clearly visible in his face: "How can you be so callous and uncaring?" he simply asks between clenched teeth, before leaving you.
As you walk away, Naryl stops you, a look of disgust clearly visible in her face: "How can you be so callous and uncaring?" she simply asks between clenched teeth, before leaving you.
As Jhalor walks away, you see Naryl stepping in front of you, the same look in her face as his. After a few moments of staring angrily each of you in the eye, she leaves you as well.
Here, you see a huge bronze plaque hanging above the door to this small building. The plaque, adorned with an etched sword, reads: "Adventurers Inc. - Home Office". Do you enter?

Numerous adventurers are seated in the entrance hall, waiting to be called to one of the six kiosks that are there. From behind the kiosks, you see different people going about with paperwork and files in their hands. Taking a number, you wait.
After about half an hour, your number is called. At the kiosk you are lead to, a woman greets you with a smile. "How may Adventurers Inc. be of service to you?"
"Come back any time", the woman replies, still smiling.
The woman promptly hands you a sheet of parchment: "Here is what we have available" she says.
"Very well" replies the woman. "The caravan Master will be waiting for you just outside the south-west gate of the city. You will be paid upon arrival".
"There ye are!" the caravan Master greets you. "We ride now! ALWAYS stay on ta road, ye hear?" You nod. The caravan then sets out.
"But you already have an assigned task" the lady replies. "We assign only one task at a time; please come back when you have completed your task. Thank you."  You then leave at that.
"We've arrived!" shouts the caravan Master. "A job well done by all!" He then gives you your pay.
"I'm sorry, but due to current troubles between our city and Lantharond, we have suspended our sponsoring of caravan escorts to that city".
"Very well", replies the woman. "The caravan Master will be waiting for you just outside the north-east gate of our city. You will be paid upon arrival".

"There ye are!" the caravan Master greets you. "We are ready to ride; you must always stay on the road: from here, we keep riding northward through Arvoranaan, then until we reach Lantharond!" You nod. The caravan then sets forth.
"Any information provided, regardless of quality and/or accuracy, requires a fee of 50 gold pieces", the lady tells you. Do you pay the fee?
"Another time, perhaps" the lady replies.
"Oh my!" exclaims the woman, "That has been resolved already! Maybe you should come back later until our paperwork is up to date". Resigned, you leave.

"Hey, youze guys!" a furfoot chimes, as he walks up to you. "Do ya think ya need an extra pair of hands? I'm very useful and good with my sword, dontcha know!" He smiles like a mischievous child. "I'm Daneel; I'm very much itching to git out of this ..
boring town. So? Whatcha say?" Do you take Daneel into your group?
"Excellent!" exclaims Daneel, quite happy to join you.
Daneel Nimblehands has been added to your party. Check out the Allies menu.
Daneel shrugs. "Too bad fer ya; it's yer loss, dontcha know!" he then walks away.
Jhalor intercedes: "My apologies, friends, but I don't think we should get involved with a troublesome furfoot". Do you reconsider?

You suddenly wake up, only to find that Daneel is gone!!! Where he was sleeping, you find this note: "See ya guys! Sorry if I ditch youze like that, but youze were way too boring fer me: youze don't know how ta have fun! I hope youze won't mind if I ...
helped myself to some of yer stuff: I cain't be on ta road by myself without food, gear, or money, dontcha know? Take care!" Sure enough, you find some of your valuables missing.

Jhalor grunts with frustration: "I knew that troublesome furfoot would pull a stunt like that; I should have watched him more closely to prevent this". You then reassure him, deep down blaming yourselves as well.

"Thieves!!!" a gnomish priest shouts, as he is grabbing Daneel Nimblehands' right arm. Sure enough, one of the encrusted gems of the obelisk falls from Daneel's hand under the grip of the priest. Caught red-handed, Daneel stammers as best as he can ...
a protest and tries to explain how the gem came to be in his hand, but to no avail. You are all thrown out forcibly of Gnomilar, along with a much more demure and embarassed Daneel.
"Yer not welcomed anymore in Gnomilar, ye thieves!" shouts a gnomish guard.

The guard then notices the lamp you found in the emerald dragon's hoard. "By Woralduur!" he exclaims, "Ye found the lamp! Come, go speak to our King!!!" You are then escorted to the Gnomish King's castle.

"You were told never to return here, thief!" shouts a guard. Initially surprised by this warning, you finally realize that it is directed at Daneel, who is doing his best to hide behind one of you. "You will not enter" the guard adds. Then ...
he turns to you with a stern look: "Neither will your no-good friends!"

You then look at a demure Daneel, who is visibly embarassed. "I wuz framed!!! It wuz not my fault, I tell ya!" he simply yells in frustration. He then starts brooding angrily. You want to ask him what trouble he got into here, but you drop the matter ...
at seeing his angry disposition.
You find a secret stash of food!
You find one or two weapons under the matress of this cot!

During the centuries since its foundation, Tanirith has undergone many changes and survived many disasters. Each time the city was rebuilt or expanded, it was done so on top of the previous buildings or structures. Hence, the sewers are the remains ...

of buried streets, canals, and buildings from previous incarnations of Tanirith. It is rumored that much treasures are to be found there, but that such hoards are guarded by  terrible monsters and fell creatures from the Abyss. The entrance ...
to the sewers is rumored to be under the Memorial Statue in the city park.

The Knights of the Flame is a knighthood order that was founded by Jasper Flameheart some five hundred years ago. Jasper was a great knight of virtue and nobility; his travails and good deeds are legendary here. All knights of the Flame have pledged ...

themselves to the service of Tanirith, to protect and defend its people, and to fight evil where ever they may find it. They are the defenders of the weak and a force for good. However, lately, things are not what they seem anymore with the knights.

Indeed, the knighthood has become lax, and is even bordering on not caring, about its duties to the city and the people. Numerous, good knights have left or been expulsed from the order, while too many of those staying on are less than chivalrous.
Many suspect this state of things has much to do with the current High Commander of the order, a man named Sardin Firestorm.

Tanirith was founded some seven hundred winters back, by the Warlord Ptaraz. At first a nearly-impregnable forteress, Tanirith grew as a town, then eventually became more or less the center of activities in the Sword Lands.

As any other city, Tanirith as lived through its share of despots, kings, and queens. However, for the last one hundred years, Tanirith has been ruled by a High Council, which is composed of the Lord Paladine (a former High Commander of the  ...

knighthood of the Flame) and Merchant Lords (usually the richest and most powerful ones). This form of government has proven to be quite efficient so far, and the people of Tanirith are quite content with it.
A snow storm breaks out, forcing you to lay camp for hours!!!
Once the storm has passed, you get on your way.
Wandering animals eye you as meals!
Mountain giants attack you!
Ice trolls are lairing here; upon your intrusion, they attack!
You have disturbed some strange, giant worms!
Suddenly, the hard snow and ice beneath your feet crack, opening to a deep chasm in which you fall!!!
A sudden avalanche falls on you!!!
Buried under ice and snow, you manage to slowly extricate yourselves free, but not without suffering damage from hypothermia and frostbite.
Lucky for you, your alertness allows you to escape from most of it, with only bruises, scratches and frost bites.
The winds in these parts of the Khanark Rockies blow hard, fast, and VERY cold!!!
The lava is too hot for you to get near it!
By the means of your spell, you transport yourselves on the other side of the lava crater.
Earthquake! A rockslide falls from the steep mountain cliffs upon your heads!!!
Large spiders attack!
You run into a band of fire giants!
Earthquake!!! The ground beneath your feet opens up to a deep chasm!!!
Lucky for you that your spell is still in effect, thus preventing you from falling to your deaths!
Earthquake!!! The ground opens into a fissure, thus releasing a powerful jet of hot, burning, acid gases!!!

As you come out of the tunnel after days of travel, you hear the ominous thundering of volcanic activity and ground quaking. The air is hot and thick with dust; smells of sulfur and acid assail your nostrils. Looks like you have reached a volcanic ...
area of the Khanark Rockies. Even now, you feel slight tremors under your feet: this region is likely to be very hazardous indeed!
You enter the tunnel, getting on your way back to the Lantharond area. In the distance, you still hear the ground shaking and some volcanic activity.

You enter a large tunnel seemingly carved out within the mountains. The walls are lined with bricks and mortar; obviously at least a millennium old, its constructors must have been quite advanced and determined!
You finally reach the end of the tunnel, finding yourselves back near Lantharond after days of travel.

You come upon a large crater filled with boiling lava. The temperature here is near impossible to live with, and so is the air. You feel that ground tremors are more intense; looks like you have reached a collapsed volcano.
The hot lava burns you!
The hot, toxic gases and acids burn you!
You disturb a colony of giant scorpions!!!
You have disturbed a nest of spiders!
You have disturbed a colony of snakes!
A band of fire giants lair here; they attack upon your approach!
You disturb a colony of centipedes!!!
You disturb a colony of beetles!
As you enter this cavern, you come face to face with a female red dragon! With a terrifying roar, she alerts her lair-mates and attacks you!
After having dealt with these red dragons, their hoard is yours for the taking!

With the accessways splitting up like this, you realize that this would separate or fragment any large invading army, therefore increasing the defense capabilities of the dwarves. Quite an ingenious way to defend their undercity! You also notice that ...
With the accessways converging like this after splitting up earlier, you realize that this would throw into chaos any invading army. The ingeniosity of the dwarves keep amazing you!
Dwarven warriors on watch scrutinize you as you pass the gates, but you are otherwise left unbothered.
This is one of the Living Halls of the undercity.
This is the Common Halls of the undercity; numerous dwarves are about.
These are the Forge Halls; the sounds of hammers hitting anvils, and flaring of fires, are quite evident of that!
These are the Craft Halls of the undercity.
These are the Smith's Halls of the undercity; the sounds of hammers hitting ores, and smeltering fires, attest well to that.
These are the War Halls of the undercity. You can hear the sounds of dwarven warriors practicing their skills at arms.
This is one of the common Dining Halls of the undercity. Many dwarves are about eating or having a drink.
This is the Feasting Hall, where all dwarves and their king celebrate special occasions and events. It is presently closed.
This is the Royal Hall. Dwarven warriors eye you severely as you pass, but you are otherwise left unbothered.
walls and/or stone slabs can be collapsed at a moment's notice, therefore effectively trapping anyone easily. The dwarves are very serious indeed about the defense of their Halls!
These are the Merchant Living Halls.

"Ye have come!" shouts gladly the dwarven merchant you had rescued from Akkar Dhun's dungeon. "I told ye that I would reward ye well, and I ain't no lying orc!" he adds with a wink. After rummaging somewhere in his house, he then comes out with ...
a small chest. smiling proudly. "There ye go!  I hope this pleases ye!"
After much heart-warming goodbyes and well-wishings, you leave the thankful dwarven merchant.
This is the display hall of the dwarven forgers' pieces of work; of course, all items are for sale. Do you enter?
This is a display hall of all the dwarven craftsmen's (leatherworkers, alchemists, artisans, brewers, etc.) workmanship; of course, they are for sale as well. Do you enter?
This is a display hall for all the stonecutters', jewelers', and smelters' pieces of work; of course, many things are for sale here. Do you enter?
You notice that this hall also houses a large central market used by the whole dwarven population. Do you enter the store to shop around?

You go at the side of the dying Naryl. "My friends", she whispers weakly, "Take the talisman that is hanging on my neck, for my mental essence will be residing within it. When you feel you need help or information about the Overlords, just hold it ...

in your hand and think of me: my essence will awake and I shall speak with you. Goodbye until then ..." Naryl then passes away. You then notice that the talisman she spoke about starts pulsating, as if suddenly alive. You take it as requested by Naryl.
This is the hall of the Master Forger. You see that he is quite busy at teaching others how to go about and perfect the craft.
This is the hall of the Master Stonecutter and Smelter. You see that he is quite busy at teaching others how to go about perfecting the craft.
This is the hall of the Master Crafter. He is quite busy at theaching others many crafts and how to go about perfecting them.

Holding her pulsating talisman and whispering her name, you then see in your minds the face of Naryl Dragonstone, smiling. "Greetings, my friends" her calm, telepathic voice projects in your thoughts, "How may I be of help?"

The lady opens the file: "As you may have heard, some of Tanirith's vineyards have begun rotting unexpectedly. Priests are baffled by this and have yet to identify the source of this phenomenon. Obviously, this is a ploy to sap away at Tanirith's ...

trading power and revenues, since the wine is a popular export product. Go to the vineyards, which are just north-west of the city: once there, find the source of this rotting and eradicate it." Accepting this far-reaching task, you leave.

The offices of Adventurers Inc. are as busy as ever. Lucky for you, you can go straight to the "Reward Claims" kiosk without waiting in line. There, a woman smiles warmly at you: "Congratulations for a job superbly done!" She then hands you the reward.
"Do you require more of our services?" the woman asks.

The lady opens the file: "Since the last month or so, unexplicable tensions have risen between Tanirith and Lantharond, a long-time ally and friend. Some suspect that the King of Lantharond has turned an evil leaf, while others lean toward a more ...

insidious cause. In any case, there are no more communications or relations between the two cities, and stories about Tanirith caravans or patrols of knights of the Flame being attacked by Lantharond's cavalry troopers are now emerging. Lantharond ...

lies on the same coast as Tanirith, but north of here. Go in this area, investigate what exactly is going on, and resolve the matter in anyway; whether it is by bringing down the King of Lantharond, or by finding a means to bring back the peace,
will be up to you and according to exactly what truly lies behind this situation." Accepting this far-reaching task, you leave.

The lady opens the file:"In the last three months or so, we've heard rumors about an emerging group known only so far as the "Cult of Lankharh". Who or what is Lankharh, we are not sure. What we do know is that they are hiding somewhere in the sewers ...

of Tanirith; that's what tells us that this cult must be up to no good. In fact, some think that there may even be some kind of connection between this cult and the rotting of Tanirith's vineyards. In any case, find this cult, investigate what it ...

is about and, if it is a threat, then feel free to eradicate it. Use the secret entrance to get to the sewers, which is underneath the memorial statue in the City Park."  Accepting this far-reaching task, you get on your way.

The woman opens the file: "Pyrokhalistyranellan, a.k.a. Pyrostorm, is a huge, mature, adult red dragon. For the last centuries, he has been a terror in the region, attacking caravans and even laying siege to cities for fealty. But some years ago ...

his activities unexplicably ceased. Our resident warlocks have learned through magics that the wyrm is still alive; therefore his death cannot explain his "disappearance". Many of us think that, instead, he has gone into a cycle of rest. We fear the ...

worst when he'll awake! Therefore, your mission is to kill Pyrostorm before he resumes his plundering and killing activities. All we know, is that his lair is somewhere near the collapsed volcano in the Khanark Rockies, far north of here. You can get ...

to this dangerous place through an age-old tunnel within the rockies; this tunnel lies just north-west of Lantharond, itself north of us along the coast. Good luck!"  With a determined nod, you get on your way.

You then hear one of the adult dragons, a female, stirring and moaning. Obviously, she is not dead yet. "Heal me ..." she whispers, "and I will take you to where Pyrokhalistyranellan hides". Astounded by this revelation, you press her for more details.
You take a final look around the lair, mumbling to yourselves in a bit of frustration: indeed, it looks like Pyrostorm was not among these red dragons.

"We were his family" she replies, "Months ago, his mind was overpowered by strange humans and he was forced leave us in order to guard a place they wished to keep safe from trespassers. Heal me, and I give my dragon word that I will fly you there".
"I sense she speaks truthfully: she will keep her word", intervenes Naryl in her usual cryptic manner.
Do you accept the red dragon's offer?
"Trust a red dragon's word? Does she think us fools?" chimes in Runelore, chuckling at the absurd notion.
"Trust ta word of a red dragon??? Is she nuts? She wants ta sucker us, I tell ya!" intecedes Daneel, very nervous and scared by the proposition.
"My friends", intervenes Jhalor, "A dragon word is always honored, even by the lowest and most vile of dragons".
"A dragon word", chimes in Helm with a wise voice, "is an honored word, even fer red dragons".
"Does this one think us fools enough to trust the word of a vile and treacherous red dragon?" chimes in Scyrella, quite offended by the notion.
"Ya know", chimes in Braggan, chuckling at what he's about to say, "even red dragons must honor a dragon word given!"

"I know for a fact", intervenes Strider with his usually calm voice, "that a dragon word is always respected once given, even by evil dragons: as I understand it, it's a matter of preserving the honor of all dragonkind".

With a nod to the female dragon, you accept her offer. After you have healed her, she gladly flies you to where Pyrostorm is being forced to hide. To your surprise (and delight), the journey takes less than a hour, riding on powerful dragon wings!
"We've arrived" announces the red dragon. "My sire lies somewhere within this cave".  After all have disembarked from her back, she then flies away swiftly, and without further due.
Thinking the better of it, you put the dragon out of her misery. In the end, you would rather take your chances by foot than risking too much on a red dragon's back. Without further due, you leave.

You spot Daneel Nimblehands, the furfoot thief who joined you only to leave you after taking some of your gear with him. The fellow is badly bruised and looks depressed. Upon seeing you, he gasps in astonishment (along with a visible trace of dread!).

"Hey guys!" he says timidly, "How are ya? I hope there's no hard feelings, ya know, cuz, like I wrote ya, I just had ta leave, ya know?" Seeing that you are still quite angry about that, Daneel starts talking very nervously:

"Look, youze guys! I can make it up to ya! I swear I do! See? I've learned things about how business is run in here!" Relieved to have caught your attention, he goes on: "On ta second floor of ta prison, ya see, ya'll find ta top man of ta place ...

His name's Halem El-Yessef; he used ta be some big shot Pirate Lord until months ago, when he wuz deposed by another who, I hear, is now ta Queen of ta pirates no less! She sold him out to ta authorities, I tell ya! Well, since he's been here, he's ...

become like ta boss of ta house, ya see? He recruits ta meanest, badest guys in here to his service; of course, then he gets all ta perks, ya know, like more food and stuffs, and no one dares confront him, ya know what I mean?" You nod in understanding.

He then leans to you in whisper: "Well, fer one, I've learned that he has a sure plan to be sprung out of Tarterys Island! Some pirate buddies of him are ta help. Fer two, those guys he recruits, with a few exceptions, all know some password since ...

they apparently are all pirates, ex-pirates, or dealers with pirates themselves". He then grins proudly: "An I know ta damn password! My little ears reach far, dontcha know? Yesserie! But they won't accept me, cuz they don't believe I ever wuz ...

a pirate or, as the saying goes, in ta loop anyways". You then understand how he got his bruises. Knowing what you are thiking, Daneel sighs. "Yep, they made me understand that it would be in my best interest not to talk about it. But, see? ...

With youze guys, they could believe ya were at least in ta loop, and so they'll believe me too!!! So whadaya say, guys? I give ta password, if ya take me with youze until once we get outta here?"  Knowing that you won't be able to get the password ...
out of him by force or otherwise, do you accept Daneel's offer?
Daneel shakes his head in dejection at your refusal. "Ya morrons. Leave me be, then". Shrugging the whole thing off, you walk away.
Daneel Nimblehands is still sitting at this table. Do you accept his offer of the secret password in exchange for his tagging along with you to freedom?

Daneel can barely contain his joy and relief. "That's great, youze guys!!! Ta password is: sea dragon rising. I promise I'll shut up and leave everything to ya! From now until we're out, yer in total control!"
Daneel Nimblehands has rejoined your party. Check out the Allies menu.

This man looks worn down, being badly bruised and severely lacking in food. "It's no use", he mumbles to himself, barely registering your presence, "one cain't survive here if yer not part of Halem's gang ..." He then passes out.
"GO AWAY! STAY AWAY FROM ME! DON'T HURT ME AGAIN!", this frantic man shouts at your approach. From the looks of it, he is starving and appears to have been badly beaten.
This man is lying near-death from starvation and one beating too many. You wonder who could do such a thing, and how could things have become that bad in here.
The doors are triple-locked. Even with your tools, you would be hard pressed to unlock these doors.
Hidden within this sewer vent, you find some flasks of oil!
Hidden within this sewer vent, you find a few unlit torches wrapped in a leather sheet to keep them dry!
You bump into one of the prisoners. "HEY! Watch it, ya bums!" Enraged, he attacks you. Soon enough, other prisoners join the fray!
"I'll be waiting for your safe return!" shouts Naryl, distressed. "Please, do take care!"
"I shall wait for your safe return" Runelore tells you, seemingly chagrined.
"I'll await your return, friends", Jhalor tells you, visibly disapointed by the turn of events.
"I'll be waiting fer yer coming back", Braggan mumbles, obviously dreading for your fate.
"I'll wait for yer safe return, friends", Helm tells you, visibly worried about your fate.
"See youze, guys! It's been fun!" shouts Daneel, visibly relieved by not having to follow you. "Maybe we'll catch up later, okay? Take care!"

The doors are unlocked, as numerous guards walk in with food rations: "Food drive, ya bums!" announces a guard. Immediately, as many prisoners rush and fight their way to the droped food packs, the guards get out and lock the doors again.
Do you attempt to fight your way to some food for your own?

Standing at a safe distance, you watch with disgust the prisoners nearly kill each other for the food rations. You are aghast that the prison authorities would allow something like that to occur. In any case, you are left without even crumbs to eat ...

Guards open the door, yelling out your names. Slowly, you walk up to them: "Ah! There ye are! Yer time is served: we are shipping ye back ta Tanirith!" Relieved, you follow the guards. You are then given back your gear, then sailed back to the city.

"This is great, youze guys!" shouts Daneel with glee, laughing out of joy at the same time. "Good thing they mistook me fer being with youze all along, eh? Well, it wuz fun in any case!" Without further word, Daneel Nimblehands scampers away.

You then spot a group of bullies coming down from the stairs at the end of the prison compound. They walk around, bullying or beating some prisonners to take their food; once they feel like they've got enough rations, they go back upstairs.
All along, you noticed that they are armed! You wonder where they could have gotten their weapons.

You spot a group of bullies coming down the stairs at the end of the prison compound. You can't help but notice that they are armed. They walk around, bullying or beating some of the prisoner to take their food. Soon enough, they come up to you.
"Halem, our boss, needs some of yer food!" snarls one of the bullies. Do you give some of your rations?
Not wanting any trouble, you hand out some of your rations.
Without further word, the bullies go back upstairs, apparently satisfied at having stolen enough food for the day.
"Oh yeah?" snarls the bully at your refusal. "I guess we'd better teach ya a lesson as to who's boss around here!" The bullies then attack!
More bullies come to beat you up!!!
Tired and bloodied, you are satisfied to have held your ground and, most important of all, to have kept the food which belonged to you.

Bloodied and nearly unconscious, you hear the bullies laughing as they take away the little of what you had. "Me think they've learned who's boss here fer good!" chimes in one of the bullies, as they go back upstairs, still laughing.
"Welcome back, friends!" Naryl greets you, very happy to see you safe and sound.
Overjoyed to be free, you then proceed to tell about what you lived while incarcerated on Tarterys Island, as you all go on your way.
"Glad to see you safe and sound, my friends!" Runelore greets you.
"Ye made it back! Praise Moradin!" exclaims Braggan, as he greets each of you with a bear hug.
"My friends!" Jhalor exclaims, visibly happy to see you again.
"Me friends! Praise be Woralduur for yer safe return!" exclaims Helm, as he gives each of you a warm clap on the shoulders.

Not surprisingly, you notice that Daneel Nimblehands has not come to greet you back. Figuring that he must be somewhere doing things up to no good, you shrug off his absence and decide to forget about him. Overjoyed to be free, you go on your way.
To your surprise, Daneel Nimblehands has already managed to unlock the door!  "There ya go, guys!" he whispers proudly while winking at you. "Now, let's go see what's behind door numbah one!"

"Well, I heard rumors" he mumbles, "that many people in power could be involved". "Yeah! Me too!", exclaims the swordsman, "One of the Lords in Sparklestone, for example" . The elf grins:"And what about Aranys' Lord?" All fall silent. You then walk away.
One of the bartenders of the inn accosts you: "Hey, ye guys", he whispers, "Do ye need priviledged information? I charge 5 gold pieces per bit!"  Do you pay?

He pockets the money:"There's a snowy-frozen region of ta Khanark Rockies far north-west of here; but watch yer step there or ye'll fall to yer deaths! Ta only way to reach this region is through a lake in ta Rockies located straight north of here".

He pockets the gold: "I hear there's a collapsed volcano still filed with lava in ta Khanark Rockies. Ta only way there is through an ancient tunnel carved within the mountains. This tunnel is supposed ta be somewhere near the city of Lantharond".
He pockets the money then whispers: "I hear that ta Lord of Aranys is quite power-hungry; ta rumor is that he's aiming ta control all trade in ta region!".

He pockets the money: "Lantharond is a fair-sized port-city lying north of Tanirith, on ta same coast. It's ruled by King Vallar Dragonheart, of ta very old Dragonheart dynasty. I hear he's been a good king since ta ten years he ascended to ta throne".
The sign here reads: "Memorial City Park". It points to the east.
The sign here reads: "Memorial City Park". It points to the north.
This sign points to the west for Bywater and the Realmz, and to the east for Sharranth and the Sword Lands.
This worn out sign reads:  "Rock Forest-Trade Caravan Waystation".  Also, the sign points to the east for Aranys, and to the west for Sharranth.
This sign points to the south-east for Sharranth.
"How did you get back in my inn???" shout both Zaran and Areyna, in unisson. You are immediately thrown out, along with a good measure of rough-handling.
The local brewery is closed. A sign reads: "Closed until new owners found". A  secret hatch leading underground is bolted shut.
The front desk is unattented, thanks to you.
You startle a few birds who fly away.
You stepped on a small spider, squashing it to death.
Nothing interesting here.
Knowing you are outmatched, you lower your weapons as a gesture of peace.
You stepped on some weird slimy substance. You wonder what it could be.
As you run away, the dragons spew their breath weapons right on you!!!
A strong, cold wind blows from the west. Far away in that direction, you notice mountain peaks white with snow, as well as snowy- and icy-white mountainous parts of the Khanark Rockies.
A few snow fluries drop slowly on you. Looking to the west, you notice mountain peaks white with snow, as well as numerous snowy- and icy-white mountainous parts of the Khanark Rockies.

You notice ice patches of various sizes floating in this region of the lake. Looking to the west, you see mountain peaks white with snow, as well as numerous snowy- and icy-white mountainous parts of the Khanark Rockies.
You are under attack!!!
This worn out sign points to the south-east for Sharranth, to the west for the Realmz, and to the north-east for Aranys.

As you are peacefully sleeping, strange and disturbing images invade your dreams. Haunting figures, the faces of which you cannot make, appear to you in all their power, energies emanating from them. They laugh at you, making you feel helpless.

You do not know who they are, or what they are, but you feel convinced that they represent a grave danger of some kind. You then all wake up startled. Looking at each other, you realize that you all had the same, disturbing dream. As the eerie ...

images fade from your mind, you wonder if Myst, the Goddess of dreams and mysteries, did not send that dream to warn you about some impending doom. But what are those unfathomable figures that you saw? What danger do they bring? You are puzzled by this.

For some reason, you now can't help but think of the disturbing dreams you've been having lately, and that the woman in the globe is most likely one of the hauting, powerful figures that you keep seeing in those dreams.
This cave is dark and damp, but otherwise looks abandoned. You see that it leads within the mountains. Do you go in?
You run into a group of gnats!

"Hey!" shouts a gnat for the remparts. You see that more like him guard the gates as well. "Who are youze? Whatcher doin' here?" Before you can answer, the gates are opened and gnats swarm out of them to get at you!
More gnats rush to you from the guard posts!
Gnats rush out of their shacks to attack the intruders that you are!
Upon your approach, numerous gnats rush out from the compound to attack you. You have barely time to notice a bigger gnat behind them, most likely their chief.
With the death of their chief, most of the gnats run away!
With the sounds of fleeing gnats getting away from you with the death of their chief, you investigate the filthy compound.
You are surprised to find a rather sizeable booty, probably made up of the raids the gnats have been undertaking lately!
Finding nothing else of interest, you leave.
This is an old, craked, dusty and dirty crypt lying almost in ruins. Carved runic markings, barely legible, are in a long-forgotten language you do not understand.
You find a surprisingly well-preserved opening mechanism. Pulling on a lever, a good part of the crypt's front lowers with a loud grinding noise.
Once the crypt is opened, stale air  -centuries old-  rush out and assaults your nostrils. After recovering from the awful smell, you see old marble stairs going down underground. Do you go down?
Do you go down inside the crypt?

This tunnel leads deep into the mountains; from the slight but very cold draft coming out, you can guess that it must lead somewhere into the snowy parts of the Khanark Rockies. Do you go into the tunnel?
After a little more than a week's journey within tortuous caves and passages, you finally arrive at the other side.
The wind is cold, strong, and almost deafening.
After a few days of travel, you end up in the snowy, frozen parts of the Khanark Rockies.
After a few days of travel, you get back into the warmer regions of the Khanark Rockies.

You overhear two women conversing: "I saw four knights checking in earlier", the first one says to the other, "they looked quite somber if not suspicious; in fact, their armors were all black! I heard they were in the second room on the left of ...

the upper floor". "Four knights? Somber and all in black?" chimes in the second woman, "Well, dark and dangerous men are often exciting, you know!"  Both ladies start giggling at that.  You then walk away.

"Intruders, meet your fate!" booms a loud, guttural voice. Out of the shadows walks a huge skeletal warrior, it's green eyes bright with the light of necromantic magics. "I guard this place, and I bring death to all who violate it!". He then attacks!
The shadows suddenly attack you!
Wandering flesh fiends eye you as lunch!
Wandering creatures attack you!
As you approach this sinister statue, it's form begins to weave and move, transforming into a fell spirit of the shadows!
This huge lever is obviously ancient, being caked with rust, cobwebs, and dust. Do you pull it down?
With much effort, you manage to pull the lever down. In the distance, somewhere within the crypt, you hear stone slabs shifting about.
The old, rusty lever is hopelessly jammed in a down position.
You leave the ancient lever be.
These old marble stairs lead down to a dark, damp and dusty undercrypt, filled with foul air and the smell of death. Do you go down?

The undercrypt fills you with dread. Eerilly quiet, your senses tell you nonetheless that creatures of the shadows and undeath abound here, lurking around and waiting for fresh life to sate their hunger. Their looming presence is overwhelming.
This antechamber appears to have never been visited by anyone since its construction. You are quite sure that it would be safe for you to camp here.
You leave the safe room.
You find here a flight of marble stairs spiralling upwards. As you start climbing them, you are envelopped in a shimmering light, then magically transported back to the surface!
A huge slab of granite slides down suddenly over the door behind you, blocking it hopelessly!!!
You hear a disembodied, echoing laugh which fills you with dread and chills your blood. It seems to be coming from everywhere at once.

This room is filled with murals and paintings of the conquering exploits of Ptaraz, as well as his numerous victorious battles. You notice what looks like armored statues standing along the columns in this musoleum.
At the same time, the statues change into skeletal warriors ... and they immediately attack!
Suddenly, a huge slab of granite falls down over the door at the other end of the room, blocking it hopelessly!!!

This thick door is made of black obsidian. A figure is carved onto it, which can only be Ptaraz. He is depicted victorious, holding his sword high while holding the decapitated head of one of his slain enemies. The door is locked. What do you want to do?
A group of wandering ghouls stumble upon you around this corner!
This dusty and damp room is filled with cobwebs and spider webs. As soon as you realize your possible predicament, the room's occupants descend upon you and attack!

A worn out bronze plaque is set on this door. Despite its age, you manage to decipher its runic markings: "Dam Yzarc, the seer of Thandyr, always held that the rugged path is the most dangerous, whereas the smooth path is the easiest and safest".
A beam of magical energy strikes you out of nowhere!!!
You find what appears to be the remains of some humanoid; however, it is hard to say since all that is left is a pile of dust with a few bone fragments strewn about.

You find the remains of what appears to be a group of crypt raiders or adventurers; their bones have been picked clean. These remains are old indeed since even the bones are barely nothing but brittle and dust. You do find a few useful items, however.

This sarcophagus of black obsidian stone is covered with dust, grime, and cobwebs. You can make out some carvings depicting various battle scenes featuring a warrior which could only be Ptaraz. Do you attempt to open it?
With great effort, you manage to slide the sarcophagus' sealing slab off the top, making it fall to the ground with a loud, stone crashing, sound.

Suddenly, a ghostly figure emerges out of the sarcophagus, gazing at you with bright glowing eyes, red with hate. "You dare disturb my resting place?", it asks in a guttural voice. "You shall pay for your folly!" it announces, just as it attacks you!

After the battle, you find that the sarcophagus is completely empty, save for worn out satin sheets and pillows that are ages-old and without any value. Was this the fell spirit of Ptaraz? You wonder ...
This old coffer holds nothing of value, save for dust and cobwebs.

This old coffer lies opened, apparently having been looted long before you found it. Indeed, it is now filled with dust and cobwebs. You do find a bauble or two, along with a few coins, obviously left behind by the hasty pillagers who preceded you.

The old, oak doors which barred this place have been broken down, probably by pillagers or looters which have preceded you. From the dust accumulated on the pieces of the doors, this must have happened centuries ago.
You enter what can only be a treasure chamber. You see chests and coffers lying near the north, west, and east walls. Surely, this must be Ptaraz' treasure!
Fortunately, none of the chests and coffers are locked. Smiling with glee, you think of this place as easy pickings!

You enter into what can only be a hall of statues. Indeed, numerous statues of marble, granite, or obsidian depict a mighty warrior in various poses or combat stances. Of course, this could be no one else but King Ptaraz.
Suddenly, many of those statues become enveloped in a shimmering aura of red magical light. Within a blink of your eyes, they are transformed into skeletal warriors which attack you immediately!

You enter a large throne room. Huge columns lie along walls of black marble, which seem to be enveloped in some kind of blueish magic aura. To the west side of the room, you notice a large throne made of platinum and etched with numerous precious stones.

You enter a large throne room. Huge columns lie along walls of black marble, which seem to be enveloped in a blueish magic aura. In the back of the room facing you, you see a large throne made of platinum and etched with numerous precious stones.

As you approach the throne, you see a skeleton already lying within it in a sitting position, its hands resting of the throne's side-arms. This must be the remains of some woman, as can be judged from the decayed robe of dyed satin and lace still ...

covering most of the bones. You also note that numerous bracelets of gold, and necklaces of silver and pearls, still adorn her remains. Her skull is facing down, as if staring at you, and is still wearing a jeweled crown of platinum.

Suddenly, the skeleton's bones seem to fly appart, along with robe, jewelry, and crown, as if caught by some strange magical whirlwind. As the pieces whirl around, they gradually disapear in order to be replaced by a disembodied figure who now sits ...

on the throne in their place. This spirit -a woman as well- is covered in dark, flowing robes of lace. Her long, curled, hair of red seems to be caught in some kind of magical breeze, moving as if it had a life of its own. With a shudder, you feel ...

her angry gaze upon you, coming out from her eyes glowing red with anger, hate, and death. "I am Tanira, queen and consort of the great and mighty Ptaraz", she announces with a whisper, which you hear very well in your very souls.

"Being an archmage, I made this place for my beloved upon his death", she continues, "then sealed myself within to die and join him in the afterlife. But the gods of Light had judged us as cruel and evil mortals, and therefore sentenced our souls ...

to remain forever prisoners of this crypt, and as well as denying us even the solace of each other's company: indeed, my beloved's resting place lies in a secret room near this hall, a room which can be entered only by living flesh". She pauses.

"But once its doors are opened, then we would be able to be with each other finally. So, in exchange for your lives and safe passage back to the surface, I ask you to find Ptaraz' room and open its doors for me".  Do you accept Queen Tanira's offer?

With a simple nod, Tanira's eye flash bright with magic, teleporting you in a corridor. A few feet ahead of you, you see the doors of what would be Ptaraz' resting room. "Enter, and touch his sarcophagus" Tanira's mind-whisper tells you.
"Very well" Tanira replies, her whisper harsh with anger. "Then, pay for your intrusion!". With a gesture of her disembodied hand, skeletal warriors appear to help her destroy you!
Panting and tired from such a battle, you notice a strange key lying on the seat of the throne. Just as you take it, the throne turns into useless rust.

Tanira appears in front of the throne. "You have not done what you were supposed to do", she whispers angrily, "so pay instead for your intrusion!". With a gesture of her disembodied hand, skeletal warriors appear to help her destroy you!
But before you get on your way, a strange key appears out of thin air and drops in your hands. "You will need it", Tanira's fading whisper tells you.
Panting and tired from this battle, you walk over to the throne in order to retrieve some of the jewels adorning it. Just as you get near it, it suddenly turns into useless dust!
A strange magical force field prevents your passage!

Overwhelmed by the numbers, you are quickly made prisoners by Tanira's skeletal warriors. "You are strong", she whispers, "and will serve me well among the ranks of my warriors". Chanting eery incantations, she weaves necromantic ...
magics and turns you into undead warriors, casting your souls into oblivion in the process.

You come upon a magical force field which blocks your way. However, the skeleton key starts chiming loudly, bringing down the force field. Having fullfilled its purpose, the key then crumbles to dust.

The doors in front of you are made of platinum and etched with carvings of Ptaraz. Somehow, the doors are aware of your presence: they begin to glow and pulsate with a bright light of many colors, then open by themselves before becoming dormant again.

You enter into a large, eerily silent musoleum. The place is filled with sculpted columns and bas reliefs in marble, all depicting the life and times of Ptaraz. A huge sarcophagus of solid gold lies in the center of the room.

The sarcophagus of solid gold is etched and carved with numerous runes and esoteric symbols in silver and platinum. On the top of the sarcophagus, you notice a depression shaped like a left hand. Do you put your hand in this depression?
Who volunteers?

As your party member puts the hand in the depression, the sarcophagus' cover slowly slides off, revealing the brittled bones of what used to be Ptaraz, founder and first king of Tanirith. At the same time, a strange light emanates from ...

within the sarcophagus, slowly rising out of it and floating up to where you stand. Gradually, the light takes the shape of a ghostly human warrior, who is now gazing at you with eyes lit red with evil and madness.

"I am Ptaraz the Conquerer, and you are fools indeed to intrude upon my resting place!" announces the ghost with a guttural voice. "It pleases me to kill once again; it has been a long time since my last battle!"

Suddenly, a mummy crawls out of the sarcophagus, gazing at you with empty eye-sockets lit by a red glow. "You dare disturb my resting place?" it asks with a chilling whisper. "You will pay for this!" it announces, just as it attacks!
Suddenly, some of the statues materialize into mummies and side with the spectre of Ptaraz, attacking in unisson!
Upon the destruction of Ptaraz' spectre, the gold sarcophagus shivers and crumbles into worthless rust! It would appear that nothing of value is to be found or retrieved in the crypt of Ptaraz ...
You then hear in your minds Ptaraz' voice one last time: "Thank you for delivering me, fools that you are!"

The spirit of Queen Tanira then materializes next to her King. For a moment, the two hold hands and stare at each other in wonder. Ptaraz then turns to you: "We thank you for allowing us to be with each other finally. As promised, we will send you ...
back to the surface. Furthermore, receive this gift of gratitude". Out of thin air, a bright gem, as big as a fist, materializes and drops in your outstretched hands.

"We may be still damned for our evil deeds", continues Ptaraz, as he gazes lovingly at Tanira, "but now that we can be with each other, this prison of our souls won't be so bad". Tanira nods: "Thank you, strangers". She then flicks her wrist ...
enveloping you in a magical aura which teleports you back to the surface!
The entrance to the undercrypt is now unaccessible once again. It appears that Ptaraz and Tanira prefer to spend the eternity together without being disturbed.

Overwhelmed by your opponents, you are quickly made prisoners by the mummies. "You are strong", chimes the spectre of Ptaraz. "You shall serve me well among my mummified retinue". Chanting eery incantations, he weaves necromantic ...
This secret antechamber is filled with chests and coffers holding coins, jewels, armors, weapons, and magic items. Looks like you have found Ptaraz' burial treasure!
You enter another secret antechamber. It is lit by the glow of a column of blue light which stands just in front of the north wall of the room.
As you approach the column of light, you notice a huge gem, about the size of a fist, floating about five feet from the floor, within the column of light itself.
Your party member is assailed by the energies of the column of light!
The column of light disapears! With haste, you catch the gem before it falls to the floor.
This huge cave is filled with stalagmites and stalagtites. A cavernous tunnel leads further underground.
You leave the cave complex.
This tunnel seems to lead further down in the underearth.

You arrive upon a huge portal made of bronze. The construction must be quite ancient since the bronze is tarnished extensively. Numerous bas-reliefs have been carved into the bronze itself, depicting a mighty wizard conquering empires and armies.
Strangely enough, the portal does not appear to be locked or protected by magic.
The lich summons shadow elf warriors to his aid!

You come upon a small crypt filled with columns and quite open (it has no doors). At the back of the crypt, you see a shadowy figure dressed in robes sitting on a marble throne. Its eyes bright with an eerie white light stare at you.

"Who dares disturb my sanctum sanctorum?" booms the shadowy figure. At it leans forward as if to get a better view of you, you notice its skeletal hands gripping a staff. You then see not a face, but a skull underneath the hood of its robes.
The stairs to the castle's main floor are now filled with debris, having collapsed at the same time as the castle itself.

Seeing your fear, but yet standing your ground, the entity chuckles. "It has been a long time since I have seen bravery in my presence!", it chimes. "I am Druroxx Bane, a powerful mage and, as you can see, a lich. I have been so for millennia, now."

"I used to conquer and rule empires, back on the continent of Anarym, which is east of this continent. In time, brave men and women rose in power, enough to force me into exile from this wonderful continent of my birth. I have since then spent my ...

near-immortality in this secluded place, quite content to sit here in peace and let my mind roam the universe. It was during such a far-reaching journey that an adventurous thief managed to steal a powerful magical orb that belongs to me, a few ...

centuries past. I managed to wound him to death, but he escaped nonetheless before dying. I am convinced that his remains lie somewhere within these caves. So, I propose a bargain to you, brave ones: find my orb and bring it back to me; in exchange, ,,,

I shall give you some of the magical items which I have kept over the millennia, along with a prized possession of that thief which he lost when he fled from me." At that, Bane produces a strange monocle which radiates strong magics. "What say you?"
Do you accept Druroxx Bane's bargain?

"Maybe you are not as brave as I thought you were", snarls Druroxx Bane. "Well then, the price for disturbing me is all your equipment and moneys. Give this, and your pathetic lives shall be spared". Do you aquiesce to Bane's demands?
With haste, you divest yourselves of your gear and your valuables, laying them at the feet of Druroxx Bane. "Well done, pathetic ones. Now leave me be and never come back!"
Druroxx Bane is laughing at your approach. "You dare come back? I was clearly wrong then: you are not brave, but utter fools!!!" He then rises from his marble throne and attacks!
A strange wind comes and blows away Druroxx Bane's bones to dust. After a quick search, you find a chest hidden behind his throne, which holds a nice treasure along with your equipment!

Bane simply nods in acknowledgement. "Do not come back unless you have found my orb" he adds, before falling into some kind of transe. You then notice a powerful magic aura shimmering about him as his mind is gone once again to some unknown dimension.

Druroxx Bane is still sitting on his marble throne in a transe, surrounded by a powerful magic aura of protection as his mind wanders somewhere in the universe. You decide it would be best not to disturb him without proper reason.

Upon your approach, Druroxx Bane comes out of his transe. "Well done. My astral form saw your success; that is why I knew you were coming back with my orb. Give it to me, and I shall give you what was promised". Do you give the orb?
"Here is the reward promised" Bane replies, with satisfaction. Despite his lich form, he seems almost as if he is smiling with happiness at having his orb back.
"Now go", Bane adds, "And do not come back. I really dislike having my peace disturbed".

"You dare come back and disturb me again?" shouts Druroxx Bane, obviously angry to no end. "Our business is concluded; I have thus no qualms at teaching you a lesson in good manners!" Rising from his marble throne, he attacks!
A strange wind descends and blows away Bane's bones to dust. After actively searching, you find a chest hidden behind his throne, containing a very interesting treasure.
"Then pay with your lives!" Bane snarls, as he rises from his throne to attack!
As you attempt to run away, you hear Bane's dreadful laugh as he launches a terrible death spell on you!
"We had a bargain!" shouts Druroxx Bane, incensed at your betrayal. He rises from his throne and attacks!

You find the remains of some adventurer. You notice that he still wears a bracelet engraved with the name "Nessar". Most of his bones have been picked clean. However, you do find a few items of value.
If these are the remains of Nessar the Master thief, where is his monocle?
Having found Nessar's remains and Bane's orb among them, you quickly get on your way to complete your bargain with the lich.
Scally, clawed hands rise out of the water to grab you!!!
You find the remains of some adventurers. You find nothing of value.
You find the remains of some troglodytes. Nothing of value is left.
You find the remains of a small group of dwarven warriors. Nothing of value is found.
You find the remains of some goblins. nothing of value is left.
You find the remains of a small group of shadow elves. Nothing of value is found.
You find the remains of some dogres. All if any valuables are long gone.
You come upon an area of the caves which is completely flooded by underground waters.
From deep under the water, you notice something glittering from the light of your torches.
After a few seconds, your party member is forced to come back to the surface: some strong undercurrents make any diving underwater practically impossible.
With the help of your spell, your party member easily dives deep underwater. After a minute or two, an unlocked chest is retrieved, holding a few valuables that catch your eye!
You find a secret passage leading to a tunnel within the rock cliffs here. Do you go into the tunnel?
You find a secret passage which appears to lead to a flooded area of the caves. Do you go in?

From the looks of things, it appears that you are heading straight to a major shadow elf outpost. Knowing that  -at least for now-  you are no match for such numbers of shadow elves, you wisely back away. Luckyly, you have not been spotted.
Out of the remparts comes a small group of shadow elves, their weapons drawn and ready to fight. "Let's kill these intruding fools!" yells one of them. In unisson, they attack!
More shadow elves join the fray, this time lead by one of their priestesses of Tlarantale, Goddess of evil and spiders.
This guard post is now empty. Rumaging through some paperwork you found, you stumble upon two interesting pieces of information.

The first is a sealed parchment, which reads like this:"By the power and wisdom of Tlanrantale, I, Highpriestess Nuralea, forward the following to all command posts: we must watch for those Overlords, learn as much as we can about them, and know of ...
their schemes. Only then will we make our own plans to usurp them or, if truly convenient, join with them. Praise our Mighty Tlarantale for revealing the exitence of these Overlords to us".

The other is a short report, most likely written by the priestess in charge of this outpost and which you just defeated. Aside from irrelevant day-to-day activities, a few lines catch your eye: "... spying scouts within the snowy regions of the ...

Khanark Rockies have uncovered a lost, ruined temple which has been occupied only recently. In fact, they report mysterious mages apparently involved in dark designs and activities. I think that this incident is related to the Cult of Lankharh which ...
operates under Tanirith, and which is itself apparently an apparatus of these Overlords we have to watch for ...".
You are surprised to find a bridge in these caves, let alone one as well built as this one. You wonder who, or what, constructed it.
You stumble upon a group of goblins, apparently camping in this cave!
You stumble upon a band of ogres camping within this cave!
You find a few valuables on this body.
A group of trolls live here, and they are not happy to see you intrude!

From all appearances, this millennia-old temple in ruins was once dedicated to Erond, God of Knowledge and Thought.  You can't even begin to guess how it ended being buried within this cave.  Do you go inside?
You leave Erond's ruined temple.
A barrier of powerful magical energies blocks this corridor.
You find a few items of interest. These must have been abandoned ages ago, when whatever disaster happened and caused the temple to be buried underground.
Your searching has uncovered suspicious cracks in the old marble of the floor. Removing the loose pieces, you find a small, unlocked chest which contains strange relics.
Erond's orb begins to pulsate brightly as you approach the magical barrier. In an instant, the barrier disapears and the orb fades into nothingness.
You are now free to walk into this large corridor!

You come upon a strange altar made of solid black marble filled with swirls of white crystals. It has no markings, with the exception of three square depressions on its top, arranged relative to each other as to form the edges of an invisible triangle.
An invisible force field surrounds a mysterious well that seems to be filled with slowly, swirling stars.
You realize that you need something to put within the squares etched unto the top of the altar, in order to activate it.
After placing the icons and praying to Erond, the swirling stars within the mysterious well behind the altar swirl faster, filling the well with pure light!
An awe-fearsome spirit then rises from the well of light, scrutinizing you with severity. Immediately, his ominous, booming voice rings throughout the temple.

"I AM THE ORACLE OF EROND", the deep, baritone voice booms, enounciating each word slowly,  "I KNOW WHAT IS, WHAT WAS, AND WHAT WILL BE. AS WELL I KNOW THE PATH WHICH YOU WALK ON, EVEN IF YOU DO NOT REALIZE IT. HEAR NOW MY WORDS AND HEED THEIR MEANING".

"LONG AGO, A RACE OF HUMAN BEINGS LEARNED TO HARNESS THE POWER OF THE MIND, POWERS OVER MATTER, ENERGY, TIME, AND OTHER MINDS. THESE HUMANS ROSE TO BECOME THE LEGENDARY LANKHARHANS AND BROUGHT ABOUT THE FABLED EMPIRE OF LANKHARH".

"EVENTUALLY, THE EMPIRE WAS BROUGHT LOW BY MEANS OF MAGIC AND PROTECTIVE DEVICES SHIELDING AGAINST THEIR POWERS. KNOW NOW THAT THE OVERLORDS WHICH YOU ARE FACING ARE DESCENDANTS OF LANKHARH, AND THUS LANKHARHANS THEMSELVES".

"THEIR PLANS GO FAR AND WIDE, BUT KNOW ALSO THAT NOT ALL LANKHARHANS SHARE THE GOALS OF THE OVERLORDS, THAT NUMBERS OPPOSE THE RETURN OF THE DREADED MIND LORDS. HEED THIS, AND YOU SHALL ACQUIRE HELP IN DEFEATING THEM. I HAVE SAID ENOUGH NOW, FOR  ..."
IT IS UP TO MORTALS TO FIND FOR THEMSELVES WHAT IS, AND WHAT IS NOT, AS WELL AS THE WHYS AND WHERES. KNOWLEDGE IS THE KEY TO UNDERSTANDING, AND LOGIC IS THE TOOL. REMEMBER THIS, ALWAYS ...".
The Oracle then returns within the well, its light suddenly vanishing in order to be filled anew with slowly, swirling stars. The Oracle of Erond is now silent once again.
Only then do you realize that the icons you have place upon the altar have vanished!
Your attempt has caused a magical backlash directed at you!!!
A small party of shadow elves is camping in this cavern. Upon seeing you, they attack!

You stumble on the bodies of numerous dwarven warriors. From the looks of it, they were hit hard and fast, and without mercy. You estimate that their demise occured about a week ago; but who (or what) could cause such damage to battle-hardened dwarves?
You run into a patrol of shadow elves! Upon seeing you, they attack!!!
As you approach these gates, the doors are opened and bloodthirsty dogres rush out to make mince meat out of you. It would appear that they have seen you coming from afar!
The gates remain open after the battle. Do you cross them and enter what seems to be a dogre village?
More dogres rush at you!!!

A huge dogre (surely the chief of this tribe) is standing fast before his house, surrounded by his loyal warriors, and waiting for you. "Me Chief Graoul", the huge dogre intones. "Before we kill ye, I've an offer ta make: rid us of ta mind-mage ...
that's been bossing us around an' keeping all our loot, an' I let ye live an' give moneys to boot. Ye do this, I live me part o' ta bargain; ye don't, we kill ye".  Do you accept Graoul's bargain?
An invisible force field surrounds this strange habitation. Its architecture surely doesn't fit with the shabby huts and houses of the dogres.
The Chief growls at your answer. "Ye morrons! We kill ye now, then!"  Immediately, Graoul and his warriors attack!
With the death of their Chief, most dogre warriors flee in terror!

You rumage through Chief Graoul's house after the battle, but find nothing of value. Looks like he wasn't lying when he mentioned that a so-called mind-mage was confiscating the accumulated riches of his dogre tribe.

As you notice that the force field surrounding this strange house is gone, you hear a sinister laugh. "Come in", whispers a deep, cruel voice. Only then you realize that both laughter and words had been mind-spoken to you!
Do you enter?

Graoul nods: "Good. Ye go to ta strange house in our village, near me house. There's some invisible barrier around it, but me thinkin' that ta mind-mage mind-heard all we said, so ta barrier will be gone an' he be waitin' for ye. Go; we wait."

Upon your approach, angry dogre warriors and Chief Graoul are waiting for you: "Why're ye here?", snarls the Chief. "Do whot ye said ye would do!". The Chief and his warriors go back into the Chief's house, muttering angrily under their breath.

Graoul and his warriors are already waiting for you. "Ye did it!" exclaims Graoul with a wide, ugly grin. "Now ta loot's ours again! Of course, its against our custom to share, so ..."  Suddenly, Graoul and his warriors attack!!!
Upon his death, your opponent releases a powerful wave of psi-energies in one, desperate attempt at killing as many of you with him.
You end up in a dark and damp basement. The stench of decay in this misbegotten place is unbearable, making you dizzy and sick to your stomach.
Suddenly, the stairs retract and a slab of marble slides over the upstairs opening!!!
Again, you "hear" the mind-mage's telepathic laugh. It would appear that you are trapped, and most likely for good at that!
The decay and dampness in this basement is a veritable feeding ground for diseases. It appears that some of you have fallen victim from one of them ...
The basement is littered with the decayed (or decaying) bodies of dogre warriors. It seems they have been trapped in here as well and eventually died of starvation, or something other ...

You find a loose tile under the inch or two of soiled water. After prying it loose, you reveal an opening which appears to lead into some underground tunnel. Glad to have found a way out, you climb down the small hole, soon finding yourselves ...
crawling within the tight tunnel, leading you directly outside the mind-mage's house! Congratulations: you have managed to outwit the trap designed by the mind-mage!
Huge, gaping pits filled with boiling acid prevent your passage! What are you to do?
This is a statue depicting a lightly garbed warrior with strange, haunting eyes. You can sense a strong magic aura about the statue.
Invisible mental energies assault your minds!

You find some travelling rations you can take with you.

Runelore walks up to you: "I will stand guard outside at the door, watching your backs just in case treachery is afoot". You nod in agreement, appreciating your companion's wisdom.

at the realization of being found out, the man yells out: "Get those intruders!!!" In a blink of an eye, you are facing the mind-mage flanked by his dogre bodyguards.

she is glaring at you, incensed: "YOU!?!" she fumes. "After all the troubles you have caused us, after acting like veritable thorns on our sides, and after disrupting our plans like you have done, you DARE show your pathetic selves to us? We may have ...

book and its portent mean exactly, you leave the small farming family.

You see the farmer in his fields, working hard. From the looks of things, all has come back to normal for him and his family. Do you approach to tell him you have reconsidered and decided finally to retrieve the holy book stolen from him?
You see the farmer, working hard in his fields. From the looks of things, all has gone back to normal for him and his small family.

"My friends", Naryl intercedes. "I have heard here the mention of a mind-mage ... to me, this means the Overlords are involved. And if they are, then this must involve us as well, especially if we are to uncover them and unravel their sinister plans!".

"So," Strider finally says, smiling, "You've uncovered some conspiracy involving a mysterious A.D., eh? Well, it's rather easy to guess who this A.D. is, no?" Chuckling, he goes on: "Akkar Dhun, of course. I have been interested in what is going on ...

A guard walks up to you: "Hey! Aren't ye the Heroes of Wailsrond?"  Unsure if you should answer, you remain silent.  The man grins: "Yes, ye're the ones! My boss would like to meet ye!".  He then opens the gate and leads you to the estate.

This estate is surrounded by a barbed wire fence. A silver plaque reads: "Sparklestone Mining and Smeltering Company". A few guards patrol the yards. One of them walks up to you: "Say! Aren't ye the Heroes of Wailsrond?"  Unsure what to answer ...

Dogres rush out of their houses to defend their village!
You enter a large cave filled with spider webs.
The doors to the Dwarven King's Halls open upon your approach.
This is a statue of the legendary dwarven hero Galduur. You notice the absence of a shield on his shield-arm.

Gathering your nerves, and keeping in mind the dwarven priest's insistence, you walk right up to the king's throne.

"Me son!!!" shouts the king with joy upon your approach. Immediately, a loud cheer greets Braggan as the king embraces him. "I feared ye would never come back", the king adds, obviously fighting back the tears welling up in his eyes. "Does this means?"

us the hope our wary hearts need! Bring on the feast and mead: for tonight, the Halls celebrate!" Amidst another thunderous cheer, the king shouts: "And let us celebrate me son, and me son's heroic friends!!!"

As you feast with Braggan, the king, and his council, you share tales of adventures, battles, and noble deeds. Many a song is sung on this night, leaving you with a deep sense of accomplishment. "Me father", Braggan asks at one point, as everyone is ...

Braggan then looks at you, winking: "Then let us find Gnomilar and convince our gnome cousins to join forces!" Without hesitation, you shout your agreement to that. Beaming with pride, the king makes another toast to your bravery.

You then gather your things as the king claps your shoulders. "You will sleep in the guest room of me hall, of course! Go to the south-east door, which leads to the guest quarters". Bidding him goodnight, you go.
Galduur's shield-arm is now holding the real shield once held by the legendary dwarven hero.
The king nods at you upon your approach. Noticing that he is quite busy, you decide not to bother him.

You proudly announce to the King that you have solved the gnome problem by finding their holy lamp and bringing it back to them; and with the lamp providing Woralduur's protection over their village, the gnome King is able to lend some of his ...

warriors to help the dwarves. "Praise be Moradin and Woralduur!" exclaims the dwarven king. "Now the odds are for us! Together with our cousins, we could now strike at the enemy's heart! So I ask ye to first find the hill giant's lair: we know it  ...
is somewhere around here in the Khanark Rockies. Once ye do, we will send warriors, both dwarves and gnomes, to help you rout them hill giant scum along with their bloody bully of a king!".

You tell the king that you have routed the giants and killed their king. "By the gods!" exclaims the dwarven king, "ye truly are heroes! But there is still the ogres, which have also allied with them orcs ...."
With a firm nod, you set yourselves to find and investigate the hill giant lair!
"Like the giants' lair," continues the king, "the ogres' lair is somewhere around here in the Khanark Rockies. Find it, and we will send warriors to bring this infested hole down!"
With a determined nod, you set yourselves to find and investigate the ogre lair!

With a humble smile, you inform the dwarven king that you have routed the ogres and killed their Chief. "By Clodurin!" exclaims the king, "We will have to sing songs about ye soon enough! Well then, all that remains for us to have victory is to ...

find the village of the orcs which are the true butchers and war-mongers! Their village is somewhere south-west of Stone Gate; find it, and we'll join ye to rid the Khanark Rockies of this scourge!!!"
With a clasp of hands, you bid the dwarven king farewell and set yourselves to find the orc village!
More warriors join the battle!

At your announcement that you have found the place, the dwarven king goes into a frenzy: "Finally, retribution will be ours!!! I'm sending a messenger to the gnome king now, to tell him we march together on the morrow!!!"

Upon your approach, alarmed orc warriors sound the call to battle; in the blink of an eye, the united gnome-dwarven punitive force is engaged by a hoard of orcs, lead by none other than their King!

Gnome warriors on watch nod respectfully to you, as you cross the gate of their village.

Guards respectfully block your way: "Our apologies", says one of the guards, "but our king is very busy in this aftermath of the war; however, he sends you again his gratitude and respect for your noble deeds and heroic help in winning the war".
The abandoned guard-post lies in near-ruins.

You are approaching a large orc village. From your vantage point, you see huge numbers of orcs going about daily business or training as warriors. Knowing you can't possibly confront such a large tribe by yourselves, you skillfully walk away undetected.
Having found the orc village, you make haste to get back to the Dwarven Halls.

"There they are!" shouts the dwarven king, all smiles. You see that the gnome king is already here as well, along with his retinue of gnome champions and priests. "Time to celebrate the Heroes of the Dwarven Halls!" adds the dwarven king. The roaring ...

supply of mead, along with loud songs and much laughter. It is obvious that the dwarves and gnomes are immensely relieved that the war, the dying and the hardships are finally over, being able to go back to the peaceful and prosperous life they enjoyed.

The celebration lasts until the early hours of the next day. Tired, you join everyone else and go to sleep. Just before you do, the dwarven and gnome kings bid you good night: "Me thanks again, me friends" says the dwarven king. "And mine as ...

well, noble ones. May the fates smile on you always!" adds the gnome king. "And before me forgets", the dwarven king says, "Me have given orders so that ye may visit our Hero's Hall and Library Hall. Me thinks you will find them very mesmerizing; fer ...
sure enough, we have some of the oldest records this side of the Realmz". With a final handshake and a wink, you take your leave.
Dwarven warriors on watch nod respectfully as you pass.
This looks like the guest-room assigned to you.

"Praise be Danuur!" exclaims the old mariner, as you give him a keg of Dwarven Hall mead. "'Tis been years since me had a swill o' that fine brew! Thank ye, lads! O' course, ye cain take me boat! Have a great sail!" The old man then runs to his house ...

to savor his mead. Just as he is about to enter, he turns to you one last time, shouting: "Oh! Before me forgets: just come an' see me when ye bring back the Windcatcher, allright lads?" With a last wave, he goes in his house.

"Welcome back, lads!" the old mariner greets you. "Me thanks fer returning me beautiful Windcatcher safe, sound, and still sea-worthy!" Laughing, he winks at you. "If ye ever need her again, just come an' ask me; an' bring more o' that mead!"
Shouldn't you return the Windcatcher to that nice, old mariner?
As you approach these gates, the doors are suddenly opened and a group of hill giants charge at you!

You also find a few letters from a man named Marath, addressed to the ogre chief, suggesting strategies for the war. The Overlords are often mentioned in these letters.

You find the remains of some marauder. From the looks of it, the poor sap was mauled by hungry wolves. Do you search the body?

A middle-aged man is sitting on the porch of his house, smoking a pipe. Visibly preoccupied by something, you decide to ask him why. "It's me brother, good people", the man replies, chagrined. "He lives in Coral Towers, ta island-city south of here".

leave here since the fishing is great right now, and me have to net all me can before ta season is over". Shaking his head in resignation, the fisherman smokes his pipe.
Do you offer to help him?

Wishing the fisherman good luck, you move on. "Safe journeys and safer returns, good people", the man tells you as you walk away. You can't help but feel a twinge of guilt at not offering to help him.

The fisherman's face becomes lit with joy and hope at your offer: "Truly, ye are kind and trusting folks! Me name's Daleck!", he exclaims as he shakes your hand. "All ye need ta do is ta give me brother this bag of money, which holds ta  ...
amount he has ta pay fer ta fine. His house is right next ta the Harbor Master's building; just tell him ye talked ta me. Thank ye again, good people!"
With the money bag in hand, you leave. "Safe journeys and safer returns!", Daleck shouts with relief, in goodbye.
You see the fisherman busy about at inspecting his fishnets; recognizing you, he waves. Do you offer to help him and his brother?

You come upon a clearing of grassland within the mountains. You see countless bodies of humanoids that are littering the area. The stench of decaying corpses assault you, making you nauseous. There must have been a great battle here, a while back.
This looks like some monument carved out of marble dedicated to a famous knight of the Flame by the name of Jasper Flameheart. The monument is old and worn out.

Your search reveals a sliding slab of marble behind the monument. Opening it, you see a rusty ladder of steel going down; from the smell of things, this must lead to the sewers under Tanirith. Do you go down?
You get out of the sewers.

The door to this room is in shambles. Looking in, you see that some of Tanirith's unfortunate beggars use this place as shelter; in fact, a few of them are sleeping or taking a rest at this moment. You are certain that you could sleep safely here.
You wake up in a startle, realizing that one of the beggars has scampered away with some of your valuables!

The walls around these stairs are covered with watery leaks and dripples. A faint rumble of moving water is heard beyond the walls. You deduce that these stairs lead to an underground passage beneath a river which runs through Tanirith.
This iron door is hopelessly jammed, having accumulated centuries of grime and rust on itself.

From the height of these double doors of reinforced (but very old) steel, you assume that you are entering the ruins of some small castle. You notice that not much of it remains after so many centuries under the earth and as part of Tanirith's sewers.
These crumbled stairs are useless since they are half-buried as well.
This looks like the ruins of some temple.  Most of it is buried under tons of soil and dirt; it is also flooded with sewer water.
Creatures inhabiting the sewers attack you, eyeing you as food!
Marauders lurking within the sewers make the jump on you!
From the looks of it, this must have been a granary or food storage area. After centuries of rot and scavenger pilfering, it is no surprise that nothing edible remains.
Most of these old bottles of wine and spirit are broken. However, a few of them are intact along with their aged (and thus better tasting) contents.
This looks like a ruined watch-tower.
You come upon a rusting trap door of steel. Someone must have put it there, but for what reason? In any case, it is hoplessly jammed.

You surprise some strangely garbed men in the middle of a conversation; for all intents and purposes, they look like monks. "Intruders!" one of them shouts. "Kill them! No one must know of our presence!" another yells. Immediately, they attack!
You wonder who were those men and what they were doing lurking around the sewers ...
Upon you approach, men dressed like monks rush to you and attack!
This door looks quite new and must have been installed here recently. The question now is: who did that, and why?
This would appear to be the rubbles of a magic shop.
This old, rotting chest holds nothing but rotten rags and other useless pieces of (old) clothing.
As you were searching, you find that the chest has a false bottom! Removing it, you uncover -to your amazement- a few items that have survived the centuries!
With the help of your spell, you find a concealed button at the base of this old, worn out altar or marble. Do you press this button?
A small compartment next to the button opens, revealing very interesting items which must have been hidden there ages ago!
The floor of this ancient corridor is filled with deep pits.  Looks like you have no choice but to turn back.
This pit is filled with an acid-like substance.
You stumble upon a band of marauders who are using this abandoned room as their hideout!
This is a stash of stolen riches accumulated by the marauders.
You find some foodstuffs stored here by the marauders.
Alerted by the raucus you have caused, a band of marauders charge at you from further down of the corridor!
The basement to which this opening leads is filled with sewer waters.
You disturb some of the sewers' occupants!
A huge, rusting but sturdy iron grid bars the way; it is also locked.
But with the help of the sewer key, you unlock the iron grid and are able to lift it open!

You surprise a man living in this secret room. From his attire, he looks like a priest. "I am Robbard, speaker for Lharishar, Goddess of life. My mission here is to help the poor folks who must take shelter in these sewers; I provide them with food ...
