and comfort, both physical and spiritual. Why have you come here?"  After assuring him of your good intentions, the priest of Lharishar relaxes his stand. "Noble adventurers, eh?" he smiles. "I have come to suspect that a dark and dangerous cult has ...

taken refuge within the sewers. I have attempted to uncover their location, but so far I only know that they hide in the eastern parts of the sewers. However, to get there, one must use the passage just north-east of here; but it is blocked ...

by a huge iron grid. But I suspect that a band of marauders, who have established a hideout south-east of here in the sewers, may possess a key which unlocks the iron grid ..." Thanking him for his help, you leave. "Come back if you are in need ...
of healing!" Robbard tells you as you leave.
You find Robbard working on plans for bringing more food to the sewers' beggars.  Rising up to greet you, he smiles warmly: "How may I help you, noble adventurers?"
You find Robbard working on the next spiritual sermon he intends to give to the sewers' beggars. Rising to greet you, he smiles warmly: "How may I help you, noble adventurers?"
You find Robbard working on new plans to bring more warm blankets for the sewers' beggars. Rising to greet you, he smiles warmly: "How may I help you, noble adventurers?"

You find Robbard quite busy at healing and curing homeless children, men, and women.  Greeting you, he smiles apologetically: "Could you come back later, noble adventurers? I will be happy to provide you with assistance then."  Resigned, you leave.
You hear a strange, slimy sound coming from the north-western end of this room.
This gaping pit is now free of slimes.
You come upon a part of the sewers which is made up from the ruins of an older incarnation of Tanirith. Not surprisingly, what little of those ruins that is left are moldy and crumbling.
The tormented spirits of dead guards of this lost castle rise to attack you!
The water here begins to run depper; from the smell of it, you know this tunnel opens into the sea.
These stairs lead down to a tunnel under the sewers and which was constructed recently. Do you take these stairs?
You stumble upon a group of those mysterious monks; obviously, they were in some sort or prayer and chanting session, and your interruption angers them to no end!
You sail right in the path of a pirate ship!!!
A pirate ship maneuvers to block your way!!!
This pirate ship is achored and currently unmanned.
This is the compound of a Pirate Lord and his followers; upon your approach, they rush out to "greet" you!
After the battle, you rummage through the compound and manage to find the Pirate Lord's stash of ill-gotten goods!
Already unhappy at having to waste their time in this compound, the pirates within are all too eager to vent their frustration on you!
Pirates from this watch-tower climb down in a rush to attack you!
As you approach this mansion, a score of pirates rush out to defend the stronghold of their Pirate Queen!

"I'm Nurale Darkstome, undisputed Pirate Queen!", a tall, beautiful woman dressed in armor announces after the battle. You see that she is standing outside the mansion, surrounded by Lords, captains, and pirates; of course, their weapons are drawn ...

"I don't know who ye dogs are", Nurale continues, "but I know  -through my spies-  that Pyre has sent you: I'll be happy to return yer severed heads to him!"  Immediately, the Pirate Queen yells the command to attack, then joins the fray in turn!

Panting and tired from such a battle, and hearing numerous other pirates scrambling within the compound, you decide it best to leave for now. Just as you gather yourselves, you notice a scroll hanging from Nurale's belt. Picking it up, you read it:

"Dear Nurale; you have proven yourself quite efficient at disrupting the trading sea lanes, and the Overlords are extremely pleased. Back on land, all is going well also; however, things in Sparklestone are slow to come to fruition. Perhaps a meeting ...

of us all is required to "convince" our collegue in Sparklestone to accelerate his part of the Overlords' plan? Let me know what you think of this.  Also, if you would be kind enough to speak with our friend in Coral Towers about his overzealous ...
despotism? I would greatly appreciate it. Continued success! Signed: A.D.".
The Pirate Queen's mansion lies in rubbles, most likely as a consequence of the intense struggle for power between the pirate factions.

"Ill met, usurper!" Halem retorts. "Ye?!?" exclaims Nurale, obviously surprised to see the former Pirate King. "But ye were supposed to be rotting on Tarterys Island!" Halem laughs in response: "Thanks to these lads, I'm here to return the favor!"
Immediately, the Pirate Queen orders her followers to attack, then joins the fray!
You notice then that different pirate factions have begun to fight each other. Not surprisingly, you loose sight of Halem amidst the chaos of this renewed strife.

Six towering, foul smelling brutes block your way: "No one's allowed upstairs" snarls the biggest of the six. "Ya better turn around, ya vermin, or else!" adds another. To emphasize this point, all six cross their huge arms over their wide chests.

At first taken aback by the fact that you know the secret password, the bullies begin to scrutinize each of you in turn. Finally, the largest one speaks: "Ya look like ta real thing, so gowon ... let Halem himself decide whay ta do with ya".
As his associates part, the largest bully jerks his thumb toward the stairs, motionning you to go ahead. Daneel then tugs at you, winking and smiling with satisfaction.
Expecting such a reaction on your part, the bullies attack just as you make your move!!!

One of the bullies then whispers something to the largest one, who then looks at you in detatched surprise. "So, yer ta ones that gave a licking ta some of our boys earlier, eh?" he snarls. You remain silent.
After a moment of thought, he then nods: "Well enough; we've need of more arms in here. So gowon upstairs an' let Halem himself decide yer worth ta him and our gang".
As his associates part, the largest bully jerks his thumb toward the stairs, motionning you to go on.
Bullies on watch nod at you.

More bullies bar your way. "So, ya wanna join us, eh?" asks one of them. You nod. "Well then, go see Halem, our boss," he replies, "just on yer right, go through ta door". The bullies part at that and let you pass.
"We're under attack!!!" bullies on watch shout, at your approach. Immediately, they make the jump on you as others come to help them!

A large man rushes in, accompanied by more bullies. He appears to be their leader. "Ye will pay fer yer outrage, ye dogs, or me name ain't Halem El-Yessef!"  With a battle cry, Halem and his remaining bullies attack!
This door is locked.

As you attempt to run away, you are quickly overwhelmed. Bound and gagged, Halem El-Yessef stands proudly before you: "Dog fools! Yer lucky we be not on me ship, cuz then me would have ye fed to ta sharks!" At Halem's silent order, his men finish you.

To your surprise, prison guards bar your way. You notice that more soldiers are keeping the other prisoners along the walls of the prison, to prevent any rioting. The prison commander walks up to you: "I've heard that ye have defeated Halem", he mumbles.

Proudly, you nod. The commander then smiles: "You don't know how relieved I am! Halem's been threatening me to use his spies to assassinate my family if I didn't let him do as he pleases ... But now that he is dead, I am free to take control of ...

Tarterys again, and better the conditions of the prisoners. As gratitude, I grant you a pardon as is allowed by the powers invested in me by our Lord Paladine. Thank you again, brave ones". You are then given back you gear and sailed back to the city.

You enter a small dining room. At the table, a large, burly man is sitting and eating. You notice that he sports a long, thick, black moustache, and eye-patch, and crops his dark hair in a ponytail. While eating, he motions you to approach.
Guards block your way: "No aunathorized visits allowed on Tarterys Island!"

"Greetings, mateys!" the man says while swallowing another bite. "Me be Halem El-Yessef, ta one an' only true Pirate King! Me heard that ye deposed that usurping witch Nurale Darkstrome, an' fer that ye have me thanks!" He laughs.

"Me only wish is ta have been there to do ta deed meself! But now that she's dead, ta time fer me ta take back what's rightfully mine has come at last! So how about it, mateys? Will ye join me to break out of this forsaken hell hole?"
"Ye made yer choice, dogs! Boys!!! Take these fools!!!" Halem yells. Immediately, some of his bullies jump on you!
"Now it's me turn, fools!" snarls Halem, as he rushes in with his remaining bullies.

Halem grins at your response: "Glad to have ye on board, mateys! Go grab some food and some weapons, then meet me in front of the stairs!"  Halem then dismisses you with a wave of his hand while he takes another bite of his meal.
Halem is making final preparations with his gang of bullies. "Me have a make-shift key to open ta doors", he tells you as he grins evilly, "so ta guards won't even know what hit them!"
With a final nod, he gives the signal to storm down the stairs and run through the door!
As Halem, his gang, some prisonners and you charge through the doors, prison guards sound the alarm and scramble to meet all of you head on!!!
You leave the prison.
You enter the prison.
"Victory!!!" yells Halem amidst loud cheers from his gang and other prisonners. "Now, let us run through the prison gates and be free!!!" With a roar, all (including you) rush out of the prison.

As you all arrive at the gates, you see numerous prison guards waiting for your attack. The guards are lead by their commander, who steps forward to speak: "Halem El-Yessef! Ye have some nerve, ye scum! Not only have ye forced me to let ye do ...
as ye please by threatening to kill my familly through your spies, but you dare to lead a riot?!? Well I say to ye: no more! Guards, attack!!!!" As one, guards and prisonners rush to meet head on!
Considering what the commander has just said, do you change your mind and help the guards instead?
You change sides and help the commander and his guards!

After the battle, the commander walks up to you: "Ye have me thanks, strangers. Fer doing the right thing, I grant ye a pardon according to the powers invested in me by our Lord Paladine". You are then given back your gear and sailed back to the city.
You join the fray against the guards!

Halem is jubilant: "We've done it, me mateys!!! We be free!!!" Amidst the roaring cheers, he then turns to you: "Ye have me thanks! Take ta boat anchored at ta pier to go inland if ye want to; I've loyal shipmates waiting on ta other side of Tarterys".

Without further due, Halem disapears through the crowd of prisonners, who are now getting into the buisiness of pillaging the place or fighting with each other. Witnessing this chaos, you wonder if you did the right thing.
The prison has been ransacked and put to the torch. Not much is left.
Tarterys castle has been ransacked and torched by the rioting prisonners. A few of them seem to have taken residence in the ruins.
With a few prisonners, you easily commandeer this small ship and sail back to the main land.
Considering your participation in the fall of Tarterys Island, you decide it best not to pass through Tanirith's gates should you be recognized ...

"Greetings, mateys!" says the man while swallowing another bite. "Me be Halem El-Yessef,  ta one and only true Pirate King! That is, until me was deposed by that witch Nurale Darkstrome, with ta help of some foul sorcerers who call themselves Overlords".

After another bite from his meal, Halem goes on: "Now, me heard ye roughed around some of me boys, eh?" You nod. "Me be impressed!" Halem replies, smilling. "In fact, ye don't look like ruffians at all, but more like adventurers, eh?" You nod again.

"Good!" replies Halem. "I've need of boys like ye to help me take back me rightful crown as Pirate King. So here's ta deal: me help ye get out of here, an' I tag along with ye until we reach ta Pirate islands. Deal?"

"There ye are!" whispers Halem. You then notice that everyone of his bullies is fast asleep, snoring loudly. "Me gave them a swig of me whiskey filled with sleeping potion" Halem explains, with a chuckle. "Me like them boys, but they wouldn't be ...

very useful ta me or ye in ta outside world. So here's ta plan: pirates loyal to me have made a secret tunnel in the mountain behind ta prison, an' they be waiting fer me in a stolen boat on ta other side of ta island. There, they will sail us back ...

to ta mainland. That'll be me part of ta bargain. Yer part will be ta find a way ta get to Pirate Isles ... an' don't ye worry about me: disguising be an art fer me!" You had noticed his change in hair style (now cropped), lack of a mustache ...
and even the loss of his eye-patch. With a mischievous wink from Halem, you follow him through a secret passage underneath the prison, leading you right to the mountain.
Halem El-Yessef has joined your party. Check out the Allies Menu.

You approach a small ship anchored by the shores of Tarterys Island. "Ahoy, there!" shouts Halem. "Ta King is back! What say you?" You then hear a voice coming from the ship: "We say: an' about time!" Grinning, Halem climbs aboard as he is greeted ...

by pirates still loyal to him. After you finally get on board as well, the ship lifts its sails and speedily bring you to the mainland, unseen. The pirates then sail on, most likely on an errand given to them by Halem.
"Me did me part" Halem tells you with a wink, "now ye do yours".  He then hands you a map: "These are ta Pirate Isles; ye must find a way ta get there". With a nod, you all get on your way.

"Hey, you!" shout a guard. You notice many others behind him, sitting at tables and enjoying a meal. "Yer not authorized ta be here!" You are promptly escorted out. "Be happy we don't lock ye in!" the guard shouts, in parting.

Guards block your way to Castle Tarterys. "No one's allowed here, and even less in the premises of the prison!" shouts one of the guards. You are then promptly escorted out. "And be happy that we don't lock ye in!" shouts the guard, in parting.
Guards block your way. "Ye going to the mainland?" one of them asks.
The guards part and let you board the ship. After a few hours' sail, you disembark in Tanirith.
You come upon a small boat anchored near the shore of this bay. You notice suspicious-looking men on board.  Do you investigate?
As you approach, you realize that these men are pirates. Upon seeing you, they attack!
With the boat on fire and starting to sink, you quickly get off and back to the shore. You wonder why these pirates were here and what they were plotting to do ...
As you enter this ruined house, a ghostly form appears out of thin air to block your way: "Begone, intruders!" the ghost tells you with its cavernous voice.  Do you turn around and leave?
At your refusal to leave, the ghost attacks!
You find a half-buried treasure. This must have belonged to the ghost, whoever he was.
However, you notice steel doors up ahead; these appear lto be some brand new addition to the place. You wonder who did this, and why ...
You find something interesting hidden under the bed.
However, some monks are busy here cooking food for their bethren: upon your intrusion, they attack!
However, numerous monks are currently eating here and are outraged by your intrusion!
Monks that were busy cooking for their bethren have been alerted by your fracas in the dinning room, and are therefore ready to meet you head on!
Monks that were eating here have been roused by the battle outside of the dinning room, and are therefore eager and ready to meet you head on!
This room is occupied by several cultist monks. Needless to say, they are quite upset by your intrusion into their private quarters.
This thick door of steel is locked.

This door of steel is triple locked; you get the feeling that you would need a special key to open it. Just as you are about to leave, you hear faint moans from numerous people: it would appear that the cultist monks keep prisonners for some reason ...
With the help of the skull key, you unlock this door.

You are shocked to find all kinds of people: men, women, children, peasants, vagrants, etc.  All of them show the signs of undernourishment and dehydration. One of them, who looks like a sailor, approaches you: "Thanks fer delivering us, good ...

strangers. These strange monks have kidnapped each and everyone of us; they make us weak, them somehow mess with our minds in order to make us join them. I tell ye, they aim to overtake Tanirith this way!" As the strongest lead the weakest out ...
of the sewers, you indicate to them where to find the exit.  Warching them walk slowly away, you are now convinced that this cult of monks is definitively up to no good.
As you approach this huge door of steel, numerous monks rush out to attack you! "More converts!" one of them yells. "Get them!" another one shouts.

You appear to have ended up in a lower level of Tanirith's sewers. You can deduce that you are still within the ruins of yet another older incarnation of the city. However, these parts have been renovated and cleared of water.
You nearly bump into monk cultists. "Intruders!" one of the exclaims. "Get them for conversion!" another one orders.
This part of the lower sewers has been blocked off; the cultists must have done this for defense purposes.
You find yourselves within an old, moldy secret room. You are certain that you could rest safely here.
You are in a dormatory, filled with beds.
You enter the renovated ruins of an old temple.
No one seems about at the present time.
"Get these intruders!" orders the monk that was presiding the prayer session. "We'll bring their heads to our Holy Master!"

You come upon an altar made of marble. It is carved with numerous, intricate symbols, the meaning of which you can not fathom. On the altar, you find a large book entitled "The Glory of the Mind Lords of Lankharh". Sifting through it quickly, you ...
understand that this book tells the story of powerful beings with incredible mind powers, and who used to rule as gods over a fabled empire known as Lankharh some ten millennia past.
The book also prophecises that the lost children of Lankharh will bring about the return of the Mind Lords, who will then claim ultimate rulership over the world entire.
While searching further, you find a secret compartment on the side of the altar. Opening it, you find something of interest.

You enter a room filled with chests of coins, gems and other valuable items. This must be then the Cult's treasure trove ... But before you can sift through the Cult's accumulated wealth, you must first get passed it's guardians.
The Cult's accumulated wealth is yours for the taking!
This corridor is hopelessly blocked by tons of rubble.
Monks on watch duty attack you the moment you open this door!
You disturb a couple of high-ranking cultists.
You stumble upon a group of high-ranking monks in conference with a man that can only be their leader. At your intrusion, they rise up to attack you. "Protect our Holy Master!" one of them shouts.

As you attempt to flee for your lives, you are quickly overwhelmed. The man the monks referred to as their master comes forth: "I am Herdalth, Holy Master of Lankharh" he announces to you solemly. "Your intrusion into our affairs warrants you death".
The monks then deliver their sentence on you.
The man the monks referred to a their Holy Master now faces you. He is surrounded by mysterious warriors and other monks, most likely his personal guards. With a nod from him, they attack!
You enter the Holy Master's private quarters.
You leave the private quarters of the Holy Master.
Your search reveals a makeshift book of wood which is tied to a leather string. Do you pull on the book?

You approach this strange glowing globe, a communication device which is becoming familiar to you. Immediately, the features of the lady Overlord begin to take shape within the device. You are unable to stop yourselves from grinning slyly as  ...

she obviously struggles to keep her calm and composure upon seeing you. "We meet yet again" she intones, her voice low and icy. "I have no time to waste with fools such as you; but to be polite, I would be remiss if I did not send proper greetings ...

so I will let servants of ours do that". She then grins evilly: "Fare you well". Suddenly, the Overlord's image dissipates within a bright, pulsating light; in an instant, warriors appear and attack you!
This area appears to be in the process of being renovated by the cultists, as attested by walls recently cleaned and repaired, as well by the humidity and water patches on the floors.
To your surprise, you find Naryl Dragonstone bound and gagged. She has been badly beaten as well.  Without any hesitation, you free her from her bonds and heal her as best you can.

"My thanks again, good adventurers" Naryl finally replies as she regains her strength. "I was investigating this cult, since I am certain that they are in league with the Overlords ... But they found me out, as you could plainly see".

She sighs. "Clearly, I cannot fight the Overlords alone. Since you and I are obviously on the same path, I would like very much to join you". She then looks at you with expectation. Do you accept Naryl into your company?
Naryl smiles: "I am happy for that. Let me gather my gear, and then rid Tanirith of this foul cult!"  Naryl Dragonstone has joined your party; check out the Allies Menu.
To your surprise, you find Naryl Dragonstone  -whom you had met earlier-  fighting for her life against cultist monks. Do you help her?
To your surprise, you find your friend Naryl Dragonstone fighting against a determined group of cultist monks. With your best battle cry, you jump into the fray to help her!

After the battle, Naryl happily clasps your hands. "My friends! " she exclaims, smiling, "You are out of Tarterys, and just in time at that!"  Preferring not to talk about Tarterys, you laugh and begin to tell her about what you have found so far.
To your surprise, you find your friend Jhalor Fireblade fighting for his life against a group of determined cultist monks. With your best battle cry, you join the fray to help him!

After the battle, Jhalor come to you smiling, happily clasping your hands: "My friends! You are out of Tarterys, and just in time to save my behind!" Not wishing to talk about Tarterys, you laugh then tell him about what you have found so far.
Shaking her head slowly in disapointment, Naryl silently gathers her gear and walks away. You get the weird feeling that you and her will never meet again ...
You walk away, leaving Naryl to her own devices. You can't help but feel deeply ashamed.
You find the body of Naryl Dragonstone. She is now beyond help.
However, the monks who defeated her are still here, and now they turn their bloodlusted attention to you!

Among useless bureaucratic paperwork (food supplies, weapon's inventory, etc.), you find on this desk four interesting items. The first is a ledger of names of people who have been converted; it appears that the cult's method was to kidnap people ...

then weaken them by starvation so that the Holy Master could use his mind powers to convert them. The second item is a letter of correspondence: "Dear G.T.; My Overlord Masters are pleased with your successfull trade-disrupting activities in Tanirith.

However, they still express misgivings about your agent in Sparklestone, especially his failure so far to take complete control of the town. It would be best that you bespeak him of this on the Overlords' behalf; however, make it clear that this be ...

his last chance; Sincerely yours, signed: Herdalth".  The third item is another letter: "Dear S.F.; I hope you are satisfied with the subservience of those last four knights I converted for you.  However, I would prefer that you weed out those you ...

feel unsuitable to our cause rather than send them forcefully to me so that I may influence their minds in our favor; indeed, such work is taxing, and I must keep by strenght for our own conversions here.  I thank you for your consideration of this ...

Sincerely yours; signed: Herdalth". The last item is yet another letter: "Dear Lhassa; Our Masters praise your work accomplished so far; they would like an estimate as to when Tanirith's vineyards will be totally eradicated. Also, could you impress ...

upon your troll servants that they should not hurt or maim my envoys? They all but killed my last one, a cabalist whom I found very capable and useful. This time, I am sending one of our psi-warriors, to be on the safe side ...
Keep up the good work; The Will of the Mind Lords be done. Signed: Herdalth".  You decide to keep those letters you feel would be most useful to you, along with some blank parchment sheets.

You come upon a huge portal of bronze, silver, and steel. The massive double doors are etched with runes and symbols you cannot decipher. This artifact must be quite ancient. Strangely, you find no opening mechanism, lock to pick, or a handle to pull.

Suddenly, you feel a throbbing in your pack sack. Opening it, you see the Writ of the Ancients glowing. Taking it out, the book pulses with a white light brighter and brighter, until a beam shoots forth from it, striking the portal like lightning.
Getting back your senses after being thrown back by the shock wave, you are awed at seeing the portal slowly opening its massive doors, revealing stairs going down.
Do you take the stairs through the opened portal?
After a few moments, the portal closes itself.
The portal closes behind you as you cross it.
You appear to have ended up in what used to be the basement and dungeons of this ruined castle.
This place appears to have been an armory centuries ago.
From the looks of it, this room used to be a pantry for clothes, drapes and other articles of the like.
From the looks of it, this room was once used for storage of all sorts of things.
This room contains many chests. However, each and everyone of them appear to have been emptied of their precious contents long ago, most probably when the castle's occupants left the place.
You enter what can only be an ancient torture room. Numerous torture inflicting devices are about, along with the skeletons of some of those who have died in such a terrible place.
Suddenly, some of the skeletons rise to take revenge on the living!!!
You find here a rack holding numerous (and frightening) torture devices; of course, all of these are rusted and (thankfully) useless.
Interestingly, your search reveals that the rack can be easily pushed aside. Having done so, you are quite certain that a secret door must be within the wall facing you!
You have entered the jailing area of the ruined castle's dungeons.
You find what can only be the castle's secret treasure, hidden here and untouched for centuries!
You find yourselves inside a very old temple; to which god, you cannot guess. Surprisingly, the temple appears to be quiet well preserved, despite centuries of being buried underground.
This must have been the hall of worship and prayers. The place is filled with benches, columns, and statues (the faces of which are not recognizable anymore).
Some of the statues animate to defend the temple!!!
The statue shatters in hundreds of razor-sharp shards!
You come upon a huge altar made of solid gold-silver and encrusted with numerous precious stones. However, there is a plainly visible magical shield which surrounds the altar.
You find a strange book stool made of platinum and surrounded by a magic aura.
Do you put the Writ of the Ancients on the book stool?
A wall moves.
Do you reclaim the Writ of the Ancients?
You come upon a three-dimensional, marble bas-relief bearing the likeliness of the head and torso of a wise man. Upon your approach, its eyes begin to pulse with a bright blue light.

"I AM THE ORACLE OF VAANYA" the figure announces, its eery voice echoing within the room. "FOR CENTURIES HAS THIS HOLY TEMPLE BEEN ABANDONNED;  SADLY, ITS CARE-TAKERS DID NOT HAVE THE TIME TO RELEASE MY ESSENCE FROM THIS ICON, SO THAT I MAY JOIN ...

BACK WITH MY HOLY MASTER'S GLORY. SO THUS I HAVE BEEN AWAITING THE COMING OF BRAVE AND NOBLE MORTALS SUCH AS YOU: FIND THE CROWN OF POWER AND ADORN MY ICON'S HEAD WITH IT; BEING RELEASED, I SHALL TELL YOU OF YOUR FUTURE BEFORE I DEPART. THE CROWN CAN ...

BE FOUND UNDERNEATH AN OLD, RUINED CASTLE LYING IN THE SEWERS OF TANIRITH. SO GO NOBLE ONES, AND FIND THIS WHICH SHALL FREE ME AT THE LAST, AND MY GRATITUDE SHALL BE YOURS".  The icon then goes silent.
Do you put the Crown of Power upon the head of the icon to free the Oracle?

The moment the crown is upon the icon, the whole bas-relief begins to shudder and gradually change form. With a final flash of blue light, you now find a towering demon Prince standing before you, grinning with arrogance and evil.

"Thank you for delivering me from this bondage, mortals" the demon exclaims. "I am Kheh'Drackh, Lord of the 222nd layer of the Abyss. Centuries ago, I was imprisoned here by priests of Codan, God of Law and Order. I promised you to tell of your ...
future, and I always keep my promises. So here it is, mortals: each and everyone shall die by my hands!!!" Grinning evilly, Kheh'Drackh launches his attack!
After the battle, there is no trace left of the bas-relief, nor of the Crown of Power.
Kheh'Drackh summons demons to his side!
You have found the temple's treasure, which has remained undisturbed for centuries!
The sign above this door reads: Maroon's Eating Halls. It appears to be filled with people. Do you enter?
You end up in Tanirith's sewers.

You are surprised to find Braggan Stoneheart, enjoying a large and tasty meal. "Me friends!" he exclaims. "Ye are back from Tarterys finally! Come, let's celebrate!" With laughter and good ribbing,  Braggan rejoins your party.

You are surprised to find Helm Goldfinger enjoying a hearty meal. "Me friends!" he exclaims. "Ye be back from Tarterys! This calls for a celebration!" Amidst laughter and camaraderie, Helm rejoins your party.

You are surprised to see Runelore Magius quietly enjoying a meal. "My friends! So, you are back from Tarterys safe and sound? That is good". With smiles and clasps of hands, Runelore rejoins your party.

You overhear a conversation: "I tell ye; strange monks walk the streets at night and kidnap good folks for whatever evil they want to do to them!" a woman exclaims. "Me thinks they hide in the sewers" another one adds. "I even heard some of them ...
use a secret door in these Eating Halls to get to their hideout!" The first woman is shocked: "Does Maroon knows about this?"  The second woman shrugs in answer.

You come upon a large half-ogre dressed in a chef's outfit. From the food stains on the garment, this must be one of the cooks of the place. You notice that he keeps grinning with satisfaction while speaking with any patron he sees.

"Greetings!" the half-ogre exclaims at your approach. "Me name's Maroon; welcome to me Eating Halls!" You then discreetly confront Maroon about the secret passage. He seems genuinely afraid: "Please! Them strange monks have threatened me and ...

me family if we did not let them use that passage to ta sewers!" Convinced by his sincerity, you promise Maroon not to let word of this for his safety and that of his family. "Thank ye, noble adventurers! Here: have a meal on me house!"
"What would you like?"
"Excellent choice!"
Once seated, you do not wait long for your food and beverages. And what a feast you have: the meal is plenty and delicious, and the drinks are more than enough!
"That will be 10 golds each, so 60 golds total".
"That will be 15 golds each, so 90 golds total".
"That will be 5 golds each, so 30 golds total".
"That will be 20 golds each, so 120 golds total".
"Greetings!" the half-ogre exclaims at your approach. "Me Maroon, and welcome to me Eating Halls! Me have ta best food in all Tanirith! Ye want ta see me menu?"

Maroon is still walking from table to table, laughing with his patrons, making sure that they enjoy their meals. "Greetings again!" he exclaims upon seeing you. "Ye back fer some more of me good food, eh?" he says while winking. "Ye want ta see me menu?"
This is a kitchen. You see many cooks and wenches busy at making the meals and preparing the drinks. One of the wenches sees you, and hushers you politely out.
The sign above the doors reads: "The Sailor's Wharf". There seems to be plenty of people inside and, judging from the noise, mostly sailors and mariners. Do you enter?
A burly, sour bartender eyes you dryly. "Oy! Whot will ye have?"
From the corner of your eye, you swear you just saw someone "disapear" behind the north-eastern wall of the tavern.
The patrol leader collects the fines. "Now go back to your activities, and none of ye better stir up any more trouble or it's to Tarterys Island ye go!" The militia patrol then leaves.
"Ye again?" the patrol leader exclaims, with anger. "Ye were warned! Off to see a magistrate with you!" You are quickly seized and marched to the Hall of Justice.
"No money to pay or ye don't want to pay? Off with ye to see a magistrate, then!" You are then promptly escorted to the Hall of Justice.
and just. Therefore, I give you one more chance to pay the total of 150 gp in fines. Which one of you will pay?"

One of the militia soldiers then whispers in the leader's ear while eyeing you suspiciously. The leader suddenly turns around to you in obvious anger: "So! Ye would be ta ones who took part in ta destruction of Tarterys, eh?" Swallowing hard, you ...

remain silent. "There be a price fer yer lousy heads, ye know", the leader snarls as he draws his sword. His soldiers ready their weapons at the same time. With surprising swiftness, you are surrounded then forcibly taken to Tanirith's Hall of Justice.

The magistrate comes into the court: "Well, well, well! I know who you are!" he intones, barely controlling his anger. "The famous adventurers who were largely responsible for the fall of Tarterys! Fools! Your descriptions are all over Tanirith!"

"Unfortunate that you had to come back here and stir up trouble, eh? But then, I do get the pleasure of sentencing you to prison for the rest of your foolish lives! While we have only begun to reconstruct Tarterys, a small jail in our Justice Hall ...

will do just fine until we can transfer you. So I have judged, and so I have sentenced!" You are then stripped of your gear and thrown in a small cell. All the while, the magistrate's words keep echoing in your head: "Life in prison. Life in prison."
In the darkness of the damp cell, you find something.

The trap door on the ceiling of your cell is opened. The bright light hurts your eyes. A pack of food is dropped, then the trap door is closed and locked again. You wonder if you will be able to live the rest of your lives like that.

You find Runelore Magius, whom you had previously met in Wailsrond, enjoying a delicious meal. "We meet again", he says, smiling.  "I heard many good things about your recents exploits; I wish more than ever to join you!"
Runelore sighs. "Ah well, I had hoped, but ...." Shrugging, he goes back to his meal, eating silently. You walk away.
You then look aside to Naryl. Although she is eyeing Runelore suspiciously still, she does not voice any more concerns about him.
The sign above the door of this store reads: "The Mariner's Toolbox". Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this store reads: "Dungarh's Leatherworks". Do you enter?
A sign on the door of this store reads: "Thalya's Street Corner Shop". Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this shop reads: "Schaxam's Little Shop of Magics". Do you enter?
The sign above the door of this shop read: "Ephaestor's Weapons and Armors". Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this shop reads: "Nyressyl's Wondrous Wonders". Do you enter?
The sign above the door of this shop reads: "Lantharond's Forgeworks". Do you enter?
From the looks of things and the people going in and out, this looks like a central market. Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this shop reads: "Tanirith's Exotic Imports". Do you enter?
This looks like a bank. Do you enter?
The sign above the door of this store reads: "The Sailor's Deck". Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this shop reads:  "Jereph's Shop of Conveniances". Do you enter?
From the look and sound of things, this must be the city's central market. Do you go in?
The sign above the door of this shop reads: "Imported Arcane Wonders". Do you enter?
This shop looks like a general store. Do you enter?
The sign above the door of this shop reads: "Leatherwork Masters". Do you enter?
Guards behind a locked gate peer at you from a window slit: "This is private property! Begone!".
This is the Hall of Justice. You see many militia patrols going in and out of the huge building; occasionally, a patrol brings in some captured misfits or criminals.
This temple is dedicated to Codan, God of Law and Order. Do you enter?
This is a temple dedicated to Tyr, God of Chivalry and Justice. Do you enter?
This is the building of the High Council, the ruling body of Tanirith. Many officials and bureaucrats come in and out, going about their government business.
Knights of the Flame on watch here approach you: "Folks without proper authorization are not allowed here. Please circulate!".
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "The Captain's Inn". Do you enter?
"Come back soon!" the innkeeper bids you, in goodbye.

Just as you are about to go up these stairs, the innkeeper stops you: "Good gents! Only those who have rented a room may go to the first floor, since that's where the rooms are". Embarassed, you move away from the stairs.

"Welcome, good gents!" the innkeeper greets you. Our rooms are cozy and clean; our flat rate is 5 gp per person for one night, so that would be 30 golds total for you. Would you like to stay for the night?
The innkeeper takes you to your room. "Goodnight and good rest! Simply leave tomorrow morning; we will service the room then".
A sign hangs above the door of this establishment, reading: "Inn of the Sea Trader". Do you go in?
As you are about to open this door, the innkeeper stops you: "Goood people! This door leads to the rooms, and only those who have rented one may go there". Embarassed, you leave the door alone.
"Greetings!" the innkeeper says, smiling. "Welcome our Inn. Our rate is 10 golds per person per night, so that would be 60 golds total for you. Would you like a room for the night?"
This elevator goes down. Do you take it?
This elevator goes up. Do you take it?
In this mine cave, you notice that the far end connects to a natural tunnel complex within the rock.
Dark elves make the jump on you!
You find a shadow elf patrol camping here!
You find here the bodies of six dwarven miners. From the looks of things, they were attacked swiftly and with deadly accuracy.
As you approach this small outpost, shadow elves storm out to attack you!
It would appear that you have taken care of the shadow elf outpost responsible for the raids on the dwarven miners. But now, the question is: where did these shadow elves come from?
You find the shadow elves' small  treasure, which they had accumulated from their raids.

Dwarven miners run up to you. "Our thanks, noble strangers! Our brothers have been avenged from ta foul shadow elves! We'll close this new mine in any case, cuz it's now and forever cursed by what's happened there".

The dwarves then go to bury their fallen comrades. To your surprise, you find a stash of goods at your feet; looking around, you see a female dwarf nodding at you as she departs with the other dwarves.
This mine elevator has been demolished and is useless.

You see numerous dwarven miners coming your way, carrying many wounded of their bethren. "Shadow elves!" exclaims one of them. "These sons-of-orcs have been raiding us fer days now, but today they've killed our own! If only we knew where their ...
durn outpost is! We'll have to close this new mine, and it's a shame, cuz it was a good one!" The dwarves keep going, leaving you to wonder whether or not you should investigate.
Numerous dwarves are standing on these battlements. "Strangers aren't allowed here! Begone now!"
This is the cemetary of the Dwarven Halls.

Just as you get down, you have barely the time to see the dwarves destroying the elevator, as to close the mine. They must not have seen you. You jump out of the  doomed elevator, lucky to have remained unharmed through this dangerous situation.
You are certain that you could rest safely in this cave.
This temple is dedicated to Moradin, God of all dwarves. Do you enter?
This temple is dedicated to Tharask, God of Bravery in Battle and of Victory in Noble Causes. The dwarves call this god "Clodurin Battleaxe". Do you enter?

"I am a psi-knight of Keryndor, an isolated and secretive country on the continent of Anarym. My real name is Naryl Thezzat. Obviously, being a psi-knight, I have mental powers as befitted to all my people; however, I have chosen to serve my country ...

and to protect my people: hence, I am not a master of psionic powers as others, whom we call "psions", can become. Our people are direct descendants of the Lankharhans; since the fall of the empire of Lankharh, our forefathers chose to live in peace ...

and isolated from the world, since so many fear those of us who have psionic powers. I have come here to stop the Overlords, because they threaten to reveal us and shatter not only our peaceful existence, but that of the people of the Realmz as well."

"Being a psi-knight, and thus not a "true" psionicist like a psion, I require such a talisman to help me focus my mental powers and use them efficiently. Without it, my psionic powers would be weak if not impossible to access. However, such a ...

mental bond can also allow one to transfer one's essence (or spirit, or soul) into one's talisman upon death of the body, if one has the capacity and discipline to do so. And this is what I managed to do. I did this in the event of my death before ...

the Overlords would be stopped, so that I may still help trusted friends such as you in attempting to defeat their plans. In effect, you could view this as some kind of immortality or preservation of one's essence".

"The Overlords are of my people. Powerful psions, they've tired of our peaceful and secretive nature, and thus wish to establish a new psionic empire, akin to the fabled Lankharh Empire. Of course, we consider them insurgents and criminals. They ...

constitute what they call an "Inner Council" comprised of the nine most powerful psions of their ranks. The Overlords that we face are three members of this Inner Council. Although the specifics of their plans remain unknown, we know that part of ...

their goals is to establish a power base either through covert subversion and/or conquest, then bring about the return of the Mind Lords to lead them and their psionic followers into establishing what they call the "New Empire".

"The Lankharh people established an empire some 12 thousand years ago on the continent of Anarym. This was a "psionic" empire, since all Lankharhans were born with innate powers of the mind, or psionic powers. Also, the empire was ...

a peaceful one, growing only through willfull adherance of other countries or cities into the empire. There came a time when powerful psionic individuals rose to become Lords, Regents, Princes and Emperors of the Empire: those were aptly named ...

"Mind Lords", and they brought about a golden age for all citizens of the Empire. But with time and each generation, those who rose as Mind Lords became less and less sane, and increasingly bent on ruthlessness, enslavement and evil. They began wars ...

of conquest not only against peoples apart of the Empire, but as well against themselves, each attempting to control all of the Empire without opposition. Those dark times are known as the "War of the Mind Lords". As these wars brought about much ...

suffering for the Lankharhans and even more so for non-psionics, powerful magics and magic weapons were devised to combat the Mind Lords and their armies of psi-warriors. Some sane and good Mind Lords even helped, along with goodly principled Lankharans.

Eventually, the evil Mind Lords were defeated and killed, leaving the Empire of Lankharh ruined and fragmented in the wake of their madness. Thus ended the Fabled Lankharh Empire after 2000 years of existence".

"Kith Khanaan is revered to this day by my people. He was but a young teenager when, as a maturing Mind Lord, he joined the rebellion against the evil Mind Lords. After the War of the Mind Lords and in the wake of the fall of the Lankharh Empire ...

Kith Khanaan took it upon himself to assemble all Lankharhans and bring them to virgin lands, far removed from non-psionic peoples, to live in peace and tranquility. You see, the Lankharhans were beginning to be hunted down and persecuted because of  ...

their psionic nature, in retribution for all the horrors the Mind Lords and their servants had inflicted upon non-psionics. However tragic and terrible such a backlash was, Kith understood there was nothing to stop it, and so did the remaining ...

Lankharhan elders. So, they all followed Kith Khanaan to establish Keryndor, which is of course my country today. Being a Mind Lord, Kith was long-lived; he had recognized that a major flaw of the Mind Lord rulership was their long lives, which ...

eventually breeded contempt, arrogance and darkness of the heart. So Kith Khanaan ruled Keryndor but a few decades, then went away, leaving my ancestors to grow and prosper in peace, and by their own hands and minds. Our legends say that he first ...
explored all of Anarym, then eventually came to the Realmz to explore the rest of world and experience it. He somehow died here".

"The Mind Lords were the most powerful individuals among the psionic Lankharhans. Their mind powers almost equalled those of gods, and they could live for centuries. They rose to become the rulers of the Lankharh Empire. Because of too much in-breeding,

the successive generations of Mind Lords became increasingly unstable mentally, and began to thirst for utter domination of Anarym, of all non-psionics (whom they considered mongrels fit only to be slaves), and even of all Lankharhans. Thus, they had ...

become nothing short of evil monsters bent on conquest and destruction, and even began warring among themselves. In time, these Wars of the Mind Lords brought about their own fall and, alas, that of the Lankharh civilization as well."

Ptaraz the Conquerer was a ruthless, determined, and strategically brillant Warlord. He reaped much havok in the Realmz some seven hundred winters past, especially since he was helped by a powerful warlock named Tanira Arkanoch who, incidentally, was ...

his beloved lady and consort. It has always remained a mystery as to how two people could be so faithful, dedicated, and loving to each other, while being capable at the same time of continuously cause much evil and suffering upon others.

In any event, Ptaraz and Tanira eventually came to the Sword Lands in order to establish a forteress and a power base for their military endeavors. Ptaraz named his forteress Tanirith, in honor of his beloved lady Tanira.  In time, Ptaraz tired of ...

marching against other cities and kingdoms, and decided to found his own kingdom with Tanirith as its capital. He and Queen Tanira ruled nearly all of the Sword Lands through despotism and terror. Near the end of his reign, Ptaraz was struck down by ...

an incurable disease. Tanira endeavored to build a crypt befitting her beloved King. According to legends, Tanira buried Ptaraz there upon his death, then magically slew herself and their most trusted warriors, so that they may remain together within ...

the crypt while protected by their retinue, even in death. Accordingly, the crypt of Ptaraz is rumored to be patrolled by undead warriors, as well as by Ptaraz and Tanira themselves. To this day, the crypt lies just north-east of Tanirith.

Arvoranaan is a small halfling community just north-northeast of Tanirith. Founded some 200 years ago, it has always been under the protection of Tanirith through the Knights of the Flame. Lantharond is a city north of Tanirith, up along the coast.

Founded some 800 years ago, it was for a time part of the kingdom established by Ptaraz the conquerer. A century after Ptaraz' death, Lantharond finally regained its independance under the leadership of Golan Dragonheart, who then established the ...

Dragonheart Dynasty. To this day, this dynasty of kings and queens have ruled Lantharond; the current monarch is Vallar Dragonheart. The relations between Lantharond and Tanirith have always been strenuous at best, interceded with small-lived wars ...

between the two cities. However, for the last two decades, Lantharond and Tanirith have been at peace and allies. Unfortunately, relations between the cities have once again deteriorated of late, for reasons which remain unknown.

The continent of Anarym is a large land mass situated far east of here, across Ukkor's ocean. Not much is known of these lands, except fables and fabulations. Some speak of powerful Mage-Kings, others of terrifying monsters prowling everywhere, and ...

yet others who tell of godly avatars warring with each other. A year ago, an exploratory ship from Umaldyr arrived in Tanirith. Umaldyr is an island-nation located some one thousand leagues east of here and claims to be part of the continent of Anarym.
Since sea-trading between Tanirith and Umaldyr is barely three months in the going, we remain still pretty much in the dark about Umaldyr itself, as well as about Anarym.
This is the Great Library of the Dwarven Halls. Do you enter?

An old dwarf dressed in robes bows respectfully to you: "Greetings, Heroes of the Dwarven Halls. I am Aradan, Highkeeper of Lore. As you see, we collect many books from the Realmz; but most precious are our own history scrolls, which we keep safe ...

in the library's vaults, along with our holy scriptures. Because you are strangers, we cannot allow you to peruse these old and ancient documents; however, much knowledge us Keepers we absorb and retain".
"Being the Highkeeper, I above all Keepers of the library hold much knowledge about the past, both recent and ancient. What would you like to know?"

The Highkeeper then smirks: "Of course, during his life, Ptaraz always sought to find the Dwarven Halls in order to conquer us. Fortunately, he never found our city, although our people often had to battle with him and his army".

The Highkeeper smiles: "Strangely, this relates to the continent of Anarym; thousands of year ago, our people were fortunate to have met with a man named Kith Khanaan, who related this story to us as a warning". Coughing once, he goes on to speak:

The Highkeeper chuckles: "Of course, Anarym is essentially like the Realmz, although its has its own dangers and perils, and inhabitants have their own "flavors" and distinctiveness. We learned a good deal of the Anarym of some nine millennia ago ...

from a man named Kith Khanaan, who came to visit our people back then, so long ago. However, I doubt that any knowledge that we have of this Anarym-of-then is relevant today or even useful anymore, after such a long time".

Galduur Ironshield was the bravest and most noble warrior of the Dwarven Halls. He lived during the times of king Ptaraz, and often had to defend the Halls against the king's armies. In fact, Galduur despised Ptaraz so, he roamed the land of Ptaraz' ...

kingdom and clashed with patrols of Tanirith, always helping the poor folks that were being oppressed by the king. Eventually, Ptaraz died; so, Galduur then took upon himself to explore the Sword Lands and root out evil wherever he found it, in order ...

to destroy it. Many tales abound concerning Galduur's heroic deeds during those times, tales either from dwarves, gnomes, humans, halflings, and even elves. He somehow disapeared some six hundred winters past. Some say that he was killed by ...

ice giants lead by their king of then, the Mighty Darrock. Others claim that he crossed a magical portal that stranded him in the continent of Anarym, or worse in the Lower Planes. In any case, all that was left of him was his shield, which quickly ...

became a revered symbol for our people. Then seventy-five years ago, one of our own stole the shield to sell it for a fortune, and thus the shield was lost to us. As for the dwarf who stole it, it is said that he was cursed by Moradin to live the ...

rest of his life as a troglodyte, and thus never got to enjoy his ill-acquired fortune. But now, the saga of Galduur's shield is finally at its end, for you have brought it back to its rightfull place: our Dwarven Halls.

The Writ of the Ancients is a human holy relic; fables say that Codan and Myst themselves created this artifact. It is said to contain all the dreams of all humans that ever lived and all of those who live today; in fact, every human dream that ...

happens is instantly recorded within the Writ. Strangely, no one may read its pages, for such a mortal is sure to become insane. Fables say that Codan required such recordings of dreams from Myst in order to account accurately of her functions within ...

the pantheon of human gods. Throughout the millennia, stories abound concerning individuals who sought to possess or read this book-artifact; but the most interesting story is that the Writ serves as a key to any temple of Codan or Myst which has  ...

to be abandonned: hence, such temples are magically sealed and may be opened, somehow, only by the Writ. It is said that wherever or whenever a temple of Codan or Myst needs to be abandonned, the Writ magically leaves its current location and appears ...
at the temple that requires to be sealed. Not surprisingly, the current whereabouts of the Writ of the Ancients are unknown.

Kith Khanaan came to visit our people some nine thousand winters past. He claimed to be a simple explorer interested in meeting new folks and visiting interesting places. Of course, he turned out to be much more than that. He came to us while we were ...

defending ourselves against an army of invading shadow elves. To the amazement of our ancestors, Kith Khanaan broke the will of the invaders with but mere thoughts of his;  with simple gestures, he made weapons fly at our enemies and impale them; he ...

also smote them with strange energies that he called forth from within him; and so on. Our ancestors knew he was not a mage of any sort, for us dwarves always recognize magic when we see it: and his powers had nothing to do with magic. Some wondered ...

that perhaps he was a god, but he always denied that. He revealed that he had travelled far from his homeland on the continent of Anarym; in fact, many stories of this continent did Kith Khanaan share with our ancestors. We remember him for being ...

a true hero and dwarven-friend; but of anything else about him, he kept the secret as if he were afraid of his true nature, if not actually trying to run from it. In any case, he stayed with us but for a year, then wandered away for more heroic ...

adventures. Not much else is know about Kith Khanaan, except that his final resting place is rumored to be somewhere in the vicinity of the collapsed volcano which lies far north of the coastal city of Lantharond.
A dwarven Library Keeper prevents your passage: "This door leads to our sacred Vault, where our oldest and most precious documents are kept. Only us Keepers, or the Highkeeper, may go there".

This huge portal is made of wrought silver and gold, and etched with numerous dwarven runes. Huge runes read: "Heroe's Hall". A dwarven warrior on guard here nods at you: "Here you will find the final resting places of our heroes". Do you go in?
Somewhat to your disapointment, you see that this is a cemetary. The names on the tombstones do not even  mean anything to you.
The guard nods solemnly to you.
This tombstone bears the name of Galduur Ironshield. Strangely enough, their is no cairn and the stone is simply planted in the ground. You wonder if a body was buried here or not.
You enter the hill giant steading.
You find yourselves in a large hall, filled with food crates and weapon racks (holding weapons too large to be of any use or value). Long tables for eating and large chairs complete the scene.
Some hill giants are here, eating. Upon your entrance, they turn around to you: "Hey! Whot are ye doin' here?" yells one giant. "They're intruders, ye fool!" adds another. "Git them!!!!"
You run into hill giants!
You enter a dormitory where numerous giants are taking a rest!
You search the room thoroughly and manage to scrounge up a few valuables.
You enter the steading's kitchen, surprising some hill giants busy at cooking food for their kinsfolk and their king.
Hill giants are here stocking up the room. At your intrusion, they attack!

To your dismay, your entrance interrupts a war council within this large conference room. The King of hill giants is there, flanked by huge mountain giant bodyguards, and surrounded by his best warriors. You barely have time to notice ...
a few ogre and orc envoys, when all of them ready their weapons. "Me dunno who ye are" snarls the hill giant king, "but ye shall regret ye ever set foot in me steading!"

On this table, you find numerous battle plans, raiding schedules, and the likes. You are surprised by the plannification involved in these plans: hill giants are not known usually for their strategic skills ...
The hill giant king's favorite pets are guarding this room!

On this desk, you find numerous letters from a man named "Merath", providing suggestions for battle plans, raiding schedules, and battle tactics. In this correspondence, you notice numerous references to the Overlords, not surprisingly.
Looks like you have found the secret stash of the hill giant king!
You enter the hill giant king's bedchamber.
Ogre warriors on guard use the "attack first, ask questions later" method upon your approach!
Obviously, this building is a compound inhabited by ogres. Do you enter this compound?

You enter a large hall filled with tables, chairs and weapon racks (mostly old clubs, axes, and spears). The place is quite dirty. To your dismay, it would appear that you have interrupted some kind of war council: indeed, you spot what can only be ...

the ogre Chief surrounded by his best warriors and discussing with some hill giant and orc envoys. Upon your entrance, all stop speaking to look at you. "Me dunno who ye are" snarls the ogre chief, "but ye'll pay fer intruding in me house uninvited!".
Some of the remaing ogre warriors were lying in wait here to ambush you!
You enter the ogre chief's room.
This chest contains the personal stash of the ogre chief.

On this table, you find battle plans, raiding schedules, and the likes. You also find numerous letters from a man named Merath, encouraging the ogres to keep the alliance with the hill giant and the orcs, as well as suggesting battle tactics ...
and other related topics relevant to the goals of conquering the gnomes and the dwarves. Not surprisingly, the Overlords are often mentionned in these letters.
A large wrought bronze sign hangs above these gates: "Tanirith-South Port 2". Numerous merchants, sailors, onlookers, fishemen, mariners and harbor workers pass through the gates.
A huge wrought bronze sign hangs above these gates: "Tanirith-South Port 1". Busy folks of all kind pass through the gates.
A huge wrought bronze sign hangs above these gates: "Tanirith-East Port". Numerous busy folks of all sorts pass through the gates.
A sign above the doors of this building reads: "Harbor Master-Central Port West". You see numerous merchants, fishemen, harbor workers and sailors about.
A sign above the doors of this building reads: "Harbor Master-Central Port East". Many harbor workers, merchants, fishermen and sailors come in and out of the place.
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master-South Port". Many sailors, ship captains, travelers and merchants go in and out of the place. Do you enter?

You walk up to a series of kiosks, each one with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets". You go to the one marked "Wailsrond". There, a lady smiles at you: "Fare to Wailsrond? That's 200 golds total". Who will pay?
"Thank you. Go to South Port-1, very last pier to the west. The boat is right at the end of the pier. Departures are at every hour; have a good sail".

You walk to a series of kiosks, each one with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets" and the destination. You go to the one marked "Coral Towers". There, a lady smiles: "Fare to the Towers? That's 1000 golds total". Who will pay?
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master-East Port". Many sailors, ship captains, travelers and merchants go in and out of the place. Do you enter?
"I'm sorry, but due to the current problems in relations between Tanirith and Lantharond, all trips to this city are suspended until further notice".
"Thank you. Go to the East Port, the very last pier to the south. Your boat is anchored at the end of this pier. Departures are at every hour. Have a good sail."

You walk up to a series of kiosks, each one with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets" and a destination. You go to the one marked "Lantharond". There, a lady smiles at you: "Trip to Lantharond? That's 600 golds total". Who will pay?

As you approach the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have ye a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon". After handing your tickets, you are shown to your cabin: "The ship sets sails in 5 minutes; the trip will last about two days".

You enter the part of Tanirith known as "High Town", where the richest people of Tanirith live, including the rulers of the city. You notice numerous guards eyeing you suspiciously, but you are otherwise left alone.
From the looks and sounds of things, this must be some kind of giant bazaar, where all sorts of things are sold. Do you enter?

You see a man lovingly toiling over his fields of vineyards. "Greetings, strangers" he bids you. "Me thinks ye'll have to wait awhile more before ye get to taste this year's wine make, cuz were still growing it!" He tells you with a wink.

Then he grows more serious: "Then again, t'is may be the last year for any vintage, what with those vineyards dying mysteriously north of here, and this strange death being somehow contagious". He shakes his head in resignation: "Well, might as well ...
enjoy this last one and make it the best vintage ever!" With final good wishes, you leave.

You see an old man sitting in a rocking chair, smoking a pipe. He looks sad and bitter. "Me grapevines" he mumbles. "Acres of them just the other side of the road ... and now claimed by this unholy earth plague ... Only few acres left behind me house...
How long will they last? I am ruined .... After generations of grapevine growing and wine making, my family looses it all ..." You leave the poor man alone as he starts crying.

This wine farm has been abandonned for months. You notice that not only the grapevines have become twisted, leafless and fruitless, but the whole ground has a sickly black-yellowish appearance and texture to it. You are baffled as to the cause of this.
You hear somthing stirring within the abandonned house. Just as you approach the door, trolls rush out to attack you!
As you approach this wine farm, you notice strange, suspicious figures lurking near the river. It looks as if they are dumping some liquid into the waters. Do you investigate this?
You shrug it off and keep on going to the farm house. There, you see a family busy toiling in their grapevine yards. You decide to keep on going.
As you near the mysterious figures, they stand up from the banks of the river and rush toward you, yelling threateningly. Only then you make them out as trolls!

After the battle, you take a look at what the trolls were dumping into the waters. From nearly empty jugs, you notice a disgusting, foul smelling black-yellowish liquid. You have no idea what is its composition or purpose.
Upon your approach, trolls on guard here rush up to meet the intruders that you are!
Do you enter this strange building?
This is a large eating hall. To your dismay, some trolls are here enjoying a meal. Upon your intrusion, they attack!
Some trolls were resting here: upon your intrusion, they rise up in arms!

In this hall, numerous trolls of various types are on guard here. You notice that of these different kinds of trolls, two of them are dressed in armor and appear to command the others. The moment you walk in, they all rise to attack!
Strange warriors guard this place. Upon your intrusion, they rise to attack!

On this desk, you find numerous letters of correspondence with a man named Herdalth. One in particular catches your eye: "Dear Herdalth; the formula I devised works well and suits our purposes. We are now producing more of it to dump into the rivers ...

near the grapevine yards, which will accelerate its dissemination into the fields.  To answer your question: yes, a continuous treatment is required, or nature itself will inactivate the agent in about a month. Finally, I would request again an ...

assistant to help me maintain my hold on the trolls' minds, particularly in the case of the stygian ones. Doing it alone is quite taxing on my mental powers, and I tire rather quickly of late. Please acquiesce to this request: otherwise, I fear my ....

part of our Masters' plans may crumble. In any case, I plan to visit you in the sewers soon, so that we may discuss this further. I hope that our Masters are pleased so far of my work; The Will of the Mind Lords Be Done. Signed: Lhassa".
You stumble upon a secret treasure cache!

You enter what can only be some sort of laboratory. Numerous trolls are on guard here, as well as a couple of strange warriors. Your attention however centers upon a woman who is busy watching over bizarre machines.
One of the guard see you and sound the alarm!  "Get these intruders!" shouts the woman, as she herself joins the battle.
This storage room holds hundreds of jars, each filled with a foul, disgusting, black-yellowish liquid. You smash the jars to pieces, wasting the substance to the ground.
You would need a special key to unlock and open this one. Just as you back away, you hear a lot of grumbles and moving about from behind the door.

You open the door with the key. To your dismay, you see  a jail-like room filled with unarmored trolls. One of them walks up to you: "This place's ta stygians, not ours. They ally wif bad womans. She mess wif minds, ours. But we hard ta mss wif ...
So she an' ta stygians lock us, an' use our blood fer bad medicine make. We did no wrong. You let us go?"
Without anything further, the trolls dash for the exit of the stygian troll's home.
Seeing their last chance of freedom being denied them, the trolls make a desperate attempt to break out by rushing you!

You see numerous trolls strapped on torture tables. From the empty look in their eyes, they appear brain-dead. Numerous tubes go in and out of them. Looking at these contraptions carefully, you realize that some tubes pump a mixture of substances ...

into their blood, while others pump out the blood mixture into bizarre machines, which appear to be powered by lava heat. The machines apparently process the treated blood and fill jars of it. The result is a sickening, black-yellowish liquid.
The strange machines at the end of the laboratory seem to have lost some of their power, but they otherwise still function.
The machines have stopped working and appear disabeled.
Having seen you prowl around this estate, mercenary guards called on Tanirith's militia: taken by surprise, you are quickly immobilized and taken to face judgement from a magistrate.
You slip past the mercenary guards of this estate and manage to enter this mansion unseen.

You see a middle-aged, stout man in conference with associates. You also notice numerous guards. "Who are you?" demands the man. "I am Jarad Noll, a High Council member and owner of this estate. I demand to know what is the meaning of your intrusion!"
"You'll see that I sell my hide at a very high price, assassins!" snarls Jarad. Immediately, his associates and guards jump on you; even Jarad joins the fray!

Servants and family members stumble in the hall, horrified by what has happened to Jarad. Fearing more guards rushing in, you snatch off Jarad's heirloom from his shirt and make a run for it, far from the estate.

You explain to Jarad what transpired between you and Akkar Dhun. "I see" Jarad says finally, after thinking much about your story. "And I am willing to bet that Golam Thrall must be behind this as well. You see, Golam is a member of the High Council ...

as well, but he is power-hungry and certainly wishes to rule Tanirith as the lone ruler. But I need proof; if I had such proof, I could write a letter to our Lord Paladine to convince him of Thrall's treacherous designs. Bring this proof, noble ...

strangers, and I shall reward you generously". Jarad then winks at you: "In addition to the Lord Paladine's gratitude, and that of the High Council, I am certain!". With a final clasp of hands, you get on your way to find such proof.

You explain to Jarad what transpired so far concerning the Overlords and show him the letter involving G.T.. "I see", muses Jarad. "I've had strong suspicions about Golam Thrall -this "G.T."- and this goes a good way to confirm them.  You see, Golam ...

is also a member of the Council, but a power-hungry one at that. I am certain he schemes for absolute rulership of Tanirith. I would need something more to convince our Lord Paladin and the Council of that; so, bring me this additional proof, noble ...

strangers, and you will be generously rewarded". You then show Jarad the letter involving G.T., which you just realized must be Golam Thrall. "This is superb!" exclaims Jarad. "But I would need another similar letter; find it, and I will be able to ...
to nail that treacherous Thrall for good!" With a clasp of hands, you set out to find that additional proof.

strangers, and you will be generously rewarded". You then show Jarad the letters involving a "G.T.", having just realized this must be Golam Thrall. "That's it!" exclaims Jarad. Without a word, Jarad then starts writing a letter.

He then hands the letter to you, smiling. "Bring this to the Lord Paladine; he will give you further instructions. In the meantime, I will bring your proof to the other members of the Council". He then winks at you: "But first, let's ...

do something about that reward I promised". After handing you a small chest, Jarad clasps hands with you. "Go see our Lord Paladine; Tanirith will yet be saved, noble strangers!" At that, you get on your way.

You explain to Jarad what transpired so far concerning the Overlords and show him the letters involving a "G.T.". "By the Gods!", Jarad exclaims. "I've had my suspicions about Golam Thrall -this "G.T."- plotting to take over Tanirith, and this proves ...

it! You see, Golam is also a member of the Council, and thus I needed proof to convince the Lord Paladine and the other council members of Golam's treacherous schemes. But now, I got it ... and him!" Without another word, Jarad starts writing a letter.

reward you for doing a great service!' After handing you a small chest, Jarad clasps hands with you. "Go see our Lord Paladine; Tanirith will yet be saved, noble strangers!"  At that, you get on your way.
Just as Jarad and his retinue charge, Jhalor glares at you: "I will not be a party to this criminal act!" He then storms angrily out of the mansion, leaving you to face Jarad Noll by yourselves.
The secret exit to the tunnel has been sealed off.
Just as you cross the gates, guards shout in alarm: "It's them! They're the ones who killed High Councillor Jarad Noll!" You are quickly immobilized and brought to a magistrate for judgement.

Warned of your appraoch, Jarad is waiting anxiously for your news. "Have you the proof?" he asks. At your negative answer, he sighs: "Very well. I beg you not to abandon this quest; Tanirith needs your help". At that, you leave.

Jarad is waiting anxiously for your news. You immediately hand him another letter involving G.T. -Golam Thrall. "Finally!" Jarad exclaims. "I now have all I need!". He then runs into his mansion, only to come out a few minutes later with a letter.
Guards on watch nod to you. "Our apologies, but Lord Noll is attending a High Council meeting".
Guards on watch nod politely. "Lord Noll is in conference with his associates and cannot be disturbed".
Guards on watch nod to you. "Our apology, but Lord Noll is away on a business trip".
As Jarad's retinue rise to battle, naryl glares at you: "I will not help you to commit a crime!" She then storms angrily out of the mansion, leaving you to face Jarad Noll by yourselves.

As Jarad's retinue rise to battle, Jhalor and Naryl glare at you: "We will not help you commit crimes!" snarls Jhalor. "I echo his sentiments", adds Naryl. Then both storm angrily out of the mansion, leaving you to fight Jarad Noll by yourselves.

The magistrate comes into the court: "Well! I know who you are!" he intones, barely containing his anger. "The assassins of High Councillor Jarad Noll! Fools! Your descriptions are all over Tanirith!" He shakes his head in disgust and disbelief.

"Because of the despicable nature of your crime" he adds, "I therefore sentence you to death by the sword, a sentence to be carried immediately!". An executionner, whom you did not notice entering, raises his two-handed sword and carries the sentence.

Jarad is waiting anxiously for your news. You then hand him the letter involving G.T. -Golam Thrall- that you uncovered. "That's superb!" exclaims Jarad, "But I need one more proof; then I'll be able to state my case against him". With a nod, you leave.

You see large numbers of people and trade caravans crossing the gates, either entering Tanirith or leaving it. When folks say that this city is the center of activity in the Sword Lands, they certainly were not exagerating!
This is Tanirith's main cemetary.
This is a temple dedicated to Agrah, Goddess of harvests, farming and agriculture. Do you enter?

This is a temple decicated to Agrah, Goddess of harvests, farming and agriculture. Just as you are about to enter, a young disciple calls out to you from the temple's fields, where he was working: "Good sirs! My apology, but all of Agrah's chosen ...
are occupied to solve the cause behind a mysterious rotting of Tanirith's grapevine yards. So for now, their healing services are not available, unfortunately". With an understanding nod, you leave.
Guards behind locked gates peer at you through arrow slits: "This is the private property of Lord Jarad Noll. Begone!"
Guards behind closed gates peer at you from arrow slits: "This is the private property of Lord Golam Thrall. Begone!"

Braggan then coughs, obviously ill at ease. "Me friends" he begins, tentatively, "Me fear we'll have to part, because me must remain with me father, to help heal and restore the dwarven Halls to what it used to be". Nodding in understanding, Braggan ...

warmly clasps your hands, fighting back the tears. "It has been me honor to fight alongside folks such as ye" he finally adds, before walking away. "Moradin be ever watchful over ye",  you hear him whisper in the corridor.

Just as you approach this house, the door opens: "Come in quick!" whispers a shady man, obviously nervous. "We heard from Akkar Dhun ye were coming and why; he wants us to give ye final instructions". Do you go in?

Entering the house, you are lead to a sitting room, quite humbly furnished. "Me's known as Black Shadow, and me welcome ye to the Assassins' Guild of Tanirith" the man announces. "We're not too keen on outsiders such as ye operating in our turf, but ...

our major sponsor convinced us to let this one pass. Me's here to tell ye to go to High Town, and straight to ta estate just south of that of yer target. There, ye will get to meet our sponsor, who's got more instructions fer ya".

"Just one warning" Black Shadow adds: "ye not come back here, or come to Tanirith to commit other paid kills, or we will enforce our claim to our turf. Now go; the estate's guards will let you pass cuz they will know ye are coming."  You nod, then leave.
No one seems about this house. Nonetheless, you feel watched and stalked. Uneasy, you walk away.

Just as you are about to knock on the door, Black Shadow comes out, followed by many of his "collegues". "Ye were warned not to come back here" he snarls. "Now ye shall know what's ta cost of crossing us!"
Not wishing to have to explain yourselves away to the city's militia, and not inclined to wait for more assassins to show up, you run away from this place.
Glancing knowingly at you, then at each other, the mercenary guards let you pass through the gates.

A stout, richly dressed middle-aged man comes to you, followed by his retinue of associates and mercenary guards. "So, you're the ones Dhun has chosen, eh?" the man muses, eyeing you critically.  "Very well" he decides finally, "Perhaps it is best ...

that outsiders to the Assassins' Guild do the job; less of a chance to trace things back to me. Well, then; here are your final instructions: first, you are to never come back here, and forget all about me, if you value your lives; understood?" You nod.

"Second, this is how you will gain access to Jarad Noll's estate: go to Arvoranaan; on the west battlement, a secret door is there. Use this door, then head straight west to the mountains. Another secret door is there, opening to an underground tunnel".

He pauses to let you absorb the information, then he goes on: "Continue straight westwards in the tunnel until you hit a dead end: another secret door is there, and it's through that last door that you will end up on Noll's estate grounds. Got it?"
"Good luck, then" he adds, before walking away back to his mansion; you are then lead outside of the estate.

You then wave Jarad's letter, explaining to them the urgency of the situation. After a few moments of pondering, a knight opens the doors of the gate: "Very well" he says, "Go straight to the castle of our Lord Paladine; the guards will let you in".
There is an inscription at the base of this archeological artifact: "First marble column erected for the first castle of King Ptaraz, Founder of Tanirith".
A knight of the Flame blocks your passage: "You are not authorized to go there, good folks".

You enter a large hall filled with columns, richly carpeted floors, and marble floors. Numerous knights of the Flame are on watch. You see the Lord Paladine, sitting on his throne,  motionning you to come foreward.
As you approach, you see the king involved in important discussions with his court counselors and representatives from other cities. You decide it would be best not to bother him.
Guards block your way into this compound. "Only soldiers and knights of the Flame are allowed here!".

You are lead to the Captain of the Guards. "Greetings, brave ones! Here is a pass that will allow you entry to the castle of the Lord Paladine. Do not loose it, please!" After taking the pass, you walk to the castle.
Guards block you way to the doors of the castle. "Have you a pass?" At your negative answer, you are hushed away.
