"Greetings, good adventurers" the Lord Paladine bids you. "I've heard of your adventures in Aranys; I must admit I'm not surprised that Dhun was involved in the problems we are facing, nor am I sorry about his demise". He then smiles at you approvingly.

You then give him Jarad Noll's letter. "By the Gods!" the Lord exclaims, "So it IS true! Golam Thrall is a traitor to Tanirith!". He then turns to speak with his court counselors. After a lenghty discussion, he turns back to you: "It would not do for ...

me to march openly against this High Councillor; aye, it would only serve to drive further dissension within the Council, aside from other political problems.  I therefore ask you to go to his estate and apprehend him, then bring him back to me so ...

that he may be judged. But I have a feeling he won't go without a fight, and a nasty one at that: therefore, you may use any force necessary to bring him down. Do this service, and you shall be rewarded".  With a determined nod, you get on your way.
Opening the gates, the guards rush out with a cruel smile on their faces, eager to draw blood!

Golam Thrall is standing outside his mansion, surrounded by his most trusted mercenary soldiers and associates. "Your being here" he snarls, "can only mean that I have been exposed. So be it. But I will not surrender!!!" At that, his forces attack!
The gates to Golam Thrall's estate are remain unguarded. However, a sign is hung next to the gates: "For Sale".

You attempt to flee but are nevertheless quickly overwhelmed. "Now that it is all in the open, I am now free to march with my army against Jarad Noll and this fool of a Lord Paladine!" Golam sneers, just before you are put to the sword.

Just as the battle is finished, numerous soldiers and some knights of the Flame rush through the gates of the estate. "Well met!" a captain greets you. "We will take over from you, brave ones! Please, go see the Lord Paladine as soon as you can!".
You slowly walk away, welcoming the rest, as the Lord Paladine's forces rout or capture the remnants of Golam Thrall's mercenary army, and secure his mansion.

"Well met, brave and noble ones!" the Lord Paladine greets you. You notice numerous high ranking officials, including Jarad Noll (who is smiling proudly at you). The Lord Paladine then turns to the distinguished assembly: "For many of us, today is a ...

sad day, for today one of our High Councillor was found guilty of crimes against us, our city, and our people. Fortunately, his threat is now gone; it is to be hoped that the damage he may have caused is limited in scope.  But I am confident that ...

Tanirith will persevere, and continue to shine as a beacon of civilization, stability, and prosperity for the Sword Lands!". A thunderous applause follows this. "So let us today honor those who have rendered heroic services to Tanirith" the Lord ...
goes on amidst the cheers, "instead of wallowing in sadness!" A louder cheer follows.
A small celebration ensues, where the Lord paladine presents you with a reward. After a few hours of congratulations, toasts and conversations, you finally take your leave.
Knights of the Flame stand guard in front of the mansion of the late Golam Thrall, to discourage would be looters.

"We are faced by many problems in Tanirith. Our grapevine yards are mysteriously rotting away, sapping at our wine trade revenues; and lately, diplomatic relations with our ally, the city of Lantharond, have inexplicably soured." He shakes ...
his head in resignation. "We need help, and it is my sincere hope that you will intervene in these matters, should you happen to come across them."

"Well met, Heroes of Wailsrond!" the Lord Paladine greets you, smiling warmly. "Lord Pyre has told me much of your exploits. I must admit that I am grateful of you visiting our fair city, Tanirith; in fact, I was looking forward to meeting you".
"Greetings, good people" the Lord Paladine bids you. "What are those urgent matters of yours which would require my attention?"
Bowing respectfully, you bid good wishes to the Lord Paladine and get on your way.
"Well met, noble heroes!" the Lord Paladine greets you, smiling warmly. "Pray tell me, what is it that seems to cloud your minds today?"

You hand the letter involving a "S.F."  As the Lord paladine reads it, he grows angry. "How could I have been such a fool?" he snarls. He then turns to you: "Sardin Firestorm, this "S.F.", is the current High Commander of the Knights of the Flame".

He pauses to calm himself. "I recommended him to this position. I had heard rumors about things going wrong with the Knighthood, but I paid no heed since they seemed to be just that -rumors. But this letter ... Well, I have no choice to take action, now.

But I must do this cautiously; I dare not move against the knighthood -my knighthood- unless I am absolutely certain that I have all the proof needed to convince the High Council, as well as those good knights that are still part of the Order. So I ...
bid you, noble ones, to find such additional proof and bring it to me". With a determined nod, you take your leave.

A wrought bronze armory identifies this group of compounds and the small fortress as the headquarters, residences, and training grounds, of the knights of the Flame. You hear the knights practicing hard their trade, both with weapons and horses.
Two knights glare at you from the battlements: "Begone from here! Only knights or sanctionned officials are allowed entry!".

Then one of the knights scrutinizes your comrade intensely: "Jhalor Fireblade?" he finally asks, sneering. Jhalor answers simply with a nod, his jaws clenched and his gaze unfathomable. "I thought so!" chuckles the other knight. "Well, well! I'm ...

certain that the High Commander will be VERY interested in hearing the news that you have dared to return to Tanirith!" The two knights then chuckle again; fearing trouble, you walk away, all the while looking questioningly at Jhalor.

You comrade sighs. "Yes, my friends. I was a knight of the Flame; I had been so honored for almost five years, until four months ago. You see, the current High Commander, Sardin Firestorm, was an excellent and noble leader of the Order at first. But ...

about six months past, he began to adopt a dubious philosophy of leadership; in fact, the better a knight of the Flame would be at following the Codes and Customs of our Order, the worst he would become in the eyes of the High Commander. Our leader ...

also began preaching ridiculous concepts such as non-interference with our neighbors, even if they were in dire need, which went against everything we believe. Everything good, that is: for I became convinced that Firestorm had become corrupted by ...

evil. Thus I began debating him privately -which was a priviledge I had since I had risen to being Second In Command-, then openly. It soon came to pass that I was facing a choice: either fight him more at the risk of creating further dissension ...

within the Order, or resign my commission in disgrace to save the Order from further chicanery. For at the time, Sardin had his supporters and I had acquired mine. So, I chose to resign, with the hope of finding the lawful means of deposing Sardin ...
and thus save what's left of the knighthood from his evil". Jhalor sighs again. "I know I should've told you of this sooner, but ...". Understanding, you comfort him as best as you can.

But I must do this rationally, and calmly, to make certain that the knighthood does not loose completely the faith and trust of the people." After thinking a bit, he nods: "Very well. I charge you of confronting Sardin and to bring him back for trial.

In the meantime, I will convene the High Council and show this damning proof you have brought me. If Sardin resists his arrest, use whatever means necessary." He then shakes his head in disgust. "It's a good thing that my priests screen every knight ...
that serves me; otherwise, I shudder at the possibilities. Now go, noble heroes, and bring this dark paladin down!" With a determined nod, you get on your way.
Knights of the Flame peers at you from the battlements: "We told you to begone from here already!"
Do you stand your ground?
The knights of the Flame rush at you from the opened gate!
The gates are unguarded.

The High Commander stands proudly outside the forteress, surrounded by his loyal knights. You also notice some strange warriors, standing protectively near him. "Your presence here can only mean that we have reached the end game, no?" He chuckles.
"Well, let's see who shall win the final round, shall we?" Immediately, Sardin Firestorm and his troops attack!

Jhalor then intercedes: "Give up, High Commander!  You have been proven unfit to lead the knighthood! You can still do the honorable thing and step down to face trial!" Sardin laughs: "You are an idealistic fool, Jhalor, and always have been!"
"Greetings again, good adventurers" the Lord Paladine bids you. "What are these urgent matters of yours which require my attention?"

As the battle winds down, soldiers and knights of the Flame, loyal to the Lord Paladine, storm the knighthood grounds. "Well done and well met, noble heroes!" a captain greets you. "Our Lord sent us over to quickly and quietly take over things, until ...

the knighthood can get back on it's horse, sort of say. Please go see our Lord as soon as you can: he wishes to speak with you!" Tired, you get on your way to the castle, as the soldiers and knights rout or capture the remaining dark knights.

You walk over to Sardin Firestorm, who is running on his very last breath. "It is ... over" he whispers with great difficulty. "T-tell ... Lord Paladine ... my mind ... prisoner ... of the ... Overlords ... Could not ... resist ... I'm so ... sorry ... "
Forgive m- ..."  He then passes away. Disturbed by Sardin's revelations, you go to the Lord Paladine's castle while pondering on them.

"Welcome back, noble heroes" the Lord Paladine greets you. He is smiling warmly, but he looks obviously affected by the recent events. "Forgive me if I do not throw another celebration in honor of the great service you have rendered, but it is best ...

that what happened remains poorly known to the people. Furthermore, the fall of the knighthood -however corrupted it had become- puts Tanirith in a lesser position of military power; I do not wish our enemies, or potential ones, to realize this."

He pauses. "At least, there remains a good number of true knights of the Flame, and they shall constitute the building stone for a better and healthier knighthood; however, I am hard pressed to find a suitable High Commander to take on this task".
The Lord Paladine sighs. "Well, that is another problem I will have to solve, and soon. In any case, please accept this reward for your heroic efforts".

Jhalor then steps forward, bowing formally to the Lord Paladine: "Mylord; I, Jhalor Fireblade, former second in command of the knighthood, volunteers for such a task, if you deem it appropriate and justified". The Lord smiles warmly: "I hoped you ...

would shed your anonymity and propose yourself, Fireblade; of course, I had recognized you, and I had learned about your resignation in disgrace. But in the light of Firestorm's corruption, I now easily fathom the honorable reasons behind your ...

decision. So, I do accept your pledge of service and thus appoint you High Commander of the knighthood for a year, until at such time a Conclave of the Order will have to confirm your appointment. But of that, I have no doubt ..." The Lord then ...

glances to some of the knights on guard, grinning. Seeing their smile and their prouder stance, you also guess that Jhalor will indeed be confirmed as High Commander. Your comrade then turns to you: "My friends; I thank you from the bottom of my ...

heart for accepting me into your heroic group and for your friendship; but now, I must leave you for this new calling".  Clasping his hands, your nod in understanding and wish him the best of luck. "Come and visit me, if you will" he adds, before ...

departing for the knighthood's forteress, under an honor guard. Nodding in approval, the Lord Paladine turns back to you: "Please, accept this reward for your heroic deeds. Again, I thank you for the service you have rendered us".
Knights of the Flame on watch block your passage: "Our deepest apologies, but High Commander Fireblade is quite occupied right now; but he does sends his very best wishes".
Knights of the Flame are busy practicing their weapon skills, while apprentices are learning these skills under the tutelage of veteran knights.
Knights of the Flame on watch block your passage: "Our apologies, but High Commander Flamestone is quite occupied, and therefore cannot recieve visitors".

"Have you the additional proof?" the Lord Paladine asks. You hand him another letter involving "S.F." that you found. After reading it, he turns to you: "Well, that's it. There's no doubt in my mind. Time to clean our own backyard, as they say ...
Dark knights are guarding this training compound.

Unlocking the doors, you find numerous knights of the Flame held captive within, stripped of their armors and their weapons. After freeing them,  they rush to the castle to arm themselves anew and bring reinforcements.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Tanirith Farm Lands". Also, an arrow points to the North for Tanirith.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Cove Hold-Trade Caravan Waystation". Also, an arrow points to the North for Tanirith, and to the West for Wailsrond, Sparklestone and Aranys.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Riverside-Trade Caravan Waystation". Also, an arrow points to the North for Sparklestone and Aranys, and to the South for Wailsrond and Tanirith.
This sign-post points to the North and East for Tanirith Wine Farms, to the South for Tanirith Farmlands, and to the East for Tanirith.
This sign-post points to the east for Tanirith, and to the North and the West for Tanirith Wine Farms.
This sign points to the South for Tanirith Farmlands, and to the East for Tanirith.
Halfling warriors on watch nod to you politely.
The sign above the door of this store reads: "Rhondo's General Store". Do you enter?
As in the case of any large city, numerous people and trade caravans pass through the gates of Sharranth.

Just as you pass, dozens of soldiers surround you: "Adventurer scum such as ye are forbidden entry to Sharranth. So has ordered our Warlord, Antraxus Storm the Mighty!" You are then promptly escorted away from the gates.
Some members of your party have apparently fell ill from the contaminated waters of the sewers.

Numerous people pass through the gates of Coral Tower, either arriving from a long boat trip or going to board a vessel. Likewise, harbor workers and sailors are busy transporting goods either from merchant boats or loading them.

As you cross the gates, guards yell out general orders to all new comers and visitors: "It is the law of Coral Towers that all must purchase a permit to circulate within  the streets, as decreed by Thorgal Ramoor, our Regent. Everyone is susceptible ...

to be asked to produce this permit; failure to do so will result in incarceration for any amount of time as deemed appropriate by the magistrate appointed by our Regent. Permits may be purchased at the Harbor Master's building".
Guards collect the permits from all those who are leaving Coral Towers, including yours.
"No permits, eh?" snarls one of the guards. "Well, ye were warned: to jail ye go!". Do you resist arrest?
"We'll see about that!" the guard shouts, just as others join him to restrain you!
Panting and tired after this clash, you make haste to get out of Coral Towers!
"It's them!!!" a guard shouts, to your surprise. "They're back! Let's get them this time!" You are then surrounded by numerous, angry, and blood thirsty guards!
Surrendering peacefully, you are promptly taken to the Magistrate Halls of Coral Towers.

The magistrate walks into the court: "What have we here?" he sneers, looking at you with disdain. "Stragglers who refuse to follow the laws of our fair city?" He chuckles. "Well, then: jail for each of you; you'll get out if we don't forget you".
You are stripped of your equipment, then thrown into a dark, damp cell.
You seriously wonder if you will ever be let out of this hole.
These are the Magistrate Halls of Coral Towers.
This is the Harbor Master building of Coral Towers. The place is filled with people. Do you go in?

After many hours of waiting in a long line of people, you finally get your turn at the kiosk marked "Permits".  There, a lady looks at you suspiciously: "Ye want permits? That's 10 gp per head, so 60 golds total".  Who will pay?

You walk to a series of kiosks, each with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets" and a destination. You go to the one for Wailsrond. There, a lady smiles at you: "Fare to Wailsrond? That's 1000 golds total".  Who will pay?
"Thank you. Go to the last pier to the south-west: your vessel is right at the end. Departures are at every hours; have a good sail".

You walk to a series of kiosks, each with a sign bearing the words "Fare Tickets" and a destination. You go to the one for Tanirith; there, a lady smiles at you: "Fare to Tanirith? That will be 1000 golds total".  Who will pay?

"It's too late" he whispers, fighting back the tears. "Its no one's fault. My wife fell ill in the disease-ridden prison, and died a few days ago. Thank you nonetheless for bringing my brother's money; it will help for a decent burial". Shocked by ...
this turn of events, you leave Mareck to grief privately. You can't help but be angered at Coral Towers' Regent, who would allow innocent people to rot in his prisons.
A patrol of soldiers stop you: "Ye have yer circulation permits?" asks the captain of the patrol.
After scrutinizing your papers, the captain orders you to move on while he and his patrol go on about their business.

This is Tanirith's famous Scholar Halls, a university. There is also a temple dedicated to Erond, God of Thought, Crafts, and Knowledge; this is not surprising since priests of Erond also function as teachers and caretakers of the Scholar Halls.
A priest approaches you: "Greetings, good strangers. Only those students enrolled in the Scholar Halls may enter them; however, anyone may enter Erond's House".  Do you want to go to Erond's temple?
The sign above the door of this place reads: "The Raging Wyvern".  Do you enter?
It appears that the place is filled with patrons; nonetheless, you hear music played by wandering bards.
A woman smiles at you: "Welcome to the Raging Wyvern. Do ye want a room for the night? It's 3 golds per person, so 18 golds total".
"Thank you. Have a good night's sleep".

You overhear a conversation: "I hear that an assassins' guild has sprung up in Tanirith" says a woman. "Really? But that's impossible! Not with the Lord Paladine and the knights of the Flames!" exclaim another. "Well, it exists anyways! I even heard ...
that this guild is in a house somewhere just south of the east-side of the Central Port!" adds the first woman.  Casually, you walk away.
A sign above the door of this inn reads: "The Journey's End".  Do you go in?
A sign above the doors of this building reads: "Cove Hold Waystation". This place seems to be a store as well as an inn.  Do you enter?
The place is not full of travelers, but there is a good number of caravan escorts, adventurers, and the like. Not suprisingly, some wandering bards are livening up the place with music.
A burly innkeeper smiles at you: "Welcome, good gents! What do ye want?"
A sour barkeeper eyes you with annoyance: "Oy! Whot do ye want?"
A wench smiles at you shyly: "Welcome, good folks. How may I serve ye?"
"Food is 1 gold per person, so 6 golds total.  Who will pay?"
You are served a bowl of hot stew with beef and vegetables. Although average in preparation and taste, it still hits the spot.
"Drinks are 1 gold apiece, so that means 6 golds total fo ye. Who will pay?"
You are served large mugs of some local brew. Somewhat bitter, it is however quite strong.
You are served hot stew with beef and vegetables, along with large mugs of brew. The stew is average, but it hits the spot; the brew is bitter, but quite strong.
"Food and drinks are 2 golds per person, so 12 golds total fer ye. Who'll pay?"
"Welcome" an innkeeper greets you. "Rooms are 2 golds a night per person, so 12 golds total for ye. Do ye want a room?"
A storekeeper greets you: "Welcome! Do ye need to buy something?"
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Riverside Waystation".  This place seems to be a store as well as an inn.  Do you go in?

between Bywater and this region; indeed, many caravans have been attacked recently, and Bywater's economy is begining to suffer for it. In fact, the King of Bywater suspects that some dark plan to bring about the fall of his city may be behind it all.
You are given large bowls of beef stew and vegetables. While not haute cuisine, it still hits the spot.
You are given large bowls of chunky chiken and pasta soup, with even vegetables in it. A bit bland, but still good.
You are given large bowls of seafood chowder (clams, shrimps, cod, crab). A bit too salty, but quite filling.
"Food is 3 golds apiece, so 12 golds total fer ye. Who'll pay?"
"Drinks are 2 golds apiece, so 12 golds total fer ye. Who'll pay?"
"Here's some rhum from Wailsrond".
"Here some wine from Tanirith".
"Here's some ale from our own brewery".
"That's six golds apiece, so 36 golds total fer ye. Who'll pay?"
A wench then comes to serve your drinks.
The bartender leans toward you to whisper: "That'll cost ye a bit ... Me price is 25 golds".  Do you pay?

The money is quickly pocketed: "Our Queen and her daughter died at sea 'cuz of a big storm, or so says our Regent -the queen's brother. But me heard that Queen Aquillae is in fact kept prisoner in a cave, somewhere beneath the rocky cliffs ..."

The money is pocketed: "Our Regent, Thorgal, is a ruthless despot.  There's word that some dissidents who resent his rule have formed an underground resistance group. Me heard that theyre operating from a house near our own Laughing Tempest ..."

The money is quickly pocketed: "The Ramoor Dynasty has been ruling Coral Towers for almost two centuries. Me heard that the family burial crypt, next to the castle, has been haunted by evil spirits ever since Thorgal Ramoor, our Regent, stole the crown".

The money is pocketed: "Our Queen and Princess died at sea some six months ago, or so says our Regent -the queen's brother. But me heard that Princess Jorale is in fact hiding from her ruthless uncle, and is planning to overthrow him ..."

A middle-aged man nods at you politely: "Greetings, adventurers! I am Sorceros; I am seeking to travel with bold fellows such as ye, and perhaps find one or two treasures along the way!"  He winks at you, smiling. "So, if ye are of need of a good ...
sorcerer, ye just say the word: I would be honored to join yer company!"  Do you accept Sorceros into your ranks?
Sorceros has joined your party; check out the Allies Menu.
"Superb!" Sorceros exclaims, quite glad to join your group.
"As you wish" replies Sorceros, visibly disapointed. As he goes back to eating his meal in silence, you walk away.
Do you reconsider and invite Sorceros to join your party?

You overhear a conversation between royal soldiers: "Me tell ye" says one, "it ain't good at all. Ta Regent's keep hiring more of them mercenaries to replace us, cuz they'll gladly do his evil biding". Another one nods: "Aye. We care fer our ...

our people, but them mercenaries don't".  He then shakes his head in disgust. "And there's not a damn thing we cain say" adds a third one, "cuz then we'll be ta ones to get executed".  At that, you walk away.

You overhear a conversation between fishermen: "Let me tell ye, me dunno if me'll be able to keep me boat" mumbles the first one. "Aye" agrees the second, "with them taxes ta Regent hits us with, we cain't keep up or make enough with ta catches we sell".

"What cain we do?" asks a third one. "With ta Queen and Pricess dead, only ta Regent's left with royal blood to rule". The first one nods: "Aye. And us to be pitied fer it!". "Careful!" adds the second. "His agents are everywhere; if they hear us, we ...
be taken to jail and left there to rot!"  At that, you walk away.

Soldiers storm into the place. The captain of the patrol goes up to two fishermen: "You two!" he snarls. "You were heard speaking ill our your rightfull Regent! The law is clear about such crimes". Turning to his men, he orders them to seize the ...
hapless fishermen. Although the poor saps protest their innocence, they are quickly immobilized with excess of force and chained.  Do you help the fishermen?
"They've accomplices! " yells one soldier. "They must be of the resistance: it's a set up!" shouts the captain, as he and his men scramble to attack you!
Panting, you decide it best to get out of this place, in case more soldiers show up!
Without further due, the soldiers carry the unconscious fishermen away, while the captain sends warning looks to anyone looking on: "Let that be a lesson to you all: the Regent is the law!".
Soldiers storm into the place. "Circulation permits, everyone!" the captain of the patrol orders, as his soldiers spread out to verify the permits of every patron, including you.
After scrutinizing your papers, a soldier walks on to other patrons. A few more minutes of verification later, the patrol walks out, having caught no one without a permit.

After scrutinizing your papers, a soldier walks on to other patrons. Finally, the patrol walks out, along with a few patrons caught without permits. You notice they are in chains, while the soldiers are grinning evilly at them.

You cross paths with a patrol. The soldiers are forcibly taking some men and women to jail, having bound them in chains. You can't help but flinch at the brutality of the soldiers, as they repeatedly shove or hit their helpless prisonners.
Do you attack the patrol to free these poor people?

Panting, you quickly break the chains of the prisonners. "Thank ye so much!" a woman tells you, fighting back tears of joy. "We've done nothing wrong, except running out of money to pay the taxes the Regent imposes on us". Then, all of them quickly ...
run away to hide. You wonder what kind of ruler is this Regent, to taxe his people to abject poverty, then to punish them for having become poor.
Hoping that no one will have seen you clearly enough to denounce you to the authorities, you get on your way as well.
Feeling helpless, you watch the patrol go on its way with the prisonners. The captain of the patrol shoots  a warning look at you as he passes by.

A shadowy man grabs you by the elbow, his eyes darting left and right as if to make sure no one is looking your way: "I know who ye are, Heroes of Wailsrond!" he whispers. "Ye must help us overthrow that despot Thorgal Ramoor. I can't tell ye more ...

in here, so I urge ye to go to the lonely house behind the Laughing Tempest. Knock on the door and whisper this password: "Ramoor". Our resistance leader is quite eager to me ye!" Without another word, the man walks away as if nothing had happened.
Guards on watch eye you severely: "Begone, ye wretches! This is ta Regent's Castle grounds, and ye sure ain't invited to go there!"
This is the Ramoor Family burial crypt.
A sign above the door of this place reads: "Inn of the Coral Reefs".  Do you enter?

Just as you arrive at the entrance of this cavern, soldiers jump out of nowhere in front of you to block your way: "Whot are ye doing here?" snarls one soldier. "Yer trespassing on ta Regent's property! Begone now!"  Do you stand your ground?
Panting and tired, you enter this cavern.

You see a woman sitting in a small chair. She is guarded by soldiers, knights, and even pirates! "Help me!" the woman shouts upon seeing you, "I am the rightful ruler of Coral Towers!" As one of the knight knocks her out, his accomplices rush to attack!
To your relief, some of the soldiers turn on the Queen's captors, seizing the chance to free her!
Overwhelmed, you are quickly seized and put to death. Your last sight is that of the Queen, weeping.

Looking at you, the Queen stands up. She is obviously weak. "My thanks, noble ones. I am Queen Aquillae Ramoor; I have been held captive here for months now. My brother, Thorgal, allied himself with devious people, including the Pirate Queen, with ...

whom he had fallen in love with. With the help of these people, he seized the crown of Coral Towers. He would have killed me then, but my daughter, Princess Jorale, escaped from his grasp; he felt he had to kill us both in secret to secure his hold ...

on the crown and the people of Coral Towers. But with Jorale free and in hiding, he was loath to murder me". The Queen sighs, shaking her head in disgust: "Damn Thorgal for the fool that he is!  Our father gave the crown to me upon his death, because ...

I was better suited to rule than my brother; aye, all he can do is act like a ruthless despot. He could never understand that the people must love and respect their Liege, for the crown and rule to remain safe and stable". The Queen sighs again.

Raising her head proudly, she then looks at you with fire in her eyes: "Well, he made his move; now, it's MY turn! I will need of your help more, noble ones: you must find Princess Jorale and bring her back to me. Only once we are together will the ...

people revolt, and then we will march to the castle and overthrow my treacherous brother! So go, noble ones: I will stay here, safely out of sight, waiting for your return".  Leaving enough food and water to the Queen, you get on your way.

As you enter the cavern, Queen Aquillae walks up to you: "Have you found her?" she asks, anxiously. At your negative response, the Queen sighs: "Very well. Do not abandon her search: she and I must stand together against Thorgal". Nodding, you leave.

After your rapping, the door of this is slightly opened, a young woman peering at you from the opening.  "What is the password?" she asks. After whispering the password, she lets you in, leading you to the basement of the house.

There, you find yourselves surrounded by men and women, their weapons at the ready. "Welcome, Heroes of Wailsrond!" the yound woman tells you. "I am Princess Jorale, daughter of Queen Aquillae Ramoor and leader of this resistance group against the ...

rule of my evil uncle, the Regent Thorgal Ramoor. Your arrival is a great sign for us, since with your help we can now march onto the castle and overthrow my uncle!"  Jorale's followers voice their approval at that. "With my mother dead, or so I have ...

resigned myself to believe, we are left with no other choice: we march now or never!" With more voiced approvals from her followers, Jorale looks you straight in the eye: "So, what say you, noble heroes?"  What do you reply?

Runelore stops you: "I don't think we should meddle in politics that do not concern us, let alone walk into something that is obviously a trap!"  Considering what Runelore just said, do you knock on this door?

After a few moments of thought, Jorale turns to you, sighing: "Your words have wisdom in them. Although I dare not hope that she is still alive, I will however accompany you to search for my mother. but if she is dead, then we march against Thorgal!"
With a nod, you and Jorale leave the house against her follower's protests, setting yourselves to find her mother, the Queen.
No one answers your rapping.

Jorale runs to her mother, both embracing each other and weeping with joy. "You are truly alive!" cries Jorale. "My daughter!" whispers the Queen. Uncomfortable, you leave them this moment of private reunion.

Raising her head proudly, she gazes at you with fire in her eyes: "Well, he made his move; now it's OUR turn!" she exclaims. "Aye, indeed!" adds Jorale with determination. "I'll contact my resistance group and we march to the castle!" The Queen smiles.

"My daughter" she says,  gazing at Jorale like a loving mother, "you are ever the tempestuous one. Let us rest first; in fact, bring me to your brave followers to rest there, while these noble heroes replenish their strenght. Then, we'll all meet ...
at the castle's gates: then will we run through the enemy!" As Jorale leads he mother out of the cavern, you bid them farewell until you meet at the castle gates for the final battle.

resigned myself to believe, we are left with no other choice: we march now or never!" With more voiced approvals, Jorale looks you straight in the eye: "So, what say you, noble heroes?" Smiling, you tell her that you have found Queen Aquillae and ...

that she is waiting to see her daughter. At first taken aghast by your announcement, Jorale embraces each and everyone of you: "She's alive! Praise the Gods!"  she exclaims, joyfully, as her followers cheer. "Take me to her, please!" Jorale tells you.
With a nod, you leave the house to go back to the cavern where the Queen remains safe and hidden, with Jorale eagerly following you.

Queen Aquillae then turns to you: "Thank you so much, noble ones. Now, we can move against my evil brother!" "Aye!" adds Jorale, "I'll contact my resistance group and we march straight to the castle!"  The Queen smiles at that.
"You have chosen your side, then! Heroes? Bah!" snarls Jorale, as she gives the signal to her followers to attack!
Having crushed the resistance group against the Regent, you decide that perhaps he may reward you ...

As you walk in this cavern, you are shocked to find the body of a woman, lying there after having been put to the sword.  From her robe and apparels, she must have been someone of royal blood.  You also see a table, chairs and a small cot. Was this ...
place inhabited by this woman? Unsure, you shrug off the matter and get on your way.

You see numerous soldiers arrayed in front of the gate. From the battlements, a middle-aged man standing proudly calls to you: "Greetings, Heroes of Wailsrond! I wanted to thank you personally for ridding me of the resistance group! However, since ...

I am not one to let loose ends wander around, and considering that you are the ones responsible for the death of Nurale Darkstrome, who was to become my queen,  I hope you'll forgive me if I am not overwhelmed with gratitude". At the snap of his ...

fingers, the Regent's forces bear down on you. Outnumbered and outmatched, you manage to fight valiantly, but to no avail. As you fall one by one, the Regent smiles with the satisfaction of an evil man getting his revenge.
Fearing that the sounds of battle have attracted too much attention, you make haste to leave this house.

Amidst cheers, everyone gathers their gear and weapons. With a regal gesture, Princess Jorale signals to move forward. Running through the streets, you see the people cower and hide instead of joining you; you wonder if that's a good sign.

Numerous soldiers are arrayed in front of the caslte gate; it would appear that the element of surprise is gone for Jorale, you and her followers. From the battlements, a regal, middle-aged man call out to Jorale and you: "Fools! Especially you, my ...

impudent niece, and you, the Heroes of Wailsrond, meddling murderers that you are! Yes, I called you murderers, for you have killed Nurale Darkstrome, my beloved! Well now, vengeance is mine!" With a snap of his finger, the Regent's forces attack!

"You think you have won? You think you can escape from me?" snarls the Regent. "My allies are very helpful in supplying men and weapons; the more you kill, the more I will have left!"  With another sharp snap of his fingers, more of his forces attack!
Outnumbered and outmatched, you manage to fight valiantly, but to no avail. As you drop one by one, you catch a glimpse of the Regent smiling like an evil man who is triumphant.

As you near the castle gate, you are relieved to see a good number of ordinary people mixed with Jorale's resistance warriors. To your surprise, the gate is already opened and appears unguarded. At your approach, Queen Aquillae nods to you.

"The time has come to overthrow the usurper!" the Queen shouts, to be answers by a roaring cheer. With a signal from Princess Jorale, all march directly to the castle, with the Queen and her daughter leading the way!
Surprisingly, this compound is empty. Your instincts tell you that this is not a good sign ...
The gates are locked!

A regal, middle-aged man stands proubly at the castle doors, surrounded by his closest aides. "You're to late, sister of mine!" he snarls. "I'm Regent, and with my allies, you can't win!". Branding her fist, Queen Aquillae steps up: "It's over, Thorgal!"

"Our people have suffered enough! Surrender and face trial for your crimes!" Suddenly, numerous soldiers come from each side of the castle, effectively surrounding you all. At the same time, you hear the gate being closed and locked.

"You are a fool, Aquillae, and always has been!" Thorgal sneers, trumphantly. "And as for you, Heroes of Wailsrond, you will finally pay for the murder of my beloved Nurale!" With a snap of his finger, his forces attack; luckyly, some soldiers help you!

As the battle winds down, numerous revolting citizen and resistance warriors take to the streets, rounding up the remaining mercenary soldiers under Thorgal's service.  With grim determination, Queen Aquillae walks over to her brother's corpse.

She then turns to face those left in the castle grounds, raising her sword high: "Coral Tower shall suffer the Regent's rule no more!" she proclaims proudly, amidst cheers and celebration. Jorale then approaches you: "Go and rest, noble heroes. My ...

mother and I will tidy things over here, as is our responsibility. Come back tomorrow at the castle, if you would". With a firm clasp of your hands, Jorale walks over to Aquillae. Tired after such a clash, you agree that a good rest would be welcomed.
Royal guards nod to you politely and respectfully.

As you approach the compound, a small contigent of royal soldiers march out to patrol the streets. Two  other guards block your way: "Our apologies, noble heroes", one of them tells you, "but only soldiers and superior officers are allowed in there".

To your surprise, numerous citizen and dignitairies are standing outside of the castle, cheering you. An alley of honor, comprised of royal soldiers, is opened to you and lead straight to the Queen, warmly smiling and motionning you to walk toward her.

Queen Aquillae is dressed in he royal robes, wearing the crown that is rightfully hers. Beside her, Princess Jorale is likewise royaly dressed and beaming at you. The Queen then raises her hand to silence the cheers. "Today, Coral Towers has much to ...

celebrate for. We are free of the Regent's tyranny, and now peace and prosperity will be ours again. We are a proud people, but we know how to be grateful".  Aquillae nods to you, before continuing: "Indeed, we are much in debt of these noble and ...

brave adventurers. Heroes of Wailsrond they may be, I know that they will forever be the Heroes of Coral Towers!" Amidst renewed cheers, the Queen hands you a small chest: "Please accept these tokens as our people's gratitude. And now, let's celebrate!"

With music, laughter and good food, the people of Coral Towers celebrate their victory and you, their heroes. Many times you have to dance, for all want to be close to you. After many hours, you bid your goodnights to the Queen and the Princess.
Tired but joyfull, only then you remember the chest that Aquillae gave you.
Royal guards block you way: "Our apologies, but the Queen and Princess are in conference with merchants and traders. However, they do send their very best to you".

In the chest, you also find numerous letters, obviously put there by the Queen after finding them in her castle. Not surprisingly, these are letters of correspondence between Thorgal Ramoor and Akkar Dhun, Doran Ghall, Lharond Dragonspurr, and Nurale ...

Darkstrome. From these, you gather that the Overlords are seeking to "secure" the Sword Lands; you also find mention of unspecified plans involving the fall of Dwarven Halls, Tanirith and Lantharond. What do the Overlords need the Sword Lands for?

From afar, you see numerous riders practicing their skills at arms in mock battles. Some are wearing the colors and armors of troopers of Lantharond, whereas other are wearing non-descript suits of armor.

By a stroke of bad luck, one of the riders sees you; shouting in alarm, he rides toward a compound further south-east, while his comrades ride fast in your direction, their weapons drawn and raised to strike!

Riders are camping here. Some of them are wearing the colors and armors of the troopers of Lantharond, whereas others are wearing non-descript armors. At your approach, they all jump on their mounts and attack!
A strange warrior, surrounded by similarly strange warriors, as well as riders wearing Lantharond trooper uniforms, calls out to you as you approach this isolated compound:
"I don't know who you are" the strange warrior snarls, "but you will regret poking your noses into business that should be left alone!" With a snap of his gloved fingers, his men attack!

"I was hoping you meddling fools would stumble your way to me" the strange warrior snarls. "Aye! My Overlord Masters warned me about you and instructed me to rid the world of your nuisance, should I get the chance!" At his silent gesture, his men attack!
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Creek Dale Waystation". Do you enter?

You overhear a conversation between two caravan traders: "I tell ye, we cain't know who's who anymore! One of my caravans was attacked by Lantharond troopers, but later I was told they were impostors by a Lantharond trader!" the first one complains.

"Aye" the second replies. "That reminds me: have ye heard about this compound that's is supposed to be just west of here?" The first one shakes his head. "Well" continues the second, "apparently a large band of riders is training there, but no one ...

knows what they are really about. So, I'm begining to wonder whether these guys are not somehow involved in this crazy business going about!"  The first one shrugs: "I think it's all a ploy by the Dragonking of Lantharond to confuse us all while he ...
wages his secret war with Tanirith".  "Could be that too" replies the second.  At that, you walk away.
Searching the compound, you manage to find some useful items.

You also notice a fireplace, still smoldering. You see that piles of papers have been burned just then, probably just before you reached the compound. Luckyly, you find a parchment sheet which has somehow escaped the destruction.

The letter dates from a few months ago and reads like this: "Sub-commander Zaroth; We are pleased by the quickness with which you have assembled this small force of riders. Here are the promised instructions for you in how to use this force; bear ...

in mind that your role in our plans is critical. First, disguise your forces to pass them as troopers of Lantharond; we will let your own judgement on how to use this subterfuge in fermenting strains in the relations between Lantharond and Tanirith ...

Second, once the first part is already producing these results, your force -still in disguise- will then begin to attack the amazons of Artemisia Forest, West of your established stronghold. You may attack them whenever and wherever, of course. This ...

part of your duties will serve to isolate and weaken Lantharond further; in this respect, We have secured some inside help from the amazon tribe. We bid you success! The Will of the Mind Lords Be Done".  Without further thinking, you secure this letter.
Numerous people cross the gates of Lantharond. You notice soldiers on the battlements, ever watchful and alert.
You retrace your steps.

These old, ancient columns are engraved in runic markings which you manage to decipher: "If the right bridge is the mind, the left bridge is the heart, and the middle bridge is wisdom, which is the right path to Power?"
The bridge collapses, making you fall into the raging waters below!!!

The eyes of the portal in front of you lit up with an eerie magical glow: "You who dare to walk the path must prove you are worthy of it. Answer my riddle and pass safely; the price of your failure will be your deaths".

"It absorbs and retains, yet it can leak; Inside it, one is at one's upmost privacy: that is why those who may know it are a danger to its sanctity.  What is it?"  the outerworldy voice intones.  What do you do or say?
"Fools!" the disembodied voice intones. "Now pay the ultimate price for your failure!"  Suddenly, dark red beams of energy strike you, killing you where you stand!
"Well answered" the disembodied voice declares. "You may pass safely".

You find runic carvings on these ancient columns, runes which you manage to decipher: "If left is first,  and the first bridge is the heart, the second is the will, the third is the soul, and the fourth is the mind, which is the key to domination?"
The lava blows out, engulfing you and burning you alive!!!
You are teleported right in the middle of a lava lake!!!

On this ancient column, you find runic markings which you can decipher: "If first is right, and the first door is the will, the second is the mind, the third is the soul, and the fourth is the heart, which will you loose to Might and Power?"

You come upon a huge portal of bronze and platinum depicting Graaz'z, God of Might, Power and Evil. Ancient runes are carved on its archway, which you manage to decipher: "The road to my temple will be the test of your worth as one deserving my favor".
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "The Great Wyrm".  Do you go in?
You bump accidentally in a burly warrior, making him spill his drink over himself and his comrades. "Ye dogs!" he exclaims, "Me's gonna make ye pay fer yer insult!"   What do you do?
Hit him.
Apologize.
Dodging your fist just in time, he draws his sword and, along with his fellow adventurers, engages your party in battle!

A bit flustered, the warrior accepts your sincere apology: "Very well" he mumbles, "Me guess this nasty business going on of late is getting on everyone's nerves". With final apologies, you walk away.
The patrol leader collects the fines: "Now, go back about yer activities, and none of ye better stirp up anymore trouble, or it's to jail ye'll go!".  The patrol then leaves.
You pay the fine. "And remember" adds the magistrate, "one more offense, and off to jail you go!"  You are then escorted out.
You are then stripped of all you equipment and gear, then thrown into a small cell.
A bit of food is thrown to you by a jailor.
The ceiling door of your cell is opened: "Allright! Ye've done yer time!" intones the jailor. You are given back your equipment and set free.
"You again?!?" Intones the magistrate, upon seeing you. "Very well, then: I sentence you to a week in jail!"

Scyrella turns to you: "Being in this part of Artemisia Forest reminds me of a folktale I heard when I was a child. This tale speaks of a party of amazons who found a secret door in the mountains around here, which lead them into a maze of tunnels ...
under the mountains.  It is said that these tunnels themselves are rumored to lead somehow to an ancient temple of evil".
Monsters are summoned!
More pirates join the fray!
More cultists rush to the defense of their Holy Master!
More assassins join the battle!
The amazons who supported the Queen take flight upon her death!
Some ogres take flight upon the death of their chief!
More troglodytes join the battle!
Skeletal warriors are summoned!

"Those high and mighty knights of the Flame are sure found wanting when it's time to act instead of boast!" he adds. "What of king Vallar?" asks a third. A fourth one answers: "I hear he just doesn't know what to make of all this; especially since ...
he keeps sending envoys and troopers to Tanirith, but they never come back". The first one sniffs at that: "Probably taken down by them amazons!"  At that, you walk away.

An old druid is sipping his wine, obviously distraught. "Greetings, young ones" he chimes, managing a strained smile. "I used to be a great druid, but now, I can't even gather the mistletoe I need to weave my spells". He sighs.

"The worst is, I found this huge oak tree on the eastern-most island from here, and it is full of good mistletoe. With that, I could still be of use to the folks of Lantharond, at least for a good while". He shakes his head, taking another sip of wine.

"You would?" the old druid exclaims, quite relieved. "Well, here is my druidic scythe: go to this oak and bring me the mistletoe. I promise you that I will reveal you the location of some secret doors in the area!" After taking his scythe, you go.
The old druid is nowhere to be found.

You find the old druid, eating a hearty meal. "You have it?" he asks. Smiling, you hand him back the scythe and the bag of mistletoe. "Thank you, young ones! Now, let me tell you my secret: I know of two secret doors which lead to a complex network ...

of tunnel underneath the mountains west of here. I managed to establish their exact coordinates: one is at X17:Y68 in the Artemisia Forest of the amazons, and the other one is at X3:Y68 in a small valley, where a river enters the underground".
"Here's a few maps that'll help" he adds, finally. With final goodbyes, you leave the old druid to his meal, and his mistletoe.
This is a huge oak tree. You notice that it is anormally filled with mistletoe.
Certain that this is the tree the old druid spoke about, you put his hand scythe to good use and collect enough mistletoe to fill a good-sized bag.

A man whispers in your ear, being careful at not being heard or seen by other patrons: "I have something of great importance to tell you about the Overlords, but not here. Meet me in the brewery right next to this place".  At that, the man walks away.
Just as you are about to enter the brewery, you are attacked!
After the battle, you recognize among the fallen attackers the man who had lured you here.
Some of the patrons nod at you politely while conversing.
A sign above the door of this building reads: "Harbor Master -Lantharond Port".  Do you enter?

You walk to a series of kiosks marked "Boat Fares" and a destination. You stop at the one for Tanirirht; there, a lady smiles at you: "Fare to Tanirirth? Our apologies, but all trips to this city are on hold until diplomatic relations are restored".
You walk to the office with the sign "Boat Rentals"; on the door, another sign reads: "Rentals unavailable until resolution of the Lantharond-Tanirith freeze in diplomatic relations".

Guards nod at you: "Ye were expected", one of them tells you. "Go on to the castle, our King is waiting", he adds rather testily, as if offended by the fact that his king has to wait for people such as you.

Guards nod at you: "Ye were expected" snarls one, while scowling at Scyrella. Obviously, he and his comrades have difficulty controlling their tempers in regards to amazons. In response, Scyrella looks upon the guards with haughtiness and indifference.

Not wishing for a strained situation to turn into a bad one, you swiftly cross the gates while discretely ushing a reluctant Scyrella ahead of you.  All the while,  she taunts the guards with a defiant smirk, as they keep glaring at her with anger.

Guards stop you: "This amazon is not welcome here!" snarls one of them, while his comrades keep their spears pointed at Scyrella. "As are you", the scowling guard adds, "since you're stinking friends of amazons!".  You are promptly escorted out.

Guards stop you:"Amazons are not welcome here!" snarls one of the guards, while his comrades point their spears at Scyrella. You promptly show them the letter you found in the riders' compound, and explain that you are to see King Dragonheart about that.

After a moment of thought, the guard nods reluctantly: "Aye. I now remember we were told about you and to let you pass freely; but we weren't told about any amazon". Still scowling and glaring at Scyrella, the guards finally let you pass.
King Dragonheart's Royal Mage nods at you politely.
King Dragonheart's General nods at you politely.
The Queen of Lantharond nods to you politely.
King Vallar Dragonheart is busy conferencing with his advisors. Deciding it would be best not to disturb him for no reason, you leave.

King Vallar Dragonheart nods to you solemnly: "Greetings, noble adventurers. I understand from one of my trooper captains that you may have uncovered some ruffiants who are attempting to pass themselves as troopers, in order to forment trouble?"

Nodding, you then explain to king Dragonheart what you have done and found so far, including the Overlords and their apparent plans. "I am impressed by what you have accomplished" replies the king. "However, I need tangible proof of what you are ...

advancing, especially concerning those so-called trooper impostors. If you can find such a proof, do bring it to me: then, I shall reconsider these matters very carefully". Bowing formally after being dismissed by king Dragonheart, you leave.

Bowing politely, you explain all you have uncovered so far, especially concerning the Overlords. To support your claims, you hand over the letter you found in the riders' compound. As king Dragonheart reads it, you see him gawk in surprise and confusion.

As he finishes reading the document, the king turns to his royal mage: "Kaylor!" the king asks, sternly, "How is it that your magics have never told you anything of this? Surely, you should have easily managed to uncover such deception, which has ...

greatly endangered our people and tarnished our reputation in the area!" You see Kaylor slowly backing away, a sneer of pure malice etched on his face: "You are a fool, Dragonheart! The Overlords made me an offer I could not refuse; I was to slowly ...

enslave your mind and that of the queen's, but because of these foolish meddlers, I must now act swiftly: I will thus get rid of these adventurers and impose my will upon the crown!"  Summonning psi-warriors to his aid, Kaylor launches an attack on you!

King Vallar Dragomheart nods to you solemnly:  "Greetings, noble adventurers. I've been forewarned that you have things of upmost importance to convey to me?"  You then proceed to tell him everything you have found out about the Overlords, including ...

their involvement in the current amazon-Lantharond war, which has resulted in the death of the amazon queen at your hands. You finally announce to king Dragonheart that the amazons wish to send peace envoys to him, in order to end this senseless war.

After a moment of thought, king Dragonheart turns to Scyrella Silverspear: "Then, must I assume that we are honored by the presence of the new amazon queen?" he asks respectfully, his eyes full of compassion. Scyrella bows formally in response.

"Nay, good king" she finally answers. "I have sworn to bring down these evil Overlords; until then, our elder has been appointed regent. As for what these brave adventurers have told you, I confirm everything of it, including my formal offer of peace ...

to you, so that we may end this war which was no one's doing but that of these same Overlords". The kings nods at that: "Well spoken, honorable amazon Princess. We will welcome peace; but to convince my people, I would need proof of this conspiracy".
Bowing to king Dragonheart, you leave to find the proof of the ongoing conspiracy you have uncovered.
You immediately hand to the king the letter you found in the riders' compound. As he reads it, you see him gawk in surprise and confusion.

After the battle, king Dragonheart walk over the body of his royal mage: "Aye" he mumbles, "I was a fool not to see you for the treacherous leech that you were". He then turns to the assembly of his court: "Let it be known that Lantharond is no more ...

at war with the amazons! We will warmly receive their peace envoys. We will also send special envoys to Tanirith to show this damning document to the Lord Paladine, so that our alliance may be restored once and for all!"  At that, loud cheers erupt.

King Vallar Dragonheart nods formally: "Greetings, noble adventurers; and greetings to you as well, amazon Princess. I must admit that I am surprised by your presence here, considering the sad circumstances of war between our peoples".

You then proceed to explain all you have found so far concerning the Overlords; Scyrella Silverspear adds details of her own about trooper impostors attacking the amazons. The king nods thoughtfully: "What you tell me is grave indeed", he muses.

He then continues: "However, I think solid proof is required not only to convince my people of this conspiracy, but to convince the amazon queen and her people as well. Find this proof, then first show it to the amazon queen; then, bring it to me".

After the battle, the king walks over to the body of his royal mage: "Aye" he snarls, "I was a fool indeed, for not seeing the treacherous leech you were". He then turns to you: "Go, and show your document to the amazon queen, then bring it back to me".
King Vallar Dragonheart nods formally: "Greetings, good adventurers. It is my understanding that you may have things of great importance to bring to my attention?"

You interrupt his reading by pointing out that the amazon queen -which was under the influence of the Overlords- has been killed by your hands, and that the amazons wish to re-establish peace between them and Lantharond.

The king pauses in his reading: "And what say you, honorable amazon Princess?" he asks to Scyrella Silverspear, which much formality and decorum befitting her lineage. "I confirm all of it, king Dragonheart" she replies, with the same formality.
Bowing respectfully, you take your leave amidst the court's rumblings and mumblings, as everyone begins to recover from the shock of Kaylor's treachery.
King Vallar Dragonheart greets you warmly: "Welcome back, good adventurers! What news have you for me?"

As you attempt to flee, you are overwhelmed by Kaylor's psi-warriors. As they deliver the final blow, you see Kaylor laughing with glee as he weaves a mind-bending spell which will enslave the king and the queen of Lantharond, along with their court.

Amidst the cheers, king Dragonheart clasps your hands: "Your deeds deserve our gratitude as well as a generous reward! Please, accept these gifts from us!"  Smiling, the queen of Lantharond hands you a small chest.
"Our thanks once again" adds the queen. After a few hours of good-natured celebration, you take your leave from the court of Lantharond, with the king and queen's best wishes.
The queen smiles warmly at you, while she is busy confering with dignitaries. You decide not to bother her.

Smiling as you hand back the letter to the king, you announce to him that the amazons are ready to send special envoys to re-establish peace with Lantharond. You also tell him how the Overlords had influenced the queen, and that she had to be killed.

"Then let it be known" chimes the king with joy, "that we'll warmly receive the amazon envoys; also, we shall send envoys to Tanirith to show the Lord Paladine this document, so that he sees that we've honored our alliance all along!" Loud cheers erupt.
to you, so that we may end this senseless war which was no one's to begin with, but that of these same Overlords".
"Thank you. Go to the last pier, which is south-east of this building; there, your vessel and crew will be waiting. Have a good sail."

You walk to a series of kiosks with the sign "Boat Fares" and a destination. Stopping in front of the one for Tanirith, a lady behind the kiosk smiles: "Fare to Tanirith? That'll be 600 golds, please".  Who will pay?
"Thank you. Go to the last pier, which is south-east of this building; your vessel is anchored there. Departures are at every hour; have a good sail".
These are the Halls of Justice of Lantharond.
This is the musoleum of the Dragonheart Dynasty. You notice numerous guards watching over this huge crypt.
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Inn of the Singing Mermaid".  Do you go in?
A sign above the door of this place reads: "The Dragon's Lair".  Do you enter?
Numerous fishermen are busy unloading their catches in order to bring them to Lantharond's markets.

You notice old, runic markings on these crumbling columns which you manage to decipher: "To finally reach my temple and obtain my favors, you must now walk upon the icy, cold landscape that has become your soul. Come: I am waiting".
A sign above the door of this place reads: "Crescent Lake Store and Inn". Do you enter?

"WHO DARES TRESPASS HERE?" booms a loud voice, coming from within this cavern. Soon enough, a huge reptilian head peers out: "I HAVE BEEN SET TO GUARD THIS PLACE, SO BEGONE OR BE DEAD!"  Do you leave?
Without further words, the huge red dragon immediately attacks!
To your disapointment, the huge dragon's hoard is nowhere to be found. However, you notice that the cavern opens into an underground tunnel.
Without any further words, the huge dragon immediately attacks. At the same time, the female dragon that flew you here returns to help her sire!!!
As you attempt to flee for your lives, deadly fire balls rain on you!
You come upon a huge portal of bronze. Obviously ancient, it appears to have remained untouched by the passage of time, as well as by the heat and upheavals of the surrounding volcanic landscape.

You manage to decipher ancient runes etched in silver upon the portal: "Here lies the adventurer Kith Khanaan. Ye who read this must leave him to rest in peace".  The portal appears unlocked; do you open it?
The ancient statues within this antechamber animate and attack the intruders that you are!
This portal of iron is protected by a magical shield. Beside it, you notice a strange plate of metal with a depression shaped like a human left hand.  What do you do?
Powerful energies assault your volunteer!!!
The magical shield is dissipated!

Naryl Dragonstone steps in your path: "My friends, please allow me". Without any time for you to react, she puts her left hand onto the metal plate; immediately, the plate begins to glow, as the magical shield of the portal is dissipated!

Aghast, you stare at Naryl who is now visibly embarassed. She then shrugs with a mischievous grin: "I'm really sorry. I suppose this is the time to come clean with you. So please, ask me any question now, so that we may proceed ahead with a clean slate".

Mulling over all that Naryl has freely revealed to you, you shake your head somewhat in disbelief. "I am sorry for this gentle deception my friends, but I hope you understand why I had to act this way" adds Naryl. You nod, making her sigh with relief.

You suddenly feel Naryl's talisman pulsating. Taking it out, its glow begins to envelop each member of your party. "Choose one of your own to put the left hand onto the metal plate" Naryl's ethereal voice tells you in your minds.
You discover a secret door of iron disguised as a wall!

You are shocked to find the body of Naryl Dragonstone, who had left you a while ago because she disagreed with your methods and your callous ways.  She seems to have died quite recently, and from critical sword wounds at that. Next to her, you find ...

some sort of magical talisman, broken to pieces and now useless. You wonder who -or what- killed her, as well as why -and how- she came to this remote, secluded place. Unfortunately, her secrets died with her and now you will never know.
A magical rune is activated the moment you touch this ancient sarcophagus, summoning psi-warriors who attack you on sight!
Do you open the sarcophagus?
You find the mummified remains of what must be Kith Khanaan. Interestingly, the mummy is fully armored and armed. Do you take the mummy's items?
Out of respect for Kith Khanaan and gratitude for his gifts, you close back his sarcophagus.

"Wait!" Naryl intercedes. "We must find Kith Khanaan's talisman!". At your look of confusion, Naryl takes out a small talisman from underneath her shirt; it is comprised of an emerald-like stone set on a delicate neck-chain of silver. Naryl then speaks:

mental bond can also allow one to transfer one's essence (or spirit, or soul) into a talisman upon death, if one has the capacity and discipline to do so. In effect, you could view this as a form of immortality or essence preservation". She pauses.

"In my people, it is customary for elders to do just that upon their natural death, so that their wisdom may remain available to us. This was the case a well during the Empire of Lankharh, and the Mind Lords of then used these means to preserve their ...

essence, if not for the time when they may transfer it back to a receptive vessel. Thus, Kith must have transfered his essence, so that his wisdom may be brought back one day to Keryndor! So, you see: we must find his talisman!"
Naryl stops at this column. "I feel a powerful presence from within this column!" she exclaims. Do you search this column further?
Your search reveals a secret compartment. Opening it, you find a strange talisman glowing with an eerie white light.
"You should activate it now, or as soon as possible" whispers Naryl, obviously in awe of the object.

"Halt!" exclaims Runelore, to your complete surprise.  "I have allowed you to come this far and accomplish as much as you have, but now I must do my allies' bidding: I therefore cannot permit you to gain what is within Kith Khanaan's sarcophagus".
Summoning psi-warriors to his aid, Runelore launches his attack!
Looks like Runelore was an accomplice of the Overlords all along.  Feeling betrayed, yet still hadly believing it, you mend your wounds both physical and emotional.

As you flee for your lives, you are overwhelmed by the psi-warriors. "It is sad, actually", muses Runelore, his voice cold and detached, "since I had grown rather fond of you. But you know the Overlords, so ..." The warriors put you to death at that.

It would appear that Runelore was an accomplice of the Overlords all along. Feeling betrayed and still unbelieving, you look at Naryl: she did warn you about him. In response, she clasps your shoulder compassionately, silently comforting you.

The light from the talisman flows out, gradually taking the vague shape of a human being. "I AM KITH KHANAAN" his telepathic voice booms into your minds. "FOR MILLENNIA I HAVE WAITED TO BE FOUND BY ONE OF MY PEOPLE, SO THAT I MAY BE TAKEN BACK TO ...

KERYNDOR". Kneeling reverently, Naryl intercedes: "Great One" she whispers, "I, Naryl Thezzat, psi-knight of the ancient Order of Thesserack, has come here with the help of these non-psionics to deliver you. But urgent matters force me to petition ...

you for help. Please, look into my mind: I open it freely to you".  Naryl's head then jerks back as Kith Khanaan's essence peers into her thoughts; at the same time, you are feeling a strange pressure on your temples from the emanating telepathic ...

energies of the essence. "I UNDERSTAND AND ACKNOWLEDGE THE WISDOM OF YOUR COURSE OF ACTION, GOOD AND NOBLE PSI-KNIGHT. I WILL INDEED HELP" replies Kith Khanaan, finally. Suddenly, the essence englobes Naryl, as her body begins to convulse violently.

Before you can react, Naryl screams then falls flat on the floor. You notice that the essence has disapeared. Just as you approach her tentatively, she calmly rises up. As she turns to you, you are horrified to see a strange, white light emanating ...

from her eyes. "No need to worry" she whispers, although her voice sounds like a bizarre mixture between hers and that of Kith Khanaan. "Your noble friend petitioned me to use her mind and body as a temporary vessel, so that I may launch a surprise ...

mental assault on the renegades, or Overlords as you call them, when we finally meet face to face. I could not refuse her, especially that it pains me that to this day, there are still some of my people who place themselves above others such as you".

She sighs. "Keep my armors and weapons: they'll serve you better. But give me my talisman, for Naryl must possess it when I will leave her body". Awed, you give the talisman back. Naryl grins: "Now, let us teach the renegades the lesson they deserve!"

A bit confused by all this, you shake your head in resignation then move on. Naryl follows you silently, although she keeps testing out her arms and articulations, as Kith Khanaan's essence is obviously getting used to her body. You manage not to laugh.
Naryl Thezzat has joined your party. Check out the Allies Menu.

You come upon an ancient tower. From its crumbling outer walls, it must be thousands of years old. You see no doors about, except for an open archway which leads directly inside. Runic inscriptions above the archway read: "Welcome, Ye Who Seeks Power".
The cold winds blow into the tower through the archway, resulting in a keening howl which chills your souls. Do you walk inside?
Bitter-cold winds blow hard through the archway, almost knocking you down as you walk outside.
Between these two disks of obsidian marble, a pyramid-shaped altar stands. Although most likely millennia old, the artifact still crackles with dark energies.
The altar's dark energies lash out at you!
The winds blows hard and bitter-cold.

Your search reveals a loose tile on the floor, right underneath the inch or so of snow which has accumulated here. Clearing the snow, you pry the loose tile, revealing a small lever.  Do you pull on it?

With the winds blowing hard and cold on your backs, you enter a large, desolate hall. The place is filled with varying thickness of snow and ice. You can easily spot occasional fresh animal or yetis footprints; however, the place appears abandoned.
You stumble upon a group of psi-warriors busy at snooping around!
The ancient floor gives way under your feet!!!
The floor has given way here, leaving a dangerous gaping hole in its place.
Just as you walk into this room, you are assaulted by the restless spirits of dead priests of Graaz'z!

A floating, ectoplasmic entity glares at you with eyes glowing with anger and hate: "Trespassers!" its outerworldly voice booms. "As Highpriest of this temple, I command you to lay down all your valuables, or die for insulting Graaz'z!"  Do you comply?

Reluctantly, you divest yourselves of all your gear and throw it in front of the entity. Gloating, the entity grins evilly: "Fools! Graaz'z does not forgive the weak!"  With a word of power, you are smitten on the spot!
The entity smiles: "Good. You are brave enough. But are you strong enough to please Graaz'z?"  Summoning ghosts of his priests and shadow wraiths, the entity attacks!
You flee for your lives!!!
The restless spirits of dead priests of Graaz'z vent their hate upon you!

You find yourselves in what can only be the temple's basement. To your surprise, the place appears quite clean, with obvious signs of renovation on the walls and doors. Furthermore, the place is warm, indicating that it is being heated.
You disturb some psi-warriors who are on watch duty!
You disturb some psi-warriors who were resting here!
You enter a dining area; to your dismay, numerous psi-warriors are here enjoying a frugal meal!
You disturb a few sub-commanders resting here!

This lofty study is occupied by sub-commanders who are in a conversation with a woman whom you are begining to know very well: the lady Overlord. "Take care of these meddling mongrels!" she snarls to her sub-commanders, as she rushes out to another room.

In this lofty study, you find sub-commanders in a conversation with a woman whom you now know well: the Lady Overlord. However, you are shocked to find Runelore Magius at her side. "Deal with these mongrels!" the Overlord snarls at him and her ...

sub-commanders, before stomping out to another room. Runelore the grins evilly at you: "I thought you would somehow turn to our side. But now, I finally have to do what I had been charged of doing all along: rid my Overlord allies of you!"
Runelore and his accomplices launch their attack!
This is a kitchen. No one is about.
This place is empty, save for a strange statue nestled between the two columns on the north wall.
To your surprise, you find the ranger Strider in the middle of a clash with psi-warriors. Before you can even react, some of the psi-warriors advance your way!

After the battle, Strider walks up to you, grinning: "Thought you could keep me away, eh?" he quips. "Well, I had to investigate this place and rid the area of these Overlords. My thanks for helping me, friends; but now, you are stuck with me whether ...

you like it or not!" He winks, still grinning: "Hey! Be glad I did not bring Whitefang along! Anyways, I came to this specific room to somehow inactivate this statue, which is nestled between the columns on the north wall: I'm sure it's responsible ...

for those mysterious mental attacks which plague all non-psionics in here!" Gathering his gear, Strider joins your party: "Well?" he quips again, "Let's not stand here! Let us teach those Overlords the lesson they deserve!"
Shaking your head in resignation, you turn your attention to that statue Strider just mentioned.

Naryl steps in front of you: "My friends" she says, quite concerned, "We must find Kith Khanaan's tomb, where we should find useful items to help us against the Overlords. I feel their presence within this ancient tower, and they are too strong".
Convinced by her concerns, you decide it best to find what you need to tackle the Overlords face to face.

A sub-commander is occupied in front of a communication globe. Obviously, he is trying to make it work, but for some reason it refuses to do so. Upon your intrusion, his dogre bodyguards sound the alarm!

In this luxurious room, you see the Lady Overlord standing between two men garbed in exotic armors. You guess that they are the other two Overlords. Numerous psi-warriors and sub-commanders are here as well, along with some non-lankharhan allies.

"As you see" the lady Overlord sneers, "we were waiting for you. Allow me to make the introductions". She motions to the Overlord on her right: "This is Commander Zaar Enol, Sixth Speaker of the Inner Council". She then motions to the one on her left:

"This is Commander Berl Vezzir, Fifth Speaker of the Inner Council". She finally bows mockingly: "And I am General Arla Qui, Third Speaker of the Inner Council.  Our six other counterparts are away for now, back in our country of Keryndor, on Anarym".

"I have to admit" General Qui continues, "that you have been quite the thorns on our sides. Although you have disrupted our plans for the Sword Lands, you do not see that you cannot stop us. Indeed, our goals are vast and wide, reaching far and between.

So you see: despite what you think you may have achieved, you will not prevent the inevitable. We will prevail to establish a New Lankharh and bring back the Mind Lords, so that our people may finally rule over all the non-psionic mongrels, as is ...

our birthright. So, regardless of what happens here today, know that our conquest of the Sword Lands will be achieved, either through subversion or by force.  However, we are willing to accept you into our fold as loyal agents; you will have some ...
fair degree of freedom and power under our New Order, but you will still service us. So, my worthy adversaries, what say you?"  Do you accept to join the Overlords?

General Qui bows her head: "Welcome into the New Order". The three Overlords then burrow their psionic tendrils into your minds, putting you under their control and making you their new special agents to further their dark plans for the Sword Lands.
General Qui smirks at your answer: "I am almost glad that you have made this choice". With a mental command, the Overlords order their warriors and allies to attack!

As you attempt to flee, you are quickly overwhelmed. "That was a brave effort" muses General Qui, "but quite futile. However, you have been worthy adversaries and your skills would be quite useful to us yet".
You decide to search the place.

Naryl then steps forward, her body glowing with an eerie white light: "I am the essence of Kith Khanaan" she intones, "inhabiting within Naryl Thezzat, psi-knight of the Order of Thesserack". At that, the three Overlords step back, aghast.

"Great One!" exclaims General Qui, "We are honored and humbled by your presence! Look at what we are doing, what we are striving to achieve, and know that we are doing it all to bring back your glory and that of your sublime peers!"

Naryl shakes her head in disgust: "Haven't you learned anything? Why is it that there are still those like you who place themselves above others because they feel they are superior? Didn't you know that the Mind Lords were as sad, tragic mistake?"

Naryl sighs, lowering her voice: "That I was a mistake? Mind Lords can do nothing but eventually grow mad or evil, because our minds are not entirely adapted to hold the tremendous powers which reside within us! Even I had to resort to powerful magic ...

to help me maintain my sanity". She then glares directly at the three Overlords: "You are spoiled, arrogant children who have learned nothing of their parents' mistakes and tragedies.  You are so smug in your deluded superiority, that you do not see ...
your own failings. Well, no more! The lesson begins anew here and now!" Kith/Naryl suddenly unleashes a powerful psionic storm which assaults all in the room, save you.

Once the dust settles, Naryl nearly faints as the eerie glow leaves her. Catching her in time from falling to the floor, you see that she is back to her old self: "Kith had weaken after all this time in his talisman and he did not have time to adapt ...

to my body" she mumbles. "So he was forced out of me after his attack, and now he's back in his talisman". You then look about the room: with all the psi-warriors that are now lying unconscious or dead, you wonder what a Kith Khanaan at his best ...

would have done! "We must attack the Overlords now" Naryl exclaims, having recovered, "while they are still reeling from Kith's attack!" With a determined nod, you engage the Overlords in the final confrontation!

You go to Naryl who is lying unconscious. As you bandage her wounds, she comes back to: "Have we won?" she asks. You nod silently. Closing her eyes, she then activates her mind powers to heal herself, bathing her body in a soft glow of light.

On this large table, you find numerous letters of correspondence with those Overlords collaborators whom you have previously defeated.  You also see numerous maps of the Sword Lands. You are somewhat disturbed by some of them, which appear to be ...

strategic plans of military conquests. To that effect, you find a letter from the Overlord of Sharranth: "My dear allies; my army is now grown to sufficient strenght and is poised to march. Give the word when you will".  You get a bad feeling about this.
You find a few items of interest in this unlocked chest.

You see a communication globe nestled between the two columns of the south wall. From where you stand, you can see the face of someone within the globe, obviously impatient and attempting to "see" what is about in the room.

You have difficulty making out the details of this man, as the image within the globe is all blurry and distorted. Yet, it reminds you still of those unsettling dreams you had a while ago. "Who are you?" demands the man, before cutting himself short.

"So, my fellow council members have met their demise, then" he snarls, glaring at you. "Although their loss pains us, this turn of events does not matter. I salute you for your efforts, but it is too late: the second part of our plan is already underway
