and there is nothing you can do about it. The Sword Lands will have a few months of reprieve, so you better enjoy this time: for after that, War will come upon these lands". The image of this new Overlord then disapears as the globe disintegrates!

Congratulations for completing the main plot of Trouble in the Sword Lands! Feel free to wander around some more, since there are many smaller adventures and numerous other treasures to unearth within this scenario!

We hope you had fun with Trouble in the Sword Lands, and thank you again for registering. Don't miss "WAR IN THE SWORD LANDS", Part Two of the Sword Lands Trilogy, which will be coming out soon for your enjoyment!

"My friends" Naryl intercedes. "I'm afraid that this is where we must part. I have to go back to Keryndor, on Anarym, to inform my people of what was accomplished here, and also to bring back Kith Khanaan's talisman, so that we may benefit from his ...

wisdom". She pauses, smiling shyly: "I shall miss you all". After many warm embraces and final goodbyes,  Naryl Dragonstone/Thezzat takes out a small pebble. Holding it while muttering some incantations, she teleports away back to her far-away homeland.
As the last magical sparkle fades from the teleporting spell, you hear Naryl's final telepathic parting: "Safe journeys and safer returns, my friends".

Sighing, Strider turns to you: "I, too, must take my leave. I have to pick up Whitefang at the amazon village, then I'm off wandering these lands some more. It has been an honor to fight at your side". Grinning, Strider clasps your arms, then walks away.

"Who knows?" he adds, as he is still going on his way, "Maybe we'll run into each other again!" At that, he vanishes into thin air. Caught by surprise, you are left to wonder who was this Strider exactly ...

and your matchless bravery". With many warm embraces and final goodbyes, Scyrella slowly walks away. "Safe journeys and safer returns" she says in parting.

Scyrella sighs: "I too must leave, now that these Overlords have been vanquished. Now's the time for me to assume the responsibilities of the Queen of the amazons. I thank you for your help; I shall always value your friendship, your honor ...

"Who knows?" he adds as he catches up to Scyrella, "Maybe we'll run into each other again!" At that, he takes Scyrella's hand and both vanish into thin air. Caught by surprise, you are left to wonder who is this Strider exactly.

A suspicious-looking man bumps into you: "Psst!" he whispers, "I've an interesting map to sell. It indicates ta location of some hero's tomb. Kith Khanaan was his name. I'll sell ta map to ya for 500 golds".  Do you buy the map?
"Too bad" the man mumbles, before walking away.
"To get to ta volcanic region of ta Khanark Rockies, ya just need to go through ta ancient tunnel which is somewhere north-west of here". The man then walks away.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Cedar Cove".
This sign post points to the north for Sharranth and Mountainside, and to the south for Cedar Cove.
This sign points to the west for Mountainside, to the south-east for Sharranth, to the south for Cedar Cove, and to the north for Aranys.
This worn out sign reads: "Mountainside".
A band of minotaurs is camping here.  Upon seeing you, they attack!
This is Mountainside's general store. Do you go in?
The sign above the door of this place reads: "Rocky Cliffs Inn". Do you enter?
You see numerous minotaurs on watch along these battlements.  Wisely, you decide to walk away.
You disturb a nest of harpies!!!
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Cedar Cove's End of the Road".  Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this place reads: "The Waterfront".  Do you enter?
Fishermen are busy on the pier unloading their catches.
You spot a band of dogres rampaging through a farm field. Do you attempt to stop them?

After the clash, a farmer runs up to you:"Me thanks, good gents! These damn dogres lair in them caverns south-west of here and they've been bugging us a lot lately. Tell ye what: because of yer nice gesture, ye may use me boat anytime; it's at the pier".
Some of the dogres see you, and now the roving band turns its attention on you!
You disturb the cave of the chief of this dogre tribe. Of course, he is not happy about your intrusion: with his best warriors, he decides to show you the way out of his cave!

You are shocked to see so many soldiers walking around Sharranth. From time to time, you even spot ogres and minotaurs among the patrols. You can't help but notice as well that many of the civilians step aside and act demurely. Truly, this city is ...

rule by force. Suddenly, a patrol spot you: "Hey you!" yells a captain, "Adventurers aren't welcome in Sharranth, as decreed by our Lord Antraxus Storm!". You are immediately seized and thrown out of Sharranth.
A strange magical barrier surrounds this mansion. As you step back, you swear you saw someone -or something- looking at you through one of the upper windows.
"Ye're not allowed here!"
Not wishing to be in the way of such industrious activity, you walk away.
Well?
Hot lava prevents your passage!
"But you have already accomplished that!" replies Lord Pyre, somewhat perplexed by your strange choice.
Before you can react, you are drawn into the battle!
You walk past some of Lantharond's citizens; you notice that they are scowling at Scyrella and obviously resenting her presence in their city.

Uncertain, you produce the mysterious orb that you found on the body of "Nessar". Upon seeing it, the lich steps back in surprise. "You have found it!  Well done! Give the orb to me, and I shall give you what was promised".  Do you give the orb?
"Well," mumbles Sorceros, visibly ill-at-ease, "I guess we'll meet again, someday, eh?" Nodding shyly, as if trying to convince himself of what he just said, Sorceros slowly walks away.
You are surprised to find the steel doors locked tight. How will you get in?
You stumble upon a large gathering room, with numerous maurauders drinking and enjoying a meal. Upon your entrance, they all raise their weapons and rush you!
to you, so that we may end this war which was no one's doing but that of these same Overlords". The king nods at that: "Well spoken, honorable amazon Princess".
Pirates rise in arms to defend their isles!!!
Knights of the Flame loyal to the Lord Paladine are now standing watch over the castle of the defunct High Commander.
As you run for your lives, you are cut down to pieces!!!
You pass next to the altar once again; with nothing more to see here, you go on your way.
Some patrons nod to you politely.
Satisfied, you leave.
Do you want to leave this place?
A bitter cold draft chills you to the bones. You have no idea where this draft could have come from.

As you approach the battlements of the amazon village, you are startled to see the gates open, with Scyrella Silverspear walking up to you (along with a band of amazons ready for battle!). "You were told to leave our forest", Scyrella snarls angrily.

Then, other runes suddenly appear on the portal: "However, you are not even worthy to take the test yet. So begone, and come back only when you will have accomplished enough feats to deserve to take my test". Immediately, a magical field pushes you back.
The portal of Graaz'z remains silent.
Deciding it would be best for you to focus on the task at hand, you forego further wanderings and set yourselves to complete your task.
You are mercilessly cut down as you try to run for your lives.

Rummaging through the forest, you stumble upon ancient ruins buried by trees, branches and roots! Gripping your weapons firmly in hand, you hack away at the growth to clear the ruins as best as you can.
Once the ancient ruins exposed, you spot a crumbling flight of stairs going to some sort of basement. Do you take the stairs?
Do you enter the basement of those crumbling ruins?
You get back to the surface.

You enter a hall filled with old columns of marble. From the bas-reliefs of animals and people etched on the columns, you judge the art to be of elven origin. It would appear that you have stumbled upon ruins of an ancient elven settlement.
This old statue represents Miellakar, Goddess of the Forests. This place must have been a temple dedicated to her, a very long time ago.

"My friends" Strider intercedes as you are about to open that door. "I know for a fact that these ruins belong to the lost elven Forest-Kingdom of Aurystan, which was destroyed by Ptaraz some seven centuries past." He shakes his head.

"We should not violate these sacred ruins of the elves. Although elves haven't lived in the Sword Lands for centuries, except for some individuals, I am certain that this place is protected with powerful magic and spirits. Let us leave here in peace."

"Me friends" Braggan intercedes as you are about to open that door. "Me know fer a fact that them ruins belong to the lost elven Forest-Kingdom of Aurystan, which was destroyed by Ptaraz some seven centuries past." He shakes his head.

"Besides" he adds demurely, "I am a follower of Miellakar's ways, and thus I am loath to violate one of her sacred houses ... even if one is in ruins such as this one."
Your thorough search of this statue reveals a small button in the back of its base. Do you push the button?
The walls and ceiling collapse right behind you!
Looks like you are trapped ...

Disembodied spirits of elven maiden appear before you, eyeing you sternly: "Foolish mortals!" one of them intones. "You should not have violated Miellakar's temple, for now you should die in here, trapped as you are. But our Goddess is a kind one."
"Thus" the spirit goes on, "she is willing to take you back to the surface, provided you devest yourselves of all your gold, gems and jewels, as atonement!" Do you agree?
"Then so be it, foolish mortals!" At that, the elven spirits disappear.
You empty your money pouches and packsacks of all valuables, then leave them at your feet.
In a blinding flash of light, you are teleported back to the surface without so much as a by-your-leave.
This place looks like an old storage room. Of course, it is now filled with moldy, rusting and crumbling items that are worthless.
You enter what looks to be the main hall of a musoleum. From the broken columns and doors, it would seem that this place was ransacked ages ago.
This coffin is empty, the bones of its occupant having been thrown to the floor ages ago, in order to empty it of any valuables.
You hear a disembodied voice boom within the ancient hall: "Begone from here, or you shall face the wrath of Miellakar!"
You try to flee for your lives ... but to no avail. You are mercilessly cut down.
"You were warned" the booming diembodied voice intones, as the spirits of elven maiden appear out of nowhere to attack!
Your search of this empty coffin reveals a false bottom. Opening it, you find something that attracts your greedy eyes.
Panting and tired, you move on.
This part of the old temple is buried under rocks and dirt.
What do you want to do?
You escape to the surface!

"So we meet yet again, ice wyrm!" Strider chimes while smiling grimly. To your surprise, the sight of Strider enrages Icingbreath: "This time, little man" the dragon intones menacingly, "our encounter will be final!"

After all is said and done, you look inquisitively to Strider. Understanding your unspoken question, he shrugs dismissively: "Let's just say that old frost breath and I have met already ... twice" he muses cryptically.

As he sets to leave the cave, you grudgingly do the same. Looks like you won't get any more answers about this matter. But a question remains in your mind: what kind of man could survive alone an encounter with Icingbreath ... twice?
"An' I'll see ye tomorrow as well, me friends!" Braggan adds with a wink.
Perhaps this time you should join the dwarven king before setting out on your own?

The dwarven king and his generals are busy putting on armors and preparing their weapons. "There ye are!" he chimes jovialy. "Clodurin is smiling upon us today: a great victory we'll achieve, me tell ye!"
"Me friends! Ready fer battle?" Braggan shouts as he arrives to join all of you. You nod firmly in response as Braggan grins.
"We've received word from our kincousins!" the king exclaims. "Let us be quick about our fitting up!"

"Not the only feat they've achieved, me father!" Braggan chimes in, coming from behind you. "Me son!" the king exclaims, before rushing to embrace Braggan. "'Tis be a joyous day indeed!" he adds, before turning to you with tears rimming his eyes.

Smiling, you tell him that in your quest to solve the current Troubles, you've already found the shield and returned it to the Dwarven Halls. "Praise be Moradin and the Holy Forge!" Braggan exclaims, fighting back tears of joy welling up in his eyes.

"Well then, let me join yer group of brave heroes! Together, let us find out the root of them problems of the Sword Lands, and of me kin as well!" gathering quickly his gear, Braggan sets himself to follow you.
You also tell him of your current endeavors aimed at helping the Dwarven Halls in their war against the orcs and their allies.

You also tell him that all is well now with the Dwarven Halls, having helped the dwarves to rout their invaders. "Well then!" Braggan replies, somewhat frustrated, "At least me kin are safe fer now! Me better get on me way back to home, I s'pose."

After gathering his gear, he shakes your hand warmly once again: "Me thanks again fer saving me, brave gents: I'll never ferget ye! Time fer me to go home and help me people rebuild!" After final goodbyes, Braggan leaves for the Khanark Rockies.
It seems that this place is closed at this time of the day.

You refill your waterskins from this well.
You disturb the occupants of this cave!
You stumble into a harpy lair!
Feeling the pangs of hunger, you satiate yourself with your travel rations.
